# Muster documentation, version latest

The index of this text, with the rules for AI agents, is https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/llms.txt.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/index.md -->
# Muster

Muster is a self-hosted alert grouping and on-call service that sits after Alertmanager. It groups Alerts into Alert
Groups, the problems people act on; keeps one editable message per Alert Group in Mattermost, in Slack, in Telegram, in
any other messenger through a Bridge, or behind an outgoing webhook; and lets people acknowledge, resolve and snooze
Alert Groups.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  am["Alertmanager"] -- "Snapshots" --> integration
  subgraph muster["Muster"]
    integration["Integration"] --> routes["Routes"] --> groups["Alert Groups"]
  end
  subgraph destinations["Destinations"]
    mm["Mattermost"]
    sl["Slack"]
    tg["Telegram"]
    br["Bridge"]
    wh["Outgoing webhook"]
  end
  groups --> mm
  groups --> sl
  groups --> tg
  groups --> br
  groups --> wh
```

The Alertmanager of each cluster sends its notifications to an Integration of Muster. Routes pick Alerts by their
labels, group them into Alert Groups and decide the Destinations they are delivered to, and Muster keeps the message
of each Alert Group there up to date until the Alert Group is resolved.

![An Alert Group arrives in the Muster web UI, is acknowledged from its page and resolves](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/assets/demo.gif)

## Sections

- [Quick start](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/quick-start.md): run Muster with Docker Compose, sign in, connect Alertmanager and send a test alert,
  in about five minutes.
- [Install](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/helm.md): run Muster in production with [Helm](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/helm.md) and an external
  [PostgreSQL](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/database.md), and read the [requirements and tested versions](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/versions.md) and how
  to verify a release.
- [Integrations](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/alertmanager.md): connect the Alertmanager of a cluster, connect
  [Grafana Alerting](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/grafana.md) directly or through an Alertmanager, and watch the path from Alertmanager
  with a [Heartbeat](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/heartbeat.md).
- [Messengers](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/index.md): see what each Destination type can do, connect
  [Mattermost](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/mattermost.md), [Slack](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/slack.md) and [Telegram](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/telegram.md), reach any
  other messenger through a [Bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/bridge.md) (and [write one](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md)),
  [link your messenger accounts](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/account-links.md), and set a [proxy](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/proxies.md) for a client.
- [Outgoing webhooks](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/events.md): send the lifecycle events of Alert Groups in the
  [events mode](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/events.md), or keep a message in any chat in the
  [template mode](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/templates.md); [recipes](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/recipes.md) for a phone call, a status page,
  a second chat and an issue tracker.
- [Configure](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/messages-and-templates.md): change what [messages and templates](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/messages-and-templates.md)
  say, add links with Lookup tables and Link rules, set the [Organization](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/organization.md), and automate
  with [API tokens](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/api-tokens.md).
- [Sign-in](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/index.md): Roles and ways to sign in; [OpenID Connect with Keycloak](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/oidc-keycloak.md),
  [TOTP](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/totp.md), and [closed networks](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/closed-networks.md).
- [Concepts](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/alert-groups.md): what an [Alert Group](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/alert-groups.md) is, how
  [Routes and Group keys](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/routes-and-group-keys.md) group Alerts, the rules of
  [Snapshots](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/snapshot-semantics.md), [Loud and Quiet](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/loud-and-quiet.md) messages, the
  [statuses and commands](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/statuses-and-commands.md), and [Broken Destinations](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/broken-destinations.md).
- [Operations](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/backup-and-restore.md): [back up and restore](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/backup-and-restore.md),
  [upgrade](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/upgrades.md), [rotate the master keys](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/key-rotation.md), run
  [more than one replica](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/high-availability.md), [monitor Muster](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/monitoring.md), set an
  [outgoing heartbeat](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/outgoing-heartbeat.md), use the [command line](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/cli.md), and read the
  [Request log](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/request-log.md).
- [Runbooks](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/index.md): what each alert about Muster means and how to fix it.
- [Reference](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/index.md): metrics, log events, Internal alerts, environment variables, chart values, the API
  and the Bridge protocol.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/quick-start.md -->
# Quick start

Run Muster with Docker Compose on one machine, sign in, connect Alertmanager and send a test alert. You need Docker with
the Compose plugin, `curl` and `openssl`, and it takes about five minutes. The compose example runs one replica of
Muster beside its own PostgreSQL; for a production installation, [install with Helm](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/helm.md).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  am["Alertmanager or curl"] -- "Snapshots, port 8080" --> muster["Muster"]
  browser["Browser"] -- "web UI, port 8080" --> muster
  muster --> pg["PostgreSQL"]
```

## Start Muster

!!! note "Before the first release"
    Until Muster's first release, the tag in the download command below does not exist yet. Download from `master`
    instead: replace the tag in the URL, the part that starts with `v`, with `master`. Then, after you write `.env`,
    append the development image to it with `echo MUSTER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/muster-io/muster:edge >> .env`: `edge` is the
    image built from the newest commit on `master`.

Download the compose example into a new directory:

<!-- quickstart -->
```sh
mkdir muster && cd muster
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muster-io/muster/v0.0.0/deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml # x-release-please-version
```

Write its settings into `.env` next to it, with a generated master key and generated passwords:

<!-- quickstart -->
```sh
cat >.env <<EOF
MUSTER_SECRET_KEYS=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:8080
MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.org
MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
EOF
chmod 600 .env
```

- `MUSTER_SECRET_KEYS` is the **master key**. It encrypts the secrets Muster keeps in the database, such as the tokens
  of messenger bots, and Muster refuses to start on a database without the key that wrote it. Keep a copy of the key,
  **apart from the database backups**: see [Backup and restore](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/backup-and-restore.md).
- `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL` is the address people open, and links in messages point to it.
- `MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` create the first Admin at the first start. Use
  your own email if you like; it is also the login. Once an Admin exists, Muster ignores both.

Start Muster:

<!-- quickstart -->
```sh
docker compose up -d --wait
```

Muster creates its schema at the first start. One port, `8080`, serves the web UI, the API and ingestion.

## Sign in

Open `http://localhost:8080` and sign in with the login `admin@example.org` and the password from `.env`:

```sh
grep MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD .env
```

Muster runs on a machine without HTTPS, such as a VM? Browsers keep the session only over HTTPS or on `localhost`, and the
shortest way in is an SSH tunnel. On your own machine run `ssh -L 8080:localhost:8080 <vm>`, keep it open and browse to
`http://localhost:8080`, with `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:8080` as above. See
[Sign-in needs HTTPS or localhost](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/index.md#sign-in-needs-https-or-localhost).

Everything in the web UI and the API works only after sign-in: people sign in with a password or through
[OpenID Connect](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/oidc-keycloak.md), and automation with tokens. Each User has a Role — Admin, Responder or
Viewer — that decides what they see and change. Add the people of your team as Users under **Access**; each of them
links their own messenger accounts in their profile, as [Link your messenger accounts](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/account-links.md)
describes.

## Create an Integration

An **Integration** is the way one Alertmanager cluster sends to Muster.

1. Open **Integrations** and select **Create integration**.
2. Name it after your Alertmanager cluster, such as `prod-eu`, and select **Create**.
3. On the Integration's page, under **Tokens**, select **Create token**, then **Create**.
4. The dialog shows the **Token** and the **Alertmanager configuration** once. Copy both before you select **Done**:
   only a hash of the token is kept.

The Alertmanager configuration is a receiver that sends to Muster with the token, and a child route for it to place
first under the top-level route:

```yaml
receivers:
  - name: muster-prod-eu
    webhook_configs:
      - url: http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ingest
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 0
        http_config:
          authorization:
            type: Bearer
            credentials: mstr_int_…
route:
  routes:
    - receiver: muster-prod-eu
      continue: true
      repeat_interval: 10m
    # ... your existing child routes
```

Its URL comes from `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL`, because the compose example serves ingestion on the same address. Keep
`MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:8080` for your browser on this machine. When your Alertmanager runs on another
machine, replace `localhost` in the receiver's `url` with an address of this machine that Alertmanager reaches.
Browsers keep Muster's session only over HTTPS or on `localhost`: to open Muster from other machines, put an HTTPS
reverse proxy in front of port 8080, set `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL` in `.env` to its `https://` address and run
`docker compose up -d --wait` again. [Connect Alertmanager](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/alertmanager.md) explains every line of the
configuration, the catch-all child route to keep last, and the start delay.

## Send a test alert

You do not need Alertmanager for a first try: send what it would send. Put the token you copied into `TOKEN`, then post
a Snapshot with one firing alert:

```sh
TOKEN=mstr_int_...
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ingest \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @- <<EOF
{
  "version": "4",
  "groupKey": "{}:{alertname=\"QuickStartTest\"}",
  "status": "firing",
  "receiver": "muster-prod-eu",
  "groupLabels": {"alertname": "QuickStartTest"},
  "commonLabels": {"alertname": "QuickStartTest", "severity": "warning"},
  "commonAnnotations": {"summary": "A test alert from Quick start"},
  "externalURL": "http://localhost:9093",
  "alerts": [
    {
      "status": "firing",
      "labels": {"alertname": "QuickStartTest", "severity": "warning"},
      "annotations": {"summary": "A test alert from Quick start"},
      "startsAt": "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)",
      "endsAt": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
EOF
```

Muster answers `202`. Open **Alert Groups**: the Alert Group `QuickStartTest` is there, firing, and its page shows the
alert, its labels and its Timeline. It reached no messenger, because the alert went to the **Default route**, the Route
that takes every Alert no other Route takes, and the Default route has no Destination yet.

To resolve it, send the same request with both `"status": "firing"` changed to `"status": "resolved"`.

## Next steps

- **Set the time zone.** The Organization's time zone is UTC until you change it, so times in messages are UTC. Set it
  under **Organization → General**: see [Organization settings](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/organization.md#general).
- **Connect a messenger.** Connect [Mattermost](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/mattermost.md), [Slack](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/slack.md) or
  [Telegram](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/telegram.md), add a Destination for a channel, and add the Destination to the Default route or
  to a Route of its own; see [Routes and Group keys](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/routes-and-group-keys.md). Mattermost sends button presses
  to `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL` here, so the Mattermost server must reach that address: unless it reaches Muster at
  `http://localhost:8080`, put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of port 8080 and set `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL` to its
  `https://` address first. Slack in Socket Mode needs no address of Muster that Slack can reach.
- **Use any other messenger through a Bridge.** A [Bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/bridge.md) is a small service that connects
  Muster to a messenger it does not support natively. [Write a bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md) with the library
  for Go, [muster-bridge-go](https://github.com/muster-io/muster-bridge-go), or for Python,
  [muster-bridge-python](https://github.com/muster-io/muster-bridge-python), or try the
  [example bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#the-example-bridge) from
  [`examples/chat`](https://github.com/muster-io/muster-bridge-go/tree/master/examples/chat) of the Go library: a
  small chat with a web page, to see Muster's messages without a real messenger. It runs
  [next to this Quick start](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#the-example-bridge) as one more service of the compose project.
- **Change what messages say**, and add links to your dashboards and runbooks, as
  [Messages and templates](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/messages-and-templates.md) describes. [API tokens and
  automation](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/api-tokens.md) is for scripts and Terraform.
- **Connect your Alertmanager** as [Connect Alertmanager](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/alertmanager.md) describes, and watch the path
  from it with a [Heartbeat](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/heartbeat.md).
- **Learn how Muster groups alerts** in [Concepts](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/alert-groups.md).
- **Run it in production**: [install with Helm](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/helm.md), and read
  [Operations](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/backup-and-restore.md) for backups, upgrades and monitoring.

`docker compose down` stops Muster and keeps its data; `docker compose down -v` deletes the database too.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/helm.md -->
# Install with Helm

The Helm chart runs Muster on Kubernetes 1.30 or newer. It deploys Muster and its Services, and optionally an Ingress or
Gateway API routes, a PodDisruptionBudget, a ServiceMonitor, a NetworkPolicy, alert rules and a dashboard. It does not
include PostgreSQL: Muster takes an [external database](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/database.md). For a first try on one machine, use the
[Quick start](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/quick-start.md) with Docker Compose instead.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  browser["Browser"] -- "muster.example.org" --> app["app Service, 8080"]
  am["Alertmanager"] -- "ingest.example.org" --> ingest["ingest Service, 8081"]
  app --> pod["Muster pods"]
  ingest --> pod
  pod --> pg["PostgreSQL"]
  prom["Prometheus"] -- "/metrics" --> internal["internal Service, 8082"]
  internal --> pod
```

## Get the chart

Each release publishes the chart as an OCI artifact in the registry of the image:

```sh
helm install muster oci://ghcr.io/muster-io/charts/muster --version <version> \
  --namespace muster --create-namespace -f values.yaml
```

!!! note "Before the first release"
    Nothing is released yet, so the registry holds no chart. Install it from a clone of the repository instead, with the
    development image of `master`:

    ```sh
    git clone https://github.com/muster-io/muster && cd muster
    helm install muster deploy/helm/muster --namespace muster --create-namespace \
      -f values.yaml --set image.tag=edge
    ```

    The chart in the repository has the version `0.0.0`, and its `image.tag` defaults to `appVersion`, which names no
    existing image. A release sets the chart's version to its tag without the `v`, such as `1.2.3`, and `appVersion` to
    the tag itself, such as `v1.2.3`.

## Create the Secret

The chart never generates the master keys. Create a Secret yourself and name it in `existingSecret`; rendering fails
without it. The Secret holds, under the key names that the values `masterKeysKey`, `database.passwordKey` and
`bootstrapAdmin.passwordKey` name:

`secret-keys`
:   the default of `masterKeysKey`

    Holds the master key of the Keyring, as `openssl rand -base64 32` prints it.

`database-password`
:   the default of `database.passwordKey`

    Holds the password of the database user, unless `database.existingSecret` names another Secret for it.

`bootstrap-password`
:   no default; set `bootstrapAdmin.passwordKey`

    Holds the password of the first Admin.

```sh
kubectl create namespace muster
kubectl -n muster create secret generic muster \
  --from-literal=secret-keys="$(openssl rand -base64 32)" \
  --from-literal=database-password='<the database password>' \
  --from-literal=bootstrap-password="$(openssl rand -hex 16)"
```

The pods mount the Secret as files and read the values through `MUSTER_SECRET_KEYS_FILE`,
`MUSTER_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE` and `MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE`, so no secret appears in the pod's
environment, except the whole database URL when you name its key in `database.urlKey`.

When another operator keeps the database credentials in a Secret of its own, name that Secret in
`database.existingSecret` instead of copying the password: `database.passwordKey` and `database.urlKey` then name keys
of that Secret, and the master keys and the password of the first Admin stay in `existingSecret`. For the Secret
`muster-db-app` that CloudNativePG generates:

```yaml
existingSecret: muster
database:
  existingSecret: muster-db-app
  urlKey: uri
```

[The database](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/database.md#cloudnativepg) shows the form with `sslmode`.

!!! warning "Keep a copy of the master key"
    Muster refuses to start on a database without the key that wrote it, and a restored database is useless without it.
    Keep a copy **apart from the database backups**: see [Backup and restore](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/backup-and-restore.md).

A tool that manages Secrets, such as External Secrets or Sealed Secrets, works the same way: it only has to produce a
Secret of that name with those keys.

## Values

A short `values.yaml` for an installation with an Ingress and an external database:

```yaml
existingSecret: muster

database:
  host: muster-db-rw.muster.svc
  name: muster
  user: muster
  sslmode: require

publicURL: https://muster.example.org
ingestURL: https://ingest.example.org

bootstrapAdmin:
  email: admin@example.org
  passwordKey: bootstrap-password

replicas: 2
podDisruptionBudget:
  enabled: true

ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: nginx
  app:
    hosts:
      - host: muster.example.org
    tls:
      - secretName: muster-tls
        hosts: [muster.example.org]
  ingest:
    hosts:
      - host: ingest.example.org
    tls:
      - secretName: muster-ingest-tls
        hosts: [ingest.example.org]
```

`publicURL` is required: the chart renders without it, but Muster stops at start. The notes that `helm install` prints
warn about a missing `publicURL` or a missing database. `bootstrapAdmin` creates the first Admin once; after the first
Admin exists, Muster ignores it. Everything else about the installation — Connections, Integrations, Routes, people —
is configuration in the database and changes in the web UI and the API, never in the chart.

The full list of values, with types and defaults, is the [chart values reference](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/chart-values.md). The
chart rejects a value it does not know. Environment variables that have no value of their own go into `extraEnv`; the
[environment reference](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/environment.md) lists them.

The chart sets `MUSTER_MIGRATE_ON_START` off and runs `muster migrate` in an init container instead, under a database
lock, so that the pods of a rollout do not migrate at once. The pods run as a non-root user with a read-only root file
system. The readiness probe checks only the database, and a startup probe gives a slow start up to five minutes.

## The two public addresses

Muster has two addresses that other systems use, and the chart takes both as values:

`publicURL`
:   environment variable: `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL`

    Used for people: the web UI, links in messages, the OIDC redirect.

`ingestURL`
:   environment variable: `MUSTER_INGEST_URL`

    Used for machines: Alertmanager, Heartbeats, Mattermost button callbacks, the Telegram webhook, and the button
    presses of Slack Connections in the HTTP event mode.

`ingestURL` defaults to `publicURL`. Muster never derives either from an Ingress or a route: set them to the addresses
that people and machines really use, or the links it builds will be wrong.

Muster serves ingestion on its own listener (`8081`) apart from the web UI and the API (`8080`), and the chart gives
each a Service. A separate address for ingestion lets you expose the two differently: the web UI only inside the company
network, and ingestion to Alertmanagers in other networks, or the other way round, with different TLS settings, rate
limits and firewall rules on each. It also keeps a burst of Snapshots away from the web UI's address. When you have no
such need, give both the same host name and send the paths `/api/v1/ingest`, `/api/v1/heartbeat` and
`/api/v1/callbacks/` (with everything below them) to the ingest Service and everything else to the app Service, as
[Connect Alertmanager](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/alertmanager.md#behind-a-reverse-proxy) describes.

The third listener, `8082`, serves `/health/live`, `/health/ready` and `/metrics`. It has a Service and no Ingress or
route; do not expose it outside the cluster.

## Ingress

`ingress.enabled` creates two Ingress objects, one for the app Service and one for the ingest Service. List the hosts of
each under `ingress.app.hosts` and `ingress.ingest.hosts`, with their `tls` blocks, and set `ingress.className` and
`ingress.annotations` for your controller. A host takes an optional `path` (`/` by default) and `pathType` (`Prefix`).
Annotations apply to both Ingress objects. Set the body size limit of your controller to at least 16 MB for the ingest
host, because Muster accepts Snapshots up to that size.

## Gateway API

`httpRoute.enabled` creates two `HTTPRoute` objects (`gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1`) instead of Ingress objects, one
for each Service. Name the Gateway in `httpRoute.parentRefs` and the host names in `httpRoute.app.hostnames` and
`httpRoute.ingest.hostnames`:

```yaml
httpRoute:
  enabled: true
  parentRefs:
    - name: public
      namespace: gateway
  app:
    hostnames: [muster.example.org]
  ingest:
    hostnames: [ingest.example.org]
```

The chart does not create the Gateway and its certificates. The Gateway API resources must be installed in the cluster
and the Gateway must accept routes from the namespace of Muster. Use `ingress` or `httpRoute`, not both.

## Replicas and the PodDisruptionBudget

`replicas` is 1 by default. All replicas are active: each serves the web UI and ingestion and works on the queues, and a
Leader among them does the few jobs that must run only once. With more than one replica:

- Set `podDisruptionBudget.enabled` to `true`. The budget allows one unavailable pod (`maxUnavailable`), so a node drain
  never takes all replicas down at once.
- Spread the pods over nodes with `topologySpreadConstraints` or `affinity`.
- If the main database connection goes through PgBouncer in transaction mode, set `database.sessionHost` (and
  `sessionPort`) to a session-capable endpoint. See [the database](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/database.md#pgbouncer).
- Keep the clocks of all nodes in sync with NTP; Muster compares them with the database's clock and logs a warning on a
  skew, and the chart rule `MusterClockSkew` raises an alert.

Rolling updates run between adjacent minor versions only, and the init container of each new pod applies the database
migrations before the pod starts. Take a backup first.

## Watch Muster

`serviceMonitor.enabled` makes the Prometheus Operator scrape `/metrics` of the internal Service.
`alerting.prometheusRule.enabled` or `alerting.vmRule.enabled` renders the alert rules, and `dashboard.configMap.enabled`
or `dashboard.grafanaDashboard.enabled` the Grafana dashboard. The rules and the dashboard are reference material; the
[Runbooks](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/index.md) explain each alert, and the [metrics reference](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/metrics.md)
lists what Muster exports.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/database.md -->
# The database

Muster keeps everything in PostgreSQL 14 or newer, and nothing else stateful: no Redis and no queue. At start Muster
refuses an older PostgreSQL and stops with an error that names the cause. It needs one extension, `pg_trgm`, which ships
with PostgreSQL and which the database owner can create (a trusted extension since PostgreSQL 13); the first migration
creates it. Neither the Helm chart nor the compose example backs up the database: see
[Backup and restore](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/backup-and-restore.md), and keep the master key apart from the backups.

## As a URL or as fields

Give the database to Muster in one of two forms. The settings are in the
[environment reference](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/environment.md).

A URL
:   `MUSTER_DATABASE_URL`, such as `postgres://muster:<password>@db.example.org:5432/muster?sslmode=require`

Fields
:   `MUSTER_DATABASE_HOST`, `MUSTER_DATABASE_PORT` (default `5432`), `MUSTER_DATABASE_NAME`, `MUSTER_DATABASE_USER`,
    `MUSTER_DATABASE_PASSWORD` or `MUSTER_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE`, `MUSTER_DATABASE_SSLMODE` (default `prefer`)

When both forms are set, the URL wins and Muster logs a warning that names both. Muster ignores every `PG*` variable,
such as `PGHOST`, `PGSSLMODE`, `PGSSLROOTCERT`, `PGOPTIONS` and `PGPASSFILE`, and the password file `~/.pgpass`. Give
any other libpq setting as a parameter of the URL instead, such as `sslrootcert`, `options` or `target_session_attrs`.
Only libpq's default certificate files still apply when the URL names none: `~/.postgresql/root.crt`, and
`~/.postgresql/postgresql.crt` with `postgresql.key`; these are files, not variables, and the Muster image has none. Any
secret can come from a `*_FILE` variable.

Prefer the fields when the host, user and name are plain values and only the password is a secret: the Helm chart does
exactly that, with `database.host`, `database.port`, `database.name`, `database.user` and `database.sslmode` as values
and the password from a key of the Secret as `MUSTER_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE`. Use the URL when you need a setting that
has no field, such as `pool_max_conns` or `sslrootcert`; in the chart, `database.urlKey` names the key of the Secret that
holds the whole URL, and the field values are then ignored.

A replica's main pool holds `max(10, CPUs)` connections unless the URL sets `pool_max_conns`. On top of that, each
replica keeps about three session connections (see [PgBouncer](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/database.md#pgbouncer)). Size `max_connections` of PostgreSQL for all
replicas together.

Create the database and its user before the first start. The user owns the database, because Muster creates its tables,
indexes and partitions itself:

```sql
CREATE ROLE muster LOGIN PASSWORD '<password>';
CREATE DATABASE muster OWNER muster;
```

Muster applies its migrations at the first start: the compose example sets `MUSTER_MIGRATE_ON_START`, and the chart runs
`muster migrate` in an init container.

## CloudNativePG

[CloudNativePG](https://cloudnative-pg.io) runs PostgreSQL clusters on Kubernetes. A `Cluster` for Muster creates the
database and its owner:

```yaml
apiVersion: postgresql.cnpg.io/v1
kind: Cluster
metadata:
  name: muster-db
  namespace: muster
spec:
  instances: 3
  storage:
    size: 10Gi
  bootstrap:
    initdb:
      database: muster
      owner: muster
```

CloudNativePG serves the primary at the Service `muster-db-rw` (and the replicas read-only at `muster-db-ro`) and enables
TLS on its own. It generates the password and keeps it in the Secret `muster-db-app`, with the keys `username`,
`password`, `host`, `port`, `dbname` and `uri` among others. The chart reads the database from that Secret when you name
it in `database.existingSecret`; the Secret `muster` of [Install with Helm](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/helm.md#create-the-secret) then holds only
the master keys and the password of the first Admin:

```yaml
existingSecret: muster
database:
  existingSecret: muster-db-app
  urlKey: uri
```

The `uri` key holds a URL such as `postgresql://muster:<password>@muster-db-rw.muster:5432/muster`. It names no
`sslmode`, so Muster connects with its default, `prefer`, which uses the TLS of CloudNativePG but does not insist on
it. To require TLS, give the connection as fields and take only the password from the Secret, which also keeps the
password out of the pod's environment:

```yaml
existingSecret: muster
database:
  existingSecret: muster-db-app
  host: muster-db-rw.muster.svc
  name: muster
  user: muster
  sslmode: require
  passwordKey: password
```

When you give the `Cluster` a Secret of your own under `bootstrap.initdb.secret`, CloudNativePG generates no
`muster-db-app`, and your Secret holds no `uri`: use the fields form above, with your Secret in `database.existingSecret`
and `passwordKey: password`.

Add an `spec.backup` section to the `Cluster` (see the CloudNativePG documentation) and test a restore, together with the
master key, before you rely on it.

## Managed PostgreSQL

A managed PostgreSQL service works when it offers version 14 or newer and a role that owns an empty database. Check:

- **Version.** PostgreSQL 14 or newer. Muster is tested on 14 and 17.
- **Extensions.** Only `pg_trgm`; allow it where the service keeps an allow-list of extensions. Muster does not use
  `pg_partman`; it creates its partitions itself.
- **Session features.** Muster needs session advisory locks and `LISTEN/NOTIFY`. Plain endpoints of managed services
  provide them. A pooler endpoint that your provider adds in transaction mode does not: see [PgBouncer](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/database.md#pgbouncer).
- **Failover.** Name the endpoint that follows the primary, not an instance.
- **TLS.** Most services require it. Set `sslmode` as [below](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/database.md#tls).
- **Connections.** Check the connection limit of the plan against the pool sizes above.

Run `muster doctor` against the database after you set it up. It checks the version, the session features, the pooler
mode and whether each connection is encrypted.

## PgBouncer

Muster uses two kinds of database connections:

- The **main connection** carries every query. It may go through PgBouncer in transaction mode.
- The **session connection** carries what needs a real session: the advisory lock of the Leader, the `LISTEN`
  connection that wakes the workers and feeds live updates to the web UI, partition maintenance and the migrations. A
  transaction pooler would lose their session state between statements.

Without a separate setting, the session connection is the main connection. At start, Muster takes an advisory lock over
it and completes a `LISTEN/NOTIFY` round trip. Behind a transaction pooler this fails within five seconds, and Muster
stops with an error that names `MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_URL`.

So when the main connection goes through PgBouncer in transaction mode, give Muster a session connection that reaches
PostgreSQL directly or through a pooler in session mode:

`MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_URL`
:   A whole URL for the session connection.

`MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_HOST`
`MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_PORT`
:   Only the host and the port; the user, password, database and `sslmode` are those of the main connection.

In the chart, these are `database.sessionHost` and `database.sessionPort`. With CloudNativePG, the main connection can
use a `Pooler` object in transaction mode, whose Service takes the `Pooler`'s name, here `muster-db-pooler-rw`, and the
session connection the `-rw` Service of the `Cluster`:

```yaml
database:
  host: muster-db-pooler-rw.muster.svc
  sessionHost: muster-db-rw.muster.svc
  sessionPort: 5432
```

!!! note "PgBouncer 1.21 or newer"
    Muster's driver uses prepared statements on the main connection. In transaction mode, PgBouncer supports them from
    version **1.21**, and only when `max_prepared_statements` is above 0. An older PgBouncer, or a value of 0, makes
    queries fail with errors about missing prepared statements. Set `max_prepared_statements` to a few hundred, such as
    `200`. A pooler in session mode, or no pooler, needs no such setting.

PgBouncer is optional. Most installations connect straight to PostgreSQL, and then no session setting is needed.

## TLS

`MUSTER_DATABASE_SSLMODE` (or `sslmode` in the URL) takes the values of PostgreSQL's client library:

`disable`
:   encrypts: never · checks the server: nothing

`allow`
:   encrypts: only when the server insists · checks the server: nothing

`prefer` (default)
:   encrypts: when the server offers TLS, else falls back to plain text · checks the server: nothing

`require`
:   encrypts: always · checks the server: nothing: protects against listening in, not against an impostor

`verify-ca`
:   encrypts: always · checks the server: the certificate chain against a trusted CA

`verify-full`
:   encrypts: always · checks the server: the chain, and that the certificate names the host you connect to

`prefer` makes a fresh installation work, but it also connects without encryption to a server that has none. Muster tells
you: `muster doctor` reports each connection as encrypted or not, and a start with an unencrypted connection logs a
warning. For anything but a single machine, set `require` at least, and `verify-full` where you can: the certificate then
proves that the server is yours.

`verify-ca` and `verify-full` check against the file named by `sslrootcert` in `MUSTER_DATABASE_URL`, which must exist
in the container; without it, against `~/.postgresql/root.crt` when that file exists, and otherwise against the root
certificates of the system. The fields form has no such setting. With
`MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_HOST` and `MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_PORT`, the session connection takes the `sslmode` of the
main connection; a `MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_URL` carries its own, `prefer` when it names none.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/versions.md -->
# Requirements and tested versions

What Muster needs, which versions it was checked against, and how to verify that a release you download is the one the
project built. "Tested" means different things for different rows, so each row says which.

- **CI** means an automated job that runs on the project's pull requests or nightly, and fails the build.
- **Development stand** means a person ran the behaviour against a real server of that version and recorded what it did,
  but no job repeats it. These facts are the ground the messenger and Alertmanager features rest on; the fake servers
  that CI uses imitate them.

## Requirements

**PostgreSQL**
:   14 or newer, directly or or through a pooler whose session connection is session-capable. Nothing else
    stateful: no Redis, no queue. See [The database](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/database.md).

**Where Muster runs**
:   Binaries and container images for Linux; binaries also for macOS; both on amd64 and arm64. The container image is
    `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. The [Quick start](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/quick-start.md) needs Docker with the Compose plugin.

**Kubernetes**
:   1.30 or newer, for the [Helm chart](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/install/helm.md).

**A browser**
:   For the web UI, one that keeps a `Secure` cookie: over HTTPS, or on `localhost`. See
    [Sign-in needs HTTPS or localhost](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/index.md#sign-in-needs-https-or-localhost).

## Tested versions

PostgreSQL
:   14 and 17 in **CI**: `make test-integration` runs the integration tests on both, in containers, on every pull
    request. The compose example and the development database run PostgreSQL 17.

Kubernetes and Helm
:   Kubernetes 1.33.0 in **CI**: `make helm-check` lints the chart, renders it with the values files of the repository
    and validates the result strictly against the schemas of 1.33.0. Helm v4.3.0 does the rendering, and also packages
    the chart for a release. Nothing is run in a cluster by CI, and other versions from 1.30 are not checked.

Alertmanager
:   v0.34.1 on a **development stand**, with Prometheus v3.15.0 and vmalert v1.153.0: how it repeats, groups, restarts
    and truncates is measured there. Other versions of Alertmanager send the same webhook; if one behaves differently,
    the [Snapshot semantics](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/snapshot-semantics.md) page and the Heartbeat are how you notice.

Grafana
:   OSS 13.2.4 on a **development stand**, as one instance on SQLite and as a pair of replicas on PostgreSQL 17, through
    the webhook contact point of its built-in Alertmanager. See [Connect Grafana](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/grafana.md).

Mattermost
:   11.2.2, a test server on the **development stand**, through REST API v4 with a bot account. CI runs the same
    behaviour against a fake Mattermost server. See [Mattermost](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/mattermost.md).

Slack
:   Slack's cloud Web API and Socket Mode, on a **development stand**: a free workspace with a test app and a test
    channel. CI runs against a fake. See [Slack](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/slack.md).

Telegram
:   The cloud Bot API 10.3, on a **development stand**, with a test bot and a test channel. CI runs against a fake. See
    [Telegram](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/telegram.md).

The web UI
:   Its component tests and its end-to-end tests run in Chromium in **CI**. Other browsers are not tested.

## Image tags

The images are `ghcr.io/muster-io/muster` and the tags are:

- `vX.Y.Z`: a release. Use it, so that an upgrade is a decision you make.
- `latest`: the newest release that is not a prerelease. A prerelease tag, such as `v1.4.0-rc.1`, never moves it.
- `edge`: the newest commit on `master`, a development image.
- `sha-<7 hex digits>`: the development image of one commit.

## Verify a release

!!! note "Before the first release"
    No release exists yet, so there is nothing to verify, and the commands below have not been run against a real
    release. The development images, `edge` and `sha-…`, are **not signed** and carry no SBOM attestation: the workflow
    that builds them skips signing. Use these commands from the first release on, with its tag.

A release is built by the workflow `release.yml` of the repository, on a tag `vX.Y.Z`. It signs the container image
with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/), keyless, with the identity of that workflow run, so a valid signature
proves that the image was built by that workflow on that tag. Install cosign v3 or newer (the release signs with v3.1.3,
in the new signature format), then:

```sh
VERSION=vX.Y.Z
cosign verify ghcr.io/muster-io/muster:$VERSION \
  --certificate-identity "https://github.com/muster-io/muster/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/$VERSION" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
```

It prints the verified signature and exits `0`. To accept any release tag, replace `--certificate-identity` with
`--certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github\.com/muster-io/muster/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@refs/tags/v'`.
The signature covers the multi-architecture index and the image of each platform. To pin what you run, deploy the digest
you verified, `ghcr.io/muster-io/muster@sha256:…`, rather than the tag.

**The SBOM of the image** is an attestation that BuildKit attaches when the image is pushed, not a cosign attestation.
Read it with Docker:

```sh
docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/muster-io/muster:$VERSION --format '{{ json .SBOM }}'
```

It prints the software bill of materials, one per platform.

**The archives** are attached to the GitHub release: `muster_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz` for Linux and macOS on amd64
and arm64, `checksums.txt` with their SHA-256 sums, and one SPDX JSON software bill of materials per archive. Download
the archive and `checksums.txt` into one directory and check it:

```sh
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt
```

On macOS use `shasum -a 256 -c checksums.txt --ignore-missing`. `checksums.txt` is not signed: it finds a broken or
swapped download from the same release, not a swapped release. For that, verify the image.

The Helm chart is pushed with the release to `oci://ghcr.io/muster-io/charts` and is not signed by the release workflow.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/messages-and-templates.md -->
# Messages and templates

Muster shows every Alert Group as one **Root message** in each Destination, and edits it as the Alert Group changes.
Without any setup the message is complete: the status, the number and title, the environment and start time, the
labels, the summary, the Alerts, the links and the buttons. This page is for the Admin who wants to change what it
says: the template of a Route, whom a message mentions, and the links it carries.

## What you can change, and what you cannot

A Route has three templates, under **Routes → a Route → Message**. Each is **Built-in** or **Custom**.

**Root message**
:   The body of the message: the environment, the start time, the labels, the summary and the Alerts. The status
    colour, the heading, the links, the notices, the footer and the buttons always come from Muster, so no template can
    lose the buttons or the link to the Alert Group.

**Alert line**
:   The line of each Alert in the list of Alerts. It is also called the **Line template**.

**Ack timeout notice**
:   The reply Muster sends when nobody acknowledges an Alert Group in time.

**Language** of the same section sets the language of the built-in texts of the Route, English or Russian
(`route.language`, English by default). Times in messages are absolute and use the Organization's time zone, never
relative: see [Organization settings](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/organization.md#general).

Choosing **Custom** fills the editor with the source of the built-in template in the Route's language, so you start
from what people see today and edit it. Choosing **Built-in** again keeps your text until you leave the page.

Each editor has a **Preview** under it. Choose the **Sample** it renders against: a **Built-in example**, the **Recent
snapshots of this route**, or the Stored Snapshots of one Integration; and the **Markup of the preview**, Mattermost,
Slack or Telegram. When you save, Muster parses every template and runs it against the most recent Stored Snapshots of
the Route (up to 20, `template.dry_run_sample`, or the built-in example when there are none). A template that does not
parse, or that calls a function Muster does not have, is **not saved**: the editor marks the error at its line and
column.

The Outgoing webhook Destinations have templates of their own, written the same way: see
[template mode](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/templates.md).

## The template language

Templates are Go templates, the language of Alertmanager's own templates, and run in a sandbox:

- The functions are those of Alertmanager's templates under their own names (`toUpper`, `toLower`, `title`, `join`,
  `match`, `reReplaceAll`, `safeHtml`, `stringSlice`, `date`, `tz`, `humanizeDuration`, `toJson` and more), so an
  Alertmanager template usually carries over. On top of them come the string, list, map, conversion and regular
  expression (RE2) functions of the [sprout](https://github.com/go-sprout/sprout) library, `now` and `since` from
  Muster's clock, and two Muster functions: `lookup` (see [Links](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/messages-and-templates.md#links)) and `mention`.
- There is no function that reads the environment, files or the network; `env` does not exist. Muster has no list of
  functions in the web UI: sprout's documentation and Alertmanager's template reference are the function reference,
  and the editor names an unknown function when you save.
- Loops are capped, a template may run for 2 seconds, and the output is cut at about 50,000 characters
  (`template.output_cap`).

What the Root message template reads:

`.AlertGroup`
:   `Number`, `Title`, `Summary`, `Status`, `Route`, `SeverityLevel`, `Urgent`, `StartedAt`, `URL`, `ReopenCount`, `Owner`.

`.Alerts`, `.Status`, `.GroupLabels`, `.CommonLabels`, `.CommonAnnotations`, `.ExternalURL`
:   As in Alertmanager's templates. `.Alerts.Firing` and `.Alerts.Resolved` select by status.

The line template reads **one Alert** directly, as `.Labels`, `.Annotations`, `.Status`, `.StartsAt`, `.EndsAt`,
`.GeneratorURL` and `.Fingerprint`, and `.AlertGroup` as above.

Alert data is safe by construction. Label and annotation values arrive already escaped for the Destination's markup,
cut at 4 KB each (`message.value_cap`), and an `@` in them is neutralised with a zero-width space, so `@channel` in a
label notifies nobody. Links in messages are `http` or `https` only.

!!! tip "Two small examples"
    A line template that shows the pod and its summary:

    ```
    {{ .Labels.pod }}: {{ .Annotations.summary }}
    ```

    A Root message template that shows the summary and the pods that fire:

    ```
    {{ .AlertGroup.Summary }}
    {{ range .Alerts.Firing }}- {{ .Labels.pod }}
    {{ end }}
    ```

    Check both in the preview with a sample that has Alerts before you save.

If a template that was saved fails later, on data it did not expect, Muster does not drop the message. It renders the
**Fallback template** instead, which shows every label under Muster's heading, footer and buttons. The Route shows
**Template error** with the time and the error, the Timeline records that the fallback was used, and the Internal alert
`MusterTemplateError` fires until the template renders again; see its
[runbook](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterTemplateError.md). **Organization → System status** lists the template errors.

A long message is shortened to the limit of the messenger by cutting the list of Alerts first, then the label sections.
It always keeps the title, status, footer, buttons and the link. The list shows up to 10 lines of Alerts
(`message.alerts_listed`); above that it shows the distinct values of each label that differs, and "Full list in
Muster".

## Whom a message mentions

Each Destination has a **Mentions** section for six kinds of Loud event: nobody by default, or everyone in the chat,
chosen Muster users, or messenger groups, as far as the messenger offers them (`destination.mentions`). The
[Loud and Quiet](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/loud-and-quiet.md#mentions) page lists what each Destination type takes and why a user
needs an Account link to be mentioned.

In a template, `{{ mention "all" }}`, `{{ mention "channel" }}`, `{{ mention "here" }}`, `{{ mention "owner" }}` and
`{{ mention "group" "oncall" }}` write a trusted Mention that Muster renders for the messenger. A literal `@all` written
in a template is escaped and mentions nobody.

## Links

Links to other tools come from data, not from code in a message: Link rules read Lookup tables. They appear as one line
in the message and as the **Links** block on the Alert Group page.

A **Lookup table** is a table of values: a key and one value per named column. Open **Organization → Lookup tables →
Create table**, name it, add the columns and the rows. Limits: 50 columns and 10,000 rows, names and column names up to
200 characters, a description up to 2,000, a key or value up to 4,096 (`lookup_table.size_max`).

A **Link rule** turns an Alert Group, or each value of a label, into a link. Open **Organization → Link rules → Create
rule** and fill in:

**Name**
:   Shown as the text of the link.

**Matchers**
:   Conditions on the Alert Group's common labels. A label that only some Alerts carry counts as missing. Without
    Matchers the rule applies to every Alert Group.

**Scope**
:   **Alert Group** gives one link. **Each value of label** gives one link per distinct value of a label among the
    Alerts.

**URL template**
:   A Go template. It reads `.Labels` (the common labels for the scope Alert Group, the labels of the first Alert with
    the value otherwise), `.Value` (the label's value) and the data of the Root message template. `lookup "table" key
    "column"` reads one cell and gives an empty text when the table, the key or the column does not exist. A template
    that writes nothing, or something that is not an `http` or `https` URL, gives no link.

All the Link rules of one message together read at most 100 rows with `lookup` in one render
(`template.lookups_per_render`); the 101st is a template error, and a Link rule that fails is left out of the message
and counted.

Example: a dashboard per cluster.

1. Create the Lookup table `dashboards` with the column `url` and one row for each cluster: the key `prod-eu`, the
   value `https://grafana.example.org/d/abc123/prod-eu`.
2. Create the Link rule `Dashboard`, scope **Alert Group**, with the URL template
   `{{ lookup "dashboards" .Labels.cluster "url" }}`.
3. The preview of the rule shows the link for a sample. Alert Groups with `cluster="prod-eu"` now carry **Dashboard**.

A rule with the scope **Each value of label** and the label `pod` can build one log link per pod:
`https://logs.example.org/search?pod={{ .Value | urlquery }}`.

Muster adds links without a rule as well: the annotations `runbook_url` and `dashboard_url`, shown as **Runbook** and
**Dashboard**, and the `generatorURL` of the first firing Alert, shown as **Source**.

The built-in Link rule **Explore** opens the query of the Alert in Grafana's Explore. It reads the Lookup table
`grafana` with the columns `address` (the address of your Grafana) and `datasource_uid`, and the key is the value of the
`environment` label, else of the `cluster` label. It cannot be deleted, renamed or given another scope; its Matchers and
URL template can be changed. A Lookup table that a Link rule reads cannot be deleted or renamed.

The API has `lookup-tables` and `link-rules` for the same: see the [API reference](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/api.md). A list of
Lookup tables comes at most 50 to a page (`lookup_table.page_max`), since each carries its rows.

## Thread replies

Lifecycle events that are Thread replies, such as a Takeover or a Reopen, are sent at once. Only new Alerts are
batched, by the Route's **Thread batching window** (**Routes → a Route → Delivery**, `route.thread_batching_window`, 60
seconds by default): the first new Alert is sent at once and opens the window, and the new Alerts that arrive within it
are sent as one reply when it closes. After a quiet period longer than the window, the next one is again immediate. A
reply lists the first 10 new Alerts and then "…and K more" (`delivery.thread_alerts_listed`).

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/organization.md -->
# Organization settings

The **Organization** is the owner of all Users, Routes and data in Muster; there is one. Its settings change behaviour
for everyone, so only Admins open them: choose **Organization** in the main navigation, then a page of its
sub-navigation. Every change is recorded in the Audit log (**Organization → Audit log**) with a before and after, and two Admins
editing the same page do not overwrite each other: the second save is refused with "Someone else changed these settings.
Reload to see them.", and you
reload and apply your change again.

The defaults below are what a new installation has.

## General

**Organization → General**

**Name** (`organization.name`, `Muster`)
:   The name of the Organization.

**Time zone of messages** (`organization.time_zone`, `UTC`)
:   The time zone of every time in a message in a messenger. It is `UTC` until you change it, so a new installation
    shows times such as "started 07:12" in UTC. Times in messages are absolute, never "5 minutes ago". Each User sees the
    web UI in their own time zone, which they set in their profile.

**Start of the working day** (`organization.workday_start`, `09:00`) and **First day of the week** (`organization.week_start`, `monday`)
:   The Snooze presets "Until tomorrow 09:00" and "Until Monday 09:00" end at this time of day and on this day, in the
    time zone of the person who snoozes. A change applies to Snoozes set afterwards; a Snooze already set does not move.
    See [statuses and commands](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/statuses-and-commands.md).

## Severity levels

**Organization → Severity levels**

Alerts say how bad they are in a label. Muster turns its values into three **Severity levels**: critical, warning and
info.

**Severity label** (`organization.severity_label`, `severity`)
:   The label that carries the severity.

**Mapping** (`organization.severity_mapping`)
:   Values of that label and their level. By default `critical` is critical, `warning` is warning, and `info` and `none`
    are info. A label that is missing counts as info; any other value counts as warning and is shown as received.

**Emoji and colours** (`organization.severity_styles`)
:   The emoji and the colour of each level: critical 🟥 `#d32f2f`, warning 🟧 `#f57c00`, info 🟦 `#1976d2`.

**Values seen** (`organization.severity_values_window`, the last 14 days)
:   The values of the severity label that arrived, with their counts. A value with no mapping is marked "No mapping —
    counts as warning" and has a **Map** action. If your alerts use `P1` and `page`, map them to critical here.

## Alert handling

**Organization → Alert handling**

**Critical is Urgent** (`organization.critical_is_urgent`, on)
:   An Alert Group whose Severity level is critical is **Urgent**. See [Loud and Quiet](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/loud-and-quiet.md).

**Instance labels** (`organization.instance_labels`, `pod`, `instance`, `container`, `endpoint`)
:   A new Alert that differs from a firing one only in these labels is a **Replacement**: it stays in the same Alert
    Group, and the Timeline names the label that changed.

Changes to Severity levels and Instance labels apply to Alerts evaluated from then on. Open Alert Groups keep their
status.

## Security

**Organization → Security**

**TOTP required** (`organization.totp_required`, **Nobody**)
:   **Nobody**, **Local users** (Users who sign in with a password) or **Everyone** (OIDC users too). A person the
    policy covers who has no TOTP sets it up right after their next sign-in. See [TOTP](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/totp.md).

**Token grace for OIDC users without an offline token** (`auth.oidc_token_grace`, 7 days)
:   Applies to Users who sign in through OpenID Connect when the identity provider granted no offline token. Their
    Personal access tokens work while their last OIDC sign-in is no older than this; after that they get `401` with the
    code `oidc_recheck_required` until the person signs in through OIDC again. Service account tokens are not affected.
    See [API tokens and automation](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/api-tokens.md).

## Outbound addresses

**Organization → Outbound addresses**

The **Outbound address policy** (`organization.outbound_policy`) says which network addresses Muster may call:
Destinations, Connections, the identity provider, proxies and the outgoing heartbeat. The check runs after the name is
resolved, so a name that points at a blocked address is blocked.

- **Standard** (the default) allows private addresses and blocks loopback.
- **Strict** allows only public addresses and the entries you allow.

**Allowed** and **Denied** (`organization.outbound_allowed`, `organization.outbound_denied`, both empty) take a network
such as `10.0.0.0/8`, an address, a host name or a domain such as `*.example.org`. A denied entry always wins. Some
addresses are always blocked and no allowed entry opens them: link-local, cloud metadata, unspecified and multicast
addresses. A chat server on the loopback address, for one, needs `127.0.0.0/8` in **Allowed** under Standard.

## Retention

**Organization → Retention**

**Stored Snapshots (days)** (`retention.stored_snapshots`, 14)
:   Snapshots kept as received, for debugging, previews and replay.

**Alert details (days)** (`retention.alert_details`, 90)
:   Alerts inside Alert Groups, Timeline entries and delivery events. Never Notes.

**Alert Group summaries (days)** (`retention.alert_group_summaries`, 730)
:   The summary row of an Alert Group, with its Notes.

**Audit log (days)** (`retention.audit_log`, 365)
:   Who changed or did what.

Each period is 1 to 36,500 days. The summaries must be kept at least as long as the details, because details go first;
a save that breaks this is refused (`retention_order`).

## Elsewhere

Other Organization pages have their own guides: **Keyring** in [Key rotation](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/key-rotation.md), **Outgoing
heartbeat** (`outgoing_heartbeat.url`, unset) in [Outgoing heartbeat](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/outgoing-heartbeat.md), **Lookup
tables** and **Link rules** in [Messages and templates](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/messages-and-templates.md#links), and **System status** and the
**Audit log** for what is wrong or who changed what.

## The API

`GET /api/v1/organization` reads the Organization and its `ETag`; `PUT /api/v1/organization` replaces the fields above
with `If-Match` set to that ETag, as [API tokens and automation](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/api-tokens.md#conventions) shows. The fields are
`name`, `time_zone`, `workday_start`, `week_start`, `severity_label`, `severity_mapping`, `severity_styles`,
`critical_is_urgent`, `instance_labels`, `outgoing_heartbeat` (required, with `proxy`, whose `enabled` is
required; `url` is write-only and kept when omitted), `retention` (`stored_snapshots_days`, `alert_details_days`,
`alert_group_summaries_days`, `audit_log_days`), `totp_required` (`nobody`, `local_users` or `everyone`) and
`oidc_token_grace_seconds`. The outbound policy is `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/organization/outbound-policy`, and the values
seen are `GET /api/v1/organization/severity-values`. Reading the Organization needs any sign-in; reading the outbound
policy and the values seen needs `organization:read`, and changing anything needs `organization:write`; only the Admin
Role holds both. `workday_start` and `week_start` are optional on an update.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/api-tokens.md -->
# API tokens and automation

Everything the web UI does, a script can do through the API, as a person or as a non-person identity. This page shows
how to get a token, how to call the API, and what to expect from it. The [API reference](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/api.md) lists
every operation, its Permission and its answers; the binary serves the same specification at `/api/v1/openapi.yaml`.

## Two kinds of token

A **Personal access token** acts as a User. It has the Permissions you choose, never more than you hold, and it loses
what your Role loses. Use it for your own scripts. Its prefix is `mstr_pat_`.

A **Service account** is an identity that is not a person, such as Terraform or a pipeline. It has a name, a Role and
any number of tokens, whose prefix is `mstr_sat_`. It cannot sign in to the web UI and has no Account links.

!!! note "A Service account cannot become an Owner"
    The Owner of an Alert Group is always a User. Acknowledge from a Service account is refused with `409` and the code
    `owner_must_be_user`. It may Resolve, Snooze and add Notes, and the Timeline shows the Service account as the actor.
    A Personal access token acts as its User, so acknowledging with one makes that User the Owner.

An **Integration token** (`mstr_int_`) is a third kind and is not for the API: it sends alerts and Heartbeats only, and
the API does not accept it. See [Connect Alertmanager](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/alertmanager.md).

The prefix `mstr_` and the kind in it let secret scanners find a token that leaked into a repository. If one does,
revoke it.

## Create a Personal access token

Tokens are created in the web UI. A token cannot create or revoke another token, so there is no API call to start from
nothing.

1. Open **Profile**, **Personal access tokens**, and select **Create token**.
2. Give it a **Name** that says where it is used, such as `laptop-scripts`.
3. Under **Permissions** tick what the script needs. You see only the Permissions you hold. A script that reads Alert
   Groups needs `alert-groups:read`; one that also acknowledges needs `alert-groups:acknowledge`.
4. Choose **Expires on**. A token may have no expiry (`token.expiry` is none by default), but the page warns about a
   token that never expires: choose a date.
5. Select **Create**. The dialog shows the token once. Copy it before you close it: only a hash is kept.

The list shows when each token was created, when and from which address it was last used, and when it expires.
**Revoke** stops a script that uses it at once. The Audit log records a request made with a token as "alex via token
laptop-scripts".

## Create a Service account

1. Open **Access → Service accounts** and select **Create service account**.
2. Give it a **Name** and a **Role**: Admin, Responder or Viewer. You can give only a Role whose Permissions you hold.
3. On its page, under **Tokens**, select **Create token**, give it a name and an expiry, and copy the value once.

Its tokens act with the Role of the account, and changing the Role changes every token at once. To change a token
without a gap, create the second token, switch the pipeline to it and revoke the first. **Disable** stops all its tokens
until you **Enable** it; **Delete** revokes them for good.

## Call the API

Send the token as a bearer token. The API is under `/api/v1` of the address people open, `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL`:

```sh
MUSTER=https://muster.example.org
TOKEN=mstr_pat_...
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$MUSTER/api/v1/alert-groups?status=firing&limit=20"
```

The answer is JSON: `items` and `next_cursor`. A request with no token, or a wrong one, gets `401`; one with a token
that lacks the Permission gets `403`. Every operation in the reference names the Permission it needs.

Snooze the Alert Group `AGK7M3QX9P2RTA` until a time (the token needs `alert-groups:snooze`):

```sh
curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"until": "2026-10-20T08:00:00Z"}' "$MUSTER/api/v1/alert-groups/AGK7M3QX9P2RTA/snooze"
```

A call on the interactive path, such as a check of a Connection, answers `503` with `Retry-After` when Muster's limit
toward the messenger leaves no room within 5 seconds (`delivery.interactive_budget`); retry after the pause.

A few operations need the web session and refuse a token with `403` (`session_required`): changing your own password,
TOTP, Account links and tokens.

### Conventions

**Identifiers**
:   URLs carry the `public_id` of a resource, such as `AGK7M3QX9P2RTA`, never the `#N` of an Alert Group.

**Pagination**
:   `limit` is 50 by default and at most 500 (`api.page_size`). A page carries `next_cursor`; send it back as `cursor`
    for the next page. There are no offsets.

**Changing configuration**
:   Routes, Destinations, the Organization and other configuration carry an `ETag`, in a header and in the body. Read
    it, then update with `PUT` and `If-Match` set to it. A stale value gets `412`, a missing header `428`. This stops
    two writers from overwriting each other.

    ```sh
    curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$MUSTER/api/v1/organization" | grep -i '^etag'
    ```

    Then send the changed Organization with `-X PUT -H 'If-Match: <that value>'`. An omitted optional field keeps its
    stored value, and an explicit `null` clears one that can be cleared.

**Errors**
:   RFC 9457 problems (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `type` and `code`, and `errors[]` with a JSON pointer to
    each invalid field.

**Times and units**
:   RFC 3339 in UTC; durations in whole seconds in `*_seconds`; retention in `*_days`.

**Secrets**
:   Write-only. A read shows whether a secret is set and when it changed, never its value.

### Rate limit

The API is limited per token: 20 requests per second with bursts of 100 (`api.rate_limit`), counted on each Muster
replica. A request over the limit gets `429` with `Retry-After` in seconds; wait that long and retry. Another token is
not affected. Web sessions and ingestion are not limited.

## Tokens of OIDC users

A Personal access token of a User who signs in through OpenID Connect follows the identity provider. If the provider
refuses the person at a background re-check, the token gets `401` with the code `oidc_recheck_required` and the text
"Sign in through OIDC to make your tokens work again", and works again after the person's next OIDC sign-in, without a
new token. When the provider granted no offline token, the tokens also stop once the last OIDC sign-in is older than the
Organization's grace period (`auth.oidc_token_grace`, 7 days; **Organization → Security**, see
[Organization settings](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/organization.md#security)). Your profile shows the date until which your tokens work. Service
account tokens are not affected, which is why automation belongs on a Service account.

A web session has its own lifetimes: see [Sign-in](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/index.md#ways-to-sign-in).

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/alertmanager.md -->
# Connect Alertmanager

Muster receives alerts from Alertmanager through an Alertmanager receiver with a webhook. Each delivery is a
**Snapshot** of one Alertmanager group: every alert of the Alertmanager group that still fires, and its resolves. Muster stores each request exactly as
received, answers `202` once it is written, and processes it afterwards.

In the examples, `MUSTER_INGEST_URL` is `https://ingest.muster.example.org`.

## One Integration per Alertmanager cluster

Create one **Integration** for each Alertmanager cluster that sends to Muster. An HA pair — two or more Alertmanager
instances that gossip with each other — is **one** cluster and gets **one** Integration: both instances send the same
notifications, and Muster folds their copies together within the Integration's duplicate window. Two independent
Alertmanagers, such as one per region, get one Integration each, so that each has its own repeats, its own Static
labels and its own health.

Static labels are added to every alert of the Integration before routing, for example `cluster=prod-eu`, so that Routes
and messages can tell the clusters apart.

Alertmanager pushes its Snapshots to Muster by webhook: the Integration's connection mode is `webhook-only`
(`integration.connection_mode`), the only mode in this version.

## Create a token and paste the snippet

In **Integrations**, create the Integration, then **Create token**. Muster shows the token and a ready Alertmanager
snippet **once**; copy it before you close the dialog. Only a hash of the token is kept, so a lost token cannot be shown
again: create a new one.

The snippet has two parts. The Alertmanager receiver goes into `receivers`:

```yaml
receivers:
  - name: muster-prod-eu
    webhook_configs:
      - url: https://ingest.muster.example.org/api/v1/ingest
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 0
        http_config:
          authorization:
            type: Bearer
            credentials: mstr_int_…
```

- `send_resolved: true` sends resolves, which close alerts in Muster at once.
- `max_alerts: 0` sends every alert of the Alertmanager group. Muster treats each Snapshot as the whole Alertmanager
  group; a Truncated Snapshot makes it warn.
- The token travels as `Authorization: Bearer`. A sender that cannot set a header may append the token to the URL
  instead, as `/api/v1/ingest/<token>`; Muster's logs name only the route, never such a path.

The route goes first under the top-level `route`, before your other child routes:

```yaml
route:
  routes:
    - receiver: muster-prod-eu
      continue: true
      repeat_interval: 10m
    # ... your existing child routes
    # The last child route: a catch-all without matchers for the receiver of the top-level route.
    # - receiver: <your default receiver>
```

- With no matchers, the route takes every alert, and `continue: true` passes each alert on to the child routes after
  it, so Muster runs beside your current Alertmanager receivers while you try it.
- **Keep a catch-all child route last.** Alertmanager sends an alert to the receiver of the top-level `route` only when
  no child route matches it. The Muster route matches every alert, so without a catch-all, an alert that none of your
  other child routes matches goes to Muster alone and your default receiver stops getting it. Add a last child route
  without matchers for your default receiver, or make sure an existing later child route already catches everything.

For example, a configuration that sends critical alerts to `oncall` and everything else to the top-level `default`:

```yaml
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - receiver: oncall
      matchers: ['severity="critical"']
```

becomes:

```yaml
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - receiver: muster-prod-eu
      continue: true
      repeat_interval: 10m
    - receiver: oncall
      matchers: ['severity="critical"']
    - receiver: default
```

A critical alert goes to `muster-prod-eu` and `oncall`, any other alert to `muster-prod-eu` and `default`. Without the
last line, a warning would reach only Muster. `amtool config routes test --config.file=alertmanager.yml
severity=warning` prints the receivers an alert reaches; it should list Muster and your default receiver.

- Keep `repeat_interval` between **5 and 15 minutes** (10 minutes in the snippet, `snippet.repeat_interval`). See
  [Repeat intervals](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/alertmanager.md#repeat-intervals) for why.

Reload Alertmanager (`POST /-/reload` or `SIGHUP`). The Integration page then shows the time of the last Snapshot and
the Stored Snapshots as received.

## Repeat intervals

Keep the `repeat_interval` of the route that sends to Muster between **5 and 15 minutes**. It is a setting of the
route, not of the receiver, so a route that sends only some alerts to Muster can have its own.

Muster learns from the repeats. An Alertmanager group sends a Snapshot again each time `repeat_interval` elapses, and
Muster measures the gaps between those Snapshots. Two rules depend on them:

- An Alert is **Gone** when at least two consecutive Snapshots of its Alertmanager group, and at least
  `processing.gone_min_absence` (5 minutes), do not list it any more. This is how Muster notices an alert that
  Alertmanager dropped without a `resolved` notification.
- An Alert goes **Stale** when its Alertmanager group sends no Snapshot at all for `processing.stale_after_factor`
  (3) times the learned repeat interval, for example when the group is silenced in Alertmanager. It applies only while
  the Integration's [Heartbeat](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/heartbeat.md) is live. Until Muster has learned the interval, it waits
  `processing.stale_after_unlearned` (25 hours).

Alertmanager sends a repeat on the first `group_interval` tick after `repeat_interval` has elapsed, so the gaps are
about `repeat_interval` + `group_interval`. With 10 minutes and Alertmanager's default `group_interval` of 5 minutes,
Muster learns an interval of about 15 minutes, and an Alert of a silenced group goes Stale after about 45 minutes. With
a daily interval it takes more than three days, and the Integration page warns about an interval longer than
`processing.long_repeat_warning` (1 hour) and shows the route to put in Alertmanager. A short interval does not make
Muster noisy: Muster sends one message per Alert Group and edits it, so a repeat changes nothing that people see. It
only makes Muster faster to notice that an alert is gone.

The routes Muster has learned, with their intervals and the time each needs to resolve by absence, are on the
Integration page.

## Send every alert of the group

Set `max_alerts: 0` on the webhook configuration, as the snippet does. Alertmanager's default is no limit, but a
`max_alerts` above 0 makes it keep only the first alerts of a group in each notification and count the rest in
`truncatedAlerts`. A truncated Snapshot lists only part of the Alertmanager group, so Muster cannot tell an alert that is
missing from one that was cut off. It never takes a truncated Snapshot as proof of absence: it keeps the unlisted Alerts
firing as long as Snapshots of that group keep arriving, which can keep a resolved Alert open. It raises the Internal
alert `MusterSnapshotTruncated` for the Integration and counts the Snapshot in
`muster_ingest_truncated_snapshots_total`. If you see that alert, set `max_alerts: 0` on the receiver and reload
Alertmanager; the [runbook](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterSnapshotTruncated.md) has the steps.

## Static labels

Static labels belong to the Integration, not to Alertmanager. Add them in the Integration's settings, such as
`cluster=prod-eu`; Muster adds them to every Alert of the Integration before it routes the Alert, so a Route and a Group
key can use them as if the rules had set them.

- Use them for what the Alertmanager cluster knows and the rules do not: the cluster, the region, the environment. The
  default Group key of a Route includes `cluster`, so Alert Groups of different clusters stay apart.
- An Alert that already has the label keeps its own value. Muster then warns about the label on the Alert and in its
  Alert Group's Timeline, and the Alerts view of the Integration shows the warning. A Static label never overwrites a
  label that a rule set.

## Instance labels in informational alerts

**Instance labels** are the labels that change when the process that reports an Alert restarts, such as `pod` and
`instance`. The Organization lists them in `organization.instance_labels` (by default `pod`, `instance`, `container`
and `endpoint`).

Keep them out of informational alerts, the ones nobody needs to act on at once, such as those of a Route with the
Informational profile. A
restarted pod reports the same problem under a new `pod` label, which is a different Alert. Muster recognises that
case: it records a **Replacement**, a Quiet event in the Timeline that names the label that differs, and the Alert Group
page suggests fixing the rule. But every restart still adds an Alert and a Timeline entry to an Alert Group that was
meant to be calm, and if the label is also in the Route's Group key, each pod gets an Alert Group of its own.

Aggregate the label away in the rule instead, for example `sum without(pod, instance) (...)` in the expression. Keep the label where it helps a person find the culprit, in
an annotation rather than a label. For alerts about one particular pod that people must act on, Instance labels are fine:
there each pod is a separate problem.

## Start delay

When Alertmanager starts, it does not know the alerts that were firing before. It learns them again as the rule
evaluators (Prometheus, vmalert) send them, and until then its Alertmanager groups list only part of their alerts. A
Snapshot sent in that time is **partial**, and Muster would take the missing alerts as Gone.

Set `--dispatch.start-delay` so that Alertmanager waits before it sends. It must be at least **twice** the longer of the
rule evaluation interval and the rule evaluator's resend delay, plus a margin. Prometheus re-sends a firing alert only
every second evaluation at its defaults, so with a 1-minute evaluation interval use **about 2.5 minutes or more**:

```sh
alertmanager --dispatch.start-delay=2m30s ...
```

With 90 seconds, the first Snapshot after a start was still partial in tests.

## HA pairs need a persistent volume
