Muster stores all three secrets encrypted, never shows them again and writes them to no log line.

## Create the Connection

In Muster, create a **Connection** of type Slack. Enter a name, choose the event mode, and enter the bot token and, in
Socket Mode, the app-level token, or over HTTP the Slack signing secret. A Slack Connection has no address field, since
Slack's address is fixed. Then **Check connection**. The check runs in steps and shows the latency of each and whether
it went through the proxy:

1. **Token**: `auth.test` with the bot token, which names the bot and the workspace and fails if the token is not a
   bot's;
2. **Scopes**: every scope of the manifest is granted;
3. **App-level token**, in Socket Mode: the token belongs to the same app as the bot token, and Slack opens a
   connection for it. The check opens no WebSocket.

Over HTTP no request can show that Slack reaches the callback address or that the Slack signing secret is right, because
a bot cannot press its own button. The first press does: see [The test message](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/slack.md#the-test-message).

**Check connection** also works in the form before anything is saved. It checks the values in the form and saves
nothing, and no bot name is recorded. A stored token goes to Slack only through the saved proxy: after a change of the
proxy, type the tokens again to check, or save first.

## Invite the bot and create Destinations

A bot posts only to channels it is a member of. In Slack, invite the bot to each channel a Destination posts to, public
or private:

```text
/invite @Muster
```

In Muster, create a **Destination** of type Slack with the Connection and the channel. The form lists the public and
private channels the bot is a member of; for a channel that is not listed, type its id as Slack shows it in the
channel's details, `C…` or `G…`. A direct chat or a person cannot be a Destination. Saving runs the **Destination
check**, which asks Slack about the channel with `conversations.info` and refuses a Destination that fails:

- `channel_not_found`: no such channel, or a private channel the bot is not in;
- `channel_archived`: the channel is archived;
- `bot_not_in_channel`: "Invite the bot to the channel: /invite @{bot}", where `{bot}` is the bot's name as Slack
  reports it for the bot token, such as `muster`.

The bot's name appears in that hint only after **Check connection** has run on the saved Connection; before that it
says only "Invite the bot to the channel."

**Check** on the Destination page runs the same check at any time. When Slack refuses the bot later, for example
because someone removed it from the channel, the Destination becomes **Broken**; Muster runs the check every few
minutes while nothing waits for the Destination, and ends the Broken state once it passes again, for example after
someone invites the bot back. See [Broken Destinations](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/broken-destinations.md).

## Link accounts

A button acts as a Muster User, and a Mention reaches a person, only through an Account link. The person enters their
Slack email or name in their profile, and the bot sends a code by direct message, in the Messages tab of the app. The
code has 8 characters, is valid for 10 minutes and allows 5 attempts (`account_link.slack_code`). See [Link
Slack](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/account-links.md#link-slack).

## Where answers to presses show

A successful press is not answered: the Root message changes. Whatever the person who pressed must read — that the press
was refused, that their Slack account is not linked to Muster yet, or that the button could not be verified — shows in
the channel as a message only they can see, marked "Only visible to you". Unlike Mattermost, Slack needs no permission
beyond `chat:write` for it. For a press on a Thread reply, such as a Reminder, the answer shows in the Thread. The one
success that is answered is "Still on it", which changes no message.

Slack does not guarantee such a message: the person must be active and in the channel. When Slack refuses it, Muster
sends the same text to the press's `response_url`, on `hooks.slack.com`; an answer that fails both ways is logged and
not tried again. Answers are in the language of the User the account is linked to, and in English for an account
without a link.

A replica handles at most 2 presses at a time (`slack.parallel_presses`); the others wait, already confirmed to Slack. A
press whose deadline ends while it waits for a slot, 30 seconds after it was handed over (`slack.press_deadline`), is
answered, in English, that it failed. At most 64 presses wait for a slot in a process (`slack.max_waiting_presses`): one
more, and a press still waiting or running at the end of the shutdown's grace period, fails without an answer and is
logged. None of these bounds is configurable.

## Who gets notified

Slack cannot send a message without a notification: whom a new message notifies depends on each member's settings for
the channel and the Thread. So, as in Mattermost, **Quiet** means "without a Mention", not "nobody is notified".

- **Edits are Quiet.** An edit of the Root message carries no Mention, so a Loud change is always a new message: a new
  Root message, or a reply in the Thread. The edit drops the Mentions that the Root message had; Slack may then remove
  them from the person's list of mentions.
- **Mentions** are `@channel` and `@here`, as the Destination's Mention settings ask, and the people chosen in them,
  through their Account links. A person without a link is named by their display name as text, which notifies nobody. A
  Slack Destination takes neither `@all` nor groups. The footer of a Root message names a linked person without a
  Mention.
- **Thread replies** stay in the Thread: Muster never also broadcasts them to the channel.
- **Alert data and template text never mention anyone.** An `&`, `<` or `>` in a label or an annotation is escaped, and
  so is `@`. A literal `<!here>` or `<@U…>` written in a template is shown as text and notifies nobody. Only the
  Destination's Mention settings, `{{ mention "here" }}` and its siblings, and linked people notify.

See [Loud and Quiet](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/loud-and-quiet.md).

## Rate limits

Muster limits itself, and Slack limits it too.

`connection.slack.limiter`
:   50 requests a minute for every call of the Connection to the Web API together, the minimum Slack documents for the
    methods that edit and delete.

`destination.slack.limiter`
:   30 requests a minute for the sends and edits of a Destination together, half of Slack's "one message per second per
    channel".

Slack limits each method per app and workspace. When it answers `429`, Muster holds every request of the Connection, for
any of its Destinations, for the seconds of `Retry-After`; this is not counted as a failed attempt, and does not make a
Destination Broken. A `429` without `Retry-After` counts as a transient failure. You can change both limiters.

## Edits and deleted Root messages

Muster edits a Root message for as long as its Alert Group is open, which can be days. Slack lets a
bot edit its own messages, and no edit window is known for them. Whether a window that your workspace sets applies to
the messages of a bot, hours or days old, has not been verified; an edit that Slack refuses that way ends that delivery
as Not delivered and does not make the Destination Broken.

When someone deletes a Root message, Muster finds out at its next edit, when Slack answers `message_not_found`. It
checks that the bot is still in the channel and the channel is not archived, and then posts the Alert Group again once,
Quietly, with a note. If the bot is gone or the channel archived, the Destination becomes Broken instead. A Root message
that already had replies stays in the channel as "This message was deleted." with its replies, and Muster's later
replies still go under it until the next edit finds it gone.

A Root message deleted before it had any reply takes no reply: Slack posts a reply to it into the channel, as an
ordinary message, and answers as if it had worked. Muster notices, deletes that message at once and posts the Alert
Group again. The reply may stay in the channel for a moment. If Slack refuses the deletion, Muster does not try again:
the stray reply stays until someone deletes it, and the delivery records why.

## The test message

**Send test message** on the Destination page posts one message marked "🧪 Test message", with the buttons of its status,
and **Preview** shows the message as Muster would send it. No Alert Group changes.

A bot cannot press its own button in Slack, so the test message cannot prove that presses reach Muster, as Mattermost's
does. Press a button of the test message yourself: Muster answers you "This is a test message; nothing was changed",
even from an account without a link. That answer proves that presses reach Muster and, over HTTP, that the Slack
signing secret is right.

## The proxy

A Slack Connection has a proxy section like the others; see [Proxies](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/proxies.md). The proxy must allow `CONNECT` to
`slack.com`; in Socket Mode also to the hosts under `slack.com` that the socket uses; and to `hooks.slack.com`, where
the fallback answers to presses go. Where only the proxy can resolve outside names and the Organization's outbound
address policy is strict, add `slack.com` and `*.slack.com` to **Allowed**: the domain entry covers `hooks.slack.com`
and the socket's hosts, but not `slack.com` itself. See [Proxies](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/proxies.md#what-the-outbound-address-policy-checks).

Muster accepts a Socket Mode address only on `slack.com` or a host below it, and an answer address only on
`hooks.slack.com`. If the socket cannot open, the Leader backs off (`slack.socket_backoff`, from 1 second up to 5
minutes), logs [`slack_socket_failed`](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/log-events.md#slack_socket_failed), and does not make any
Destination Broken. It waits `slack.hello_timeout`, 10 seconds, for Slack's greeting on a new socket.

## Request log

The **Request log** of a Slack Connection records its calls to the Web API named as Slack names them, such as
`chat.postMessage` and `apps.connections.open`. Over HTTP it records each press that reaches the callback address as
`interactive`, with Muster's answer, refused ones included. In Socket Mode it records each envelope that carries an
envelope id under the type of the envelope, with the socket's host as its address and Muster's confirmation as its
answer; the app subscribes to no events, so only `interactive` envelopes arrive. Slack's greetings, disconnects and
keep-alive frames are not recorded. The answers Muster sends to a press's `response_url` are recorded as `response_url`,
with the address masked: look there when an answer never shows. Tokens, the Slack signing secret and the signature are
masked, and so are the address of the socket, the `response_url` of a press, the signed ids of buttons and the code of
an Account link. See [Request log](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/request-log.md).

## Check from the command line

`muster doctor` prints one line per Slack Connection and per Slack Destination with the same checks, without sending
anything, and a `WARN` line for a Connection whose app another program shares.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/proxies.md -->
# Proxies

Muster has no proxy for the whole installation. Each client that talks to the outside has a proxy setting of its own, so
that traffic that must go through a proxy does, and traffic that must not, such as the identity provider's, goes
straight. `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` are **never read**, in any process of Muster.

## Where you set a proxy

| Client | Where |
|---|---|
| a Mattermost, Slack, Telegram or Bridge Connection | the Connection's proxy section |
| an outgoing webhook Destination | the Destination's proxy section |
| the identity provider (OpenID Connect) | the OIDC settings |
| the Organization's outgoing heartbeat | its settings |

The setting is off by default. Every one of these has the same form:

- **Use a proxy**, a switch. Switching it off keeps the other fields, so that you can switch it on again.
- **Type**: `http`, `https` or `socks5`.
- **Address**, as `host:port` with a port from 1 to 65535.
- **Username** and **password**, when the proxy needs them. The username must not contain a colon or a line break and is
  at most 255 bytes long.

The three types differ in how Muster talks to the proxy:

| Type | Muster speaks to the proxy | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP | plain HTTP | for an HTTPS target, Muster asks the proxy for a tunnel with `CONNECT` |
| HTTPS | HTTP over TLS | the connection to the proxy is encrypted |
| SOCKS5 | the SOCKS5 protocol | the proxy resolves the name of the target |

## The password

The proxy password is a secret like the others: it is encrypted with the master key, write-only in the API and the web
UI (they show whether it is set, never the value), and replaced with `[redacted]` in every log line and error. A stored
password is used only with the proxy type and address it was saved with. When you change either, type the password
again.

## Checks take the same path

The connection check of a Connection, and the test of a Destination, go through the saved proxy just as real traffic
does. If the check works, delivery works by the same route. A check run from the form before saving uses the proxy in
the form instead. A token that is already stored goes only to the saved address of its Connection, through its saved
proxy: with a changed but unsaved address or proxy and no token typed, the check makes only a probe without the
token.

## What the outbound address policy checks

Every outbound connection of Muster is checked by the Organization's outbound address policy, **standard** or
**strict**, with its lists of allowed and denied networks, host names and domains. The Admins edit the policy under
Organization → Outbound addresses. Through a proxy, two things are checked:

1. **The proxy's own address.** It is checked like any other target, after name resolution. A proxy setting cannot reach
   a link-local or cloud metadata address, such as `169.254.169.254`, and a proxy on a loopback address works only when an
   allowed network contains it.
2. **The target.** The proxy resolves the target's name, so Muster resolves it too, and every address it gets must pass
   the policy; for a target given as an IP address, that address is checked. A request to a name that resolves to a
   blocked address is refused before it is sent, without retry, and the error names the rule.

In a closed network, only the proxy may be able to resolve outside names. When Muster cannot resolve the target's name
itself, it checks the name instead: a name that matches a denied entry is blocked, and in strict mode only a name that
matches an allowed entry passes. A request that passes is sent without an address check, and Muster logs that.

Muster cannot see where the proxy finally connects to. The Admin who sets the proxy chooses to trust it.

## Telegram

Telegram is often reached through a proxy where it is blocked. [Telegram in restricted
networks](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/telegram-restricted-networks.md) shows the proxy on the Connection, and the alternatives: a reverse proxy
under your own domain and a self-hosted Bot API server.

## Slack

A Slack Connection has no address field, since Slack's address is fixed, so a proxy sees only Slack's hosts. It must
allow `CONNECT` to `slack.com`; in Socket Mode also to the hosts under `slack.com` that the socket uses; and to
`hooks.slack.com`, where Muster sends the answer to a press when it cannot send it in the channel. When only the proxy
can resolve outside names and the policy is strict, add `slack.com` and `*.slack.com` to **Allowed**: the domain entry
covers the socket's hosts and `hooks.slack.com`, but not `slack.com` itself. See [Connect Slack](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/slack.md#the-proxy).

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/bridge.md -->
# Connect a messenger through a bridge

A **bridge** connects Muster to a messenger that Muster does not support natively. It is a separate service that
speaks the Bridge protocol with Muster on one side and talks to your messenger on the other: Muster sends it every
message as an **envelope** — the status, the title, a link, the text and the buttons — and the bridge renders the
envelope in its messenger. A **Bridge Connection** is one bot of your messenger behind one bridge: one token is one
bot. Muster posts one **Root message** per Alert Group to a channel of that messenger, edits it as the Alert Group
changes, and replies in its **Thread** for what happens later, as it does for Mattermost, Slack and Telegram.

To write a bridge, read [Write a bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md); the protocol itself is the
[Bridge protocol](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/bridge-protocol.md) reference.

In the examples, `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL` is `https://muster.example.org`, `MUSTER_INGEST_URL` is
`https://ingest.muster.example.org` and the bridge listens on `https://bridge.example.org`. The examples use the
[API](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/api.md), with a Personal access token of an Admin in `MUSTER_TOKEN`; the web UI has the same forms
under **Connections** and **Destinations**.

## Create the Connection

From your bridge, you need:

- its **base URL**, an `http` or `https` address with an optional path prefix, such as
  `https://bridge.example.org/muster`. Muster sends every request to `<base URL>/v1/…`, and only there, with
  `User-Agent: Muster/<version>`;
- the **token** it gave your bot. Muster sends it as `Authorization: Bearer` on every request, stores it encrypted and
  never shows it again.

Choose how the bridge reports **events** — the presses of buttons and the messages people write in a Thread — with the
**event delivery** mode:

- **`poll`** (`connection.bridge.event_delivery`, the default) when the bridge cannot reach Muster. The Leader asks the
  bridge for new events, so the bridge needs no address of Muster.
- **`push`** when the bridge can reach `MUSTER_INGEST_URL`. The bridge posts each event to the Connection's callback
  address, `https://ingest.muster.example.org/api/v1/callbacks/bridge/CN…`, which the Connection shows in
  `callback_url`, signed with a **push secret** that you configure on both sides. The push secret has the Standard
  Webhooks form, `whsec_` followed by base64, and is write-only like the token.

A Connection also has a **proxy**, for a bridge that Muster reaches only through one, and a **limiter**: 10 requests
per second by default, shared by all its Destinations. When the bridge answers that it is rate-limited, Muster waits
as long as it asks, whatever the limiter allows.

```sh
curl -X POST https://muster.example.org/api/v1/connections \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUSTER_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"type":"bridge","name":"Team chat","base_url":"https://bridge.example.org/muster",
       "bot_token":"the-token-of-the-bot","event_delivery":"poll","proxy":{"enabled":false},
       "limiter":{"limit":10,"per_seconds":1}}'
```

For `push`, set `"event_delivery":"push"` and add `"push_secret":"whsec_…"`.

## What the check shows

Check the Connection after you create it, and after every change of the bridge:

```sh
curl -X POST https://muster.example.org/api/v1/connections/CNK7M3QX9P2RTA/checks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUSTER_TOKEN"
```

The check calls the bridge's `getInfo` and shows two steps, each with its latency and whether it went through the
proxy:

1. **`info`**: the bridge's name and version, the messenger's name, the protocol version — Muster speaks `1` — what
   the bridge offers, such as buttons and Thread messages, its limits, such as the longest text of a message, how it
   finds people for Account links, and its event delivery modes. Muster keeps this copy on the
   Connection and reads it again before a call that depends on it once it is older than 10 minutes, so a change in the
   bridge reaches Muster without a restart.
2. **`event_delivery`**: whether the bridge offers the Connection's event delivery mode.

A failed step names its cause with a code:

`token_invalid`
:   The bridge refused the token.

`protocol_version_unknown`
:   The bridge speaks a protocol version that this Muster does not speak.

`protocol_mismatch`
:   The answer does not match the protocol, or is larger than 64 KiB.

`event_delivery_not_offered`
:   The bridge does not offer the Connection's event delivery mode.

`proxy_refused`
:   The Connection's proxy refused its credentials (`407`).

`timeout`, `connect_failed`, `dns_failed`, `tls_failed`
:   Muster got no answer from the bridge.

`blocked`
:   The outbound address policy does not allow the bridge's address.

`request_failed`
:   The bridge answered with another error; the message names its class and the bridge's text.

## Check before saving

The check above reads a saved Connection. **Check connection** in the form of a new Connection, or on the page of a
saved one while the form holds changes, checks the values in the form before anything is saved, with
`POST /api/v1/connections/checks`. It saves nothing: the `info` it reads is returned, not stored, and the Audit log
gets no entry.

- With the token typed, the steps `info` and `event_delivery` run against the base URL in the form, through the proxy in
  the form, with that token.
- Without one, a saved Connection (`connection_id`) uses its stored token only when the base URL — a trailing `/`
  aside — and the proxy are the saved ones: the stored token is sent only to the saved address, through the saved
  proxy. After a change of the base URL or of the proxy, the check makes only a dry probe, `GET <base>/v1/info` without
  the token, which a bridge answers with `401` and a problem (`application/problem+json`). An address that answers
  otherwise fails with `not_bridge`, a `404` with `wrong_path_prefix`, another status with a problem with
  `unexpected_status`; after a dry probe that passes, `info` and `event_delivery` ask you to type the token again to
  check the new address or proxy, or to save first. A new Connection without a token gets the dry probe alone too.

```sh
curl -X POST https://muster.example.org/api/v1/connections/checks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUSTER_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"type":"bridge","base_url":"https://bridge.example.org/muster","event_delivery":"poll",
       "bot_token":"the-token-of-the-bot"}'
```

## Add a Destination

A **Bridge Destination** is one channel of the messenger, named by its **channel id** — the channel as your messenger
names it, which the bridge's documentation explains how to find. Its **Mention settings** take nobody or chosen
users; everyone in the chat and messenger groups are not available through a bridge. Its limiter allows 30 requests
per minute by default, sends and edits together.

```sh
curl -X POST https://muster.example.org/api/v1/destinations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUSTER_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"type":"bridge","name":"alerts","connection_id":"CNK7M3QX9P2RTA","channel_id":"C024BE91L",
       "mentions":{"new_alert_group":{"everyone":"none","user_ids":[],"groups":[]},
                   "new_alerts":{"everyone":"none","user_ids":[],"groups":[]},
                   "reopen":{"everyone":"none","user_ids":[],"groups":[]},
                   "ack_timeout":{"everyone":"none","user_ids":[],"groups":[]},
                   "snooze_ended":{"everyone":"none","user_ids":[],"groups":[]},
                   "rise_to_urgent":{"everyone":"none","user_ids":[],"groups":[]}},
       "limiter":{"limit":30,"per_seconds":60}}'
```

Saving the Destination runs its **Destination check**, the one item `channel`: the bridge's `checkChannel`, which
posts nothing. It passes when the bot can post, edit and reply in the channel, and the Destination then shows the
channel's name as the bridge reports it. It fails with the bridge's own text when the bridge refuses the channel —
it does not exist, or the bot is not in it — with `proxy_refused` when the Connection's proxy refuses its credentials,
and with the class of the bridge's answer otherwise; a Destination that fails the check is not saved.
`POST /api/v1/destinations/DS…/checks` runs the same check at any time.

## What Muster posts

- **The envelope.** Every Root message carries its status with a colour and an emoji, the title `#N` and the Alert
  Group's title, the link "Open in Muster" to the Alert Group page, and its text in CommonMark: the labels, the
  summary, one line per Alert, the links, the notices and the footer. A Thread reply carries its text in CommonMark.
  Alert data are escaped, so a label value cannot format the message, link anywhere or mention anyone. A Loud message
  asks the bridge to notify; a Quiet one does not.
- **The length.** The text fits the longest text the bridge declares, read from the Connection's copy of its info: a
  long Root message drops its Alert lines first, then the label sections, but always keeps its title, its status, its
  footer, its buttons and its link to Muster. The bridge may still shorten what it renders, and says so.
- **Buttons.** When the bridge offers buttons, a Root message carries the buttons of its status — Ack, Resolve, one
  per Snooze duration and the two [Snooze presets](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/statuses-and-commands.md#in-messengers) "Until tomorrow
  09:00" and "Until Monday 09:00", for example — with a style hint for each, the presets `neutral` like the durations,
  at most as many as the bridge allows. Beyond that limit the Snooze buttons go first, whatever their labels: the
  "Until Monday" preset (the first day of the week), then the "Until tomorrow" preset, then the durations from the
  longest. A firing Root message on an On-call Route has seven buttons, so a bridge that allows five gets Ack, Resolve
  and the three durations, and one that allows six also "Until tomorrow 09:00". Without buttons, a bridge that forwards
  the messages of a Thread gets a last line in each Root message that is not resolved, such as "Reply in the Thread:
  ack · resolve · snooze 1h", and takes the presets as Text commands such as `snooze tomorrow`.
- **Edits and Thread replies.** An edit sends the whole envelope of the new state, Quiet and without Mentions. A Thread
  reply goes under the Root message with the Thread reference the bridge returned last.
- **Posts are not repeated.** Every new message carries an idempotency key, the same for every retry of it. When an
  answer is lost — a timeout, or a connection cut after the request — Muster retries with the same key, the bridge
  answers with the message it posted already, and Muster edits it to the current state. When the bridge did not know
  the key, the retry may have posted a second message: the Timeline records a **possible duplicate**.
- **The token never shows** in a log line, an error, the Timeline or a metric; a test shows it as `[redacted]`.

## Edit windows

Some messengers let a bot edit a message only for a while after posting it. A bridge for such a messenger declares
how long in its info, as `limits.edit_max_age_seconds`, and Muster stops editing its Root messages in time. A bridge
that declares no limit (`null`) has none: Muster edits each Root message for as long as its Alert Group changes.

- **When Muster stops editing.** Muster makes no edit of a Root message once it is as old as the bridge's limit less
  60 seconds, counted from its Publication on Muster's clock, so that a last edit does not race the messenger's: with
  a limit of 600 seconds, the last edit is made within 9 minutes. Muster reads the limit from the Connection's copy of
  the info, as for every call. When the messenger refuses an edit earlier than declared, the bridge answers `gone` with
  the `reason` `edit_window_closed`: this is not a deletion, and Muster treats the Root message as past its window at
  once. A Root message that Muster posts again after it was deleted has a window of its own.
- **Alerts reach only the Thread.** Past the window, a change that keeps the status of the Alert Group — new Alerts,
  Alerts that resolve, the counters — no longer changes the Root message, which keeps the state of its last edit; the
  Thread replies that such a change makes are sent as usual.
- **A change of status posts a new Root message.** When the status changes past the window — Acknowledge, Resolve,
  Snooze, a Reopen — Muster posts a new Root message with the current state, Quietly, to the same channel, and replies
  under the old one: "This message is no longer updated. The current one: {link}", with a link to the new message when
  the bridge returned one and to the Alert Group page otherwise. Later Thread replies go under the new Root message,
  which has a window of its own. This reply is sent once: when the bridge refuses it, the failure is recorded with the
  delivery event and the reply is not sent again.
- **A new Root message is not left behind.** When the answer to the post of a new Root message is lost, Muster posts
  it again with the same key, even if the status has changed back meanwhile, so that a message the bridge may have
  taken is never left with a stale status and live buttons: a bridge that took the first post answers with that
  message instead of posting a second one. When the Destination left the Route meanwhile, the post carries the final
  text; when the bridge answers with the earlier post, which shows an older state, Muster then gives that message the
  final edit.
- **The old message keeps working.** A press on the buttons of an older Root message, or a Text command in its
  Thread, acts on the Alert Group as on the current one.
- **The final edit is a Thread reply.** When the Destination leaves the Route or is deleted, each open Root message
  gets a final edit, "No longer updated here; current state in Muster: {link}"; past the window, Muster sends the same
  text as a Thread reply instead.
- **Storm summaries are never posted again.** Past its window, a Storm summary keeps the state of its last edit.
- **What the delivery shows.** `GET /api/v1/alert-groups/AG…/deliveries` shows `past_edit_window` as `true` for a
  Destination whose Root message is past its window, while the delivery stays `delivered`, or `pending` while a new
  Root message is due. Each new Root message posted past the window is the delivery event
  `republished_past_edit_window` in the Alert Group's Timeline, with the error of the reply under the old message when
  it failed, and the log line `bridge_republished_past_edit_window`, with the ids of the old and the new message.

## Test messages and previews

A **test message** checks how a Destination looks without touching any Alert Group:

```sh
curl -X POST https://muster.example.org/api/v1/destinations/DSK7M3QX9P2RTA/tests \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUSTER_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"source":{"kind":"example"}}'
```

It posts one message of the kind `test`, Quiet, marked "🧪 Test message" before its text, with the buttons of its
status, whose presses change nothing. It goes through the same limiters as delivery, and the result shows the step
`message` with the request — the token masked — the bridge's answer and its error class. Use
`{"source":{"kind":"alert_group","alert_group_id":"AG…"}}` to render a recent Alert Group of one of the
Destination's Routes instead of the example. `POST …/previews` with the same body returns, without posting anything,
the envelope the test would post, as JSON in the item `message`.

## Broken Destinations

A Bridge Destination becomes **Broken** when the bridge refuses it — it answers `forbidden`, for example because the
bot was removed from the channel — with the bridge's text as the reason, or when the bridge keeps failing or does not
answer for the whole Transient budget: 10 attempts within 30 minutes. A bridge that asks Muster to wait does not make
a Destination Broken unless it asks for more than 15 minutes (`bridge.retry_after_max`); an answer the bridge calls `invalid` ends that one
delivery as Not delivered and leaves the Destination healthy. When the bridge answers that a Root message is gone,
Muster publishes the Alert Group again, once; an edit refused as `gone` with the `reason` `edit_window_closed` is not a
deletion, but the end of the message's [edit window](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/bridge.md#edit-windows).

While a Destination is Broken, Muster tries again every 5 minutes: with the oldest waiting delivery, or, when nothing
waits, with the Destination check, which posts nothing. The first success ends the Broken state, and so does a
successful check or test message. See [MusterDestinationBroken](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDestinationBroken.md).
A Bridge Connection whose bridge cannot be reached does not become Broken itself: its Destinations do, and its
Connection check shows the cause.

## Account links

A press or a Mention through a bridge names a person through their Account link for that Connection; see
[Link your messenger accounts](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/account-links.md).

## Check from the command line

`muster doctor` prints one line per Bridge Connection, with the result of `getInfo`, and one line per Bridge
Destination, with the result of `checkChannel`, without posting anything.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md -->
# Write a bridge

A **bridge** connects Muster to a messenger that Muster does not support natively. This page is for the people who
write one. It starts with the bridge libraries, which do the protocol's part of a bridge, and then describes the
**Bridge protocol** step by step for a bridge written without a library. If you run a bridge that somebody else wrote,
read [Connect a messenger through a bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/bridge.md) instead.

## What a bridge is, and when to write one

Muster has native support for [Mattermost](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/mattermost.md), [Slack](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/slack.md) and [Telegram](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/telegram.md). For any other
messenger, Muster talks to a bridge: a small HTTP service that you write and run. Muster calls the bridge to post, edit
and reply to messages. The bridge calls the messenger. When people press a button or write in a Thread, the bridge
reports it back to Muster as an **event**.

Write a bridge when your team uses a messenger with a bot API that Muster does not support. A bridge does not need to
live in Muster's repository, and it may stay closed: the protocol is MIT licensed (see [Licence](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#licence)).

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph muster["Muster"]
    calls["Delivery worker and interactive path"]
    poller["Poller"]
    callback["Push callback on the ingest listener"]
    handler["Commands and Account links"]
    health["Destination health"]
  end
  subgraph bridge["Your bridge"]
    api["Bridge protocol: the /v1/ operations"]
    queue["Event queue"]
  end
  messenger["Your messenger"]

  calls -- "getInfo, postMessage, editMessage, replyInThread, checkChannel, answerEvent, findUsers, sendDirectMessage" --> api
  api -- "calls the messenger's own API" --> messenger
  messenger -- "presses, Thread messages, direct messages, deletions" --> queue
  poller -- "poll mode: pollEvents" --> queue
  queue -. "push mode: bridgeEvent, signed" .-> callback
  poller --> handler
  callback --> handler
  api -. "answers and error classes" .-> health
  health -- "Broken, every 5 minutes: the oldest waiting delivery, or checkChannel when nothing waits" --> api
```

Muster is always the caller of the `/v1/` operations, and the bridge is always the caller of the messenger. Events
travel the other way, in one of two modes that the Admin chooses on the Bridge Connection: Muster **polls** the bridge
with `pollEvents`, or the bridge **pushes** each event, signed, to Muster's callback address. The bridge answers every
call with a result or an error class, and Muster turns those into the health of the Destination: a Destination whose
bridge keeps failing, or refuses the channel, becomes Broken until a check succeeds (see
[Run your bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#run-your-bridge)).

Terms follow Muster's glossary: a **Root message** is the one editable message that shows an Alert Group in a channel
of the messenger, its **Thread** holds the replies under it, and a **Mention** is a deliberate @-reference. A **Bridge
Connection** in Muster is one bot of your messenger behind one bridge: one token is one bot.

## Start with a library

Most bridge authors should not write the protocol again. A bridge library does the protocol's part of a bridge, and
you write only the calls to your messenger.

### What a library does, and what is left to you

A library:

- serves every operation of the protocol under `/v1/`;
- checks the token of each bot in constant time, and keeps the events and idempotency keys of each bot apart;
- validates every request against `api/bridge.yaml` and every answer before it is sent, and enforces the bridge's
  limits;
- keeps each `Idempotency-Key` with its result and answers a repeated key with that result and `replayed: true`;
- builds the answer to `getInfo` from the features and limits you give it;
- answers failures as problems with an error class, and never logs a token or a push secret;
- queues events for `pollEvents`, and pushes them with Standard Webhooks signatures and retries;
- turns a direct message that carries an Account link token into an `account_link` event.

You write:

- the calls to your messenger: post, edit, reply in a Thread, check a channel and show an answer to a person, and,
  where the messenger offers them, finding a person, sending a direct message and deleting a message;
- the mapping of the messenger's failures to the five error classes (see [Error classes](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#error-classes));
- the reports of what people do: a press, a message in a Thread, a deleted message and a direct message;
- the rendering of the envelope in the messenger's markup (see [Rendering the envelope](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#rendering-the-envelope)).

The Go library, `muster-bridge-go`, follows the protocol's major version and is released from its own repository,
under the MIT licence and without a CLA. The same holds for every bridge library of the project.

### The Go library

The Go module is `github.com/muster-io/muster-bridge-go`, and its package is `bridge`.

```sh
go get github.com/muster-io/muster-bridge-go
```

The libraries are released when Muster's first release is. The module is at `0.x` until then, and `go get` without a
version takes the latest commit of its `master` branch. From the first release, `1.x` speaks protocol version 1, and
each release is a tag `vX.Y.Z`.

**1. Implement `bridge.Messenger`.** It has five methods, each given the name of the bot whose token Muster sent:
`PostMessage`, `EditMessage`, `ReplyInThread`, `CheckChannel` and `AnswerEvent`. The sketch below is for Parley, a
fictional messenger; its client `parleyClient` stands for whatever library your messenger has.

```go
// parleyMessenger is the bridge's calls to the fictional messenger Parley.
type parleyMessenger struct{ api *parleyClient }

// mention is how Parley writes a mention of a person.
func mention(p bridge.Mention) string { return "<@" + p.ExternalId + ">" }

func (m *parleyMessenger) PostMessage(ctx context.Context, bot string, in bridge.MessageInput) (
	bridge.MessagePosted, error) {
	body := bridge.ReplaceMentions(in.Body, in.Mentions, mention)
	id, err := m.api.Send(ctx, in.ChannelId, render(in.Title, body))
	if err != nil {
		return bridge.MessagePosted{}, classify(err)
	}
	return bridge.MessagePosted{MessageId: id}, nil
}

func (m *parleyMessenger) EditMessage(ctx context.Context, bot, messageID string, in bridge.MessageContent) (
	bridge.MessageEdited, error) {
	if err := m.api.Edit(ctx, messageID, render(in.Title, in.Body)); err != nil {
		return bridge.MessageEdited{}, classify(err)
	}
	return bridge.MessageEdited{}, nil
}

func (m *parleyMessenger) ReplyInThread(ctx context.Context, bot, messageID string, in bridge.ThreadReplyInput) (
	bridge.ThreadReplyPosted, error) {
	var thread string
	if in.ThreadRef != nil {
		thread = *in.ThreadRef
	}
	body := bridge.ReplaceMentions(in.Body, in.Mentions, mention)
	id, thread, err := m.api.Reply(ctx, messageID, thread, body)
	if err != nil {
		return bridge.ThreadReplyPosted{}, classify(err)
	}
	return bridge.ThreadReplyPosted{MessageId: id, ThreadRef: thread}, nil
}

func (m *parleyMessenger) CheckChannel(ctx context.Context, bot, channelID string) (string, error) {
	name, err := m.api.ChannelName(ctx, channelID)
	if err != nil {
		return "", classify(err)
	}
	return name, nil
}

// AnswerEvent answers an Account link in its direct chat, a Thread message in its Thread, and a press privately.
func (m *parleyMessenger) AnswerEvent(ctx context.Context, bot string, ev bridge.ReportedEvent, text string) (
	bridge.AnswerShownShownAs, error) {
	switch ev.Type {
	case bridge.EventTypeAccountLink:
		if err := m.api.SendDirect(ctx, ev.Chat, text); err != nil {
			return "", classify(err)
		}
		return bridge.AnswerShownShownAsDirect, nil
	case bridge.EventTypeThreadMessage:
		if _, _, err := m.api.Reply(ctx, ev.MessageID, ev.ThreadRef, text); err != nil {
			return "", classify(err)
		}
		return bridge.AnswerShownShownAsThread, nil
	default:
		if err := m.api.Whisper(ctx, ev.Chat, text); err != nil {
			return "", classify(err)
		}
		return bridge.AnswerShownShownAsEphemeral, nil
	}
}
```

For the features you declare, also implement `UserFinder` (when `UserLookup` is not `none`), `DirectMessenger` (when
the bridge offers direct messages) and `Deleter` (when it offers deletion). `bridge.New` refuses a configuration whose
features lack their interface, or whose `info` would not match the protocol, and names the reason.

**2. Answer failures with error classes.** A method returns `bridge.TransientError`, `bridge.RateLimitedError`,
`bridge.GoneError` (with `bridge.ReasonEditWindowClosed` for an edit that the messenger refuses only for the message's
age), `bridge.ForbiddenError` or `bridge.InvalidError`. Any other error, and a panic, is answered as `transient`.

```go
// classify tells Muster what a failure of Parley means. Only the bridge knows.
func classify(err error) error {
	var pe *parleyError
	if !errors.As(err, &pe) {
		return bridge.TransientError("Parley did not answer.")
	}
	switch pe.Code {
	case "slow_down":
		return bridge.RateLimitedError(time.Duration(pe.RetryIn)*time.Second, bridge.ProblemScopeChannel,
			"Parley asks to slow down.")
	case "message_not_found", "thread_removed":
		return bridge.GoneError("The message no longer exists.")
	case "edit_too_old":
		return bridge.GoneError("The message can no longer be edited.", bridge.ReasonEditWindowClosed)
	case "channel_not_found", "not_a_member", "bot_banned", "no_permission":
		return bridge.ForbiddenError("The bot is not a member of this channel.")
	case "user_blocked_bot":
		return bridge.ForbiddenError("This person cannot receive a message from the bot.")
	case "text_too_long", "bad_request":
		return bridge.InvalidError("Parley refused the request.")
	default:
		return bridge.TransientError("Parley is not available.")
	}
}
```

**3. Create the bridge with `bridge.New`.** Give it the bot's token in `Config.Bots`, the features in
`Config.Capabilities` and the limits in `Config.Limits`, and mount `b.Handler()` behind an HTTP server. The code below
is the body of a function that returns an `error`.

```go
token, err := os.ReadFile("/run/secrets/muster-token")
if err != nil {
	return err
}
messenger := &parleyMessenger{api: &parleyClient{}}

b, err := bridge.New(bridge.Config{
	Name:          "parley-bridge",
	Version:       "0.1.0",
	MessengerName: "Parley",
	Bots:          []bridge.Bot{{Name: "main", Token: strings.TrimSpace(string(token))}},
	Limits:        bridge.Limits{MaxBodyLength: 4000},
	Capabilities: bridge.Capabilities{
		Buttons: &bridge.Capabilities_Buttons{MaxPerMessage: 5, MaxPerRow: 5, DataMaxBytes: 64,
			Styles: []bridge.ButtonStyle{bridge.ButtonStylePrimary, bridge.ButtonStyleSuccess,
				bridge.ButtonStyleNeutral, bridge.ButtonStyleDanger}},
		ThreadMessages: new(bridge.CapabilitiesThreadMessagesAll),
		PrivateAnswers: &[]bridge.CapabilitiesPrivateAnswers{bridge.CapabilitiesPrivateAnswersEphemeral},
	},
	UserLookup: bridge.InfoUserLookupNone,
}, messenger)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
defer b.Close(context.Background())

srv := &http.Server{
	Addr:              "127.0.0.1:8095",
	Handler:           b.Handler(),
	ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
	// No WriteTimeout: pollEvents holds a request open for up to 60 seconds.
}
return srv.ListenAndServe()
```

`MaxBodyLength` is the longest `body` that your bridge always accepts, after its own rendering; the protocol's smallest
value is 500, and the library takes at most 100000. `Capabilities` lists the optional features: a nil member is a
feature the bridge does not offer, and Muster never calls an operation that the bridge did not declare. To serve the
handler under a path prefix, mount it with `http.StripPrefix`.

!!! warning "No WriteTimeout"
    `pollEvents` holds a request open for up to 60 seconds. Serve the handler with no `WriteTimeout`, or one above 75
    seconds. A shorter one cuts a poll off without an answer, and its events reach Muster late.
    `ReadHeaderTimeout` and `IdleTimeout` are safe to set.

**4. Report what happens in the messenger.** When a person presses a button, writes in a Thread, deletes a message of
the bot or writes to the bot, call `b.Press`, `b.ThreadMessage`, `b.MessageDeleted` or `b.DirectMessage`. Each returns
at once, so confirm a press to your messenger within its deadline whatever Muster does. Give the messenger's own id of
the update as `UpdateID`: an update that the messenger delivers twice is then queued once.

```go
// onPress is called when a person presses a button in Parley. chat is what AnswerEvent needs to whisper to
// the person; the library keeps it with the event and never sends it to Muster.
func onPress(ctx context.Context, b *bridge.Bridge, updateID, messageID, data, chat string, who bridge.Person) error {
	// ... confirm the press to Parley first, then report it. Press returns at once.
	return b.Press(ctx, "main", bridge.Press{
		UpdateID: updateID, MessageID: messageID, User: who, Data: data, Chat: chat,
	})
}
```

`Chat` comes back as `ReportedEvent.Chat` when Muster answers the event; `b.ThreadMessage` and `b.DirectMessage` take
one too.

A direct message whose whole text is an Account link token becomes an `account_link` event; any other direct message is
ignored.

**5. Turn Mention markers into mentions.** `bridge.ReplaceMentions(body, mentions, render)` replaces each marker
`[@Name](muster-mention:ref)` by what `render` returns for its entry in `mentions`, as the sketch above does. For a
bridge without `NativeMentions`, pass a nil `render` and the markers become plain names.

**6. Push, if you want it.** Give a bot a `bridge.PushTarget` with the callback address that its Bridge Connection
shows and the push secret you entered on it, in `Config.Bots` or later with `b.SetPush`. `b.Close` stops the pushers.

**7. Use a `Store` that survives restarts.** `bridge.NewMemoryStore`, the default, keeps the idempotency keys and the
queued events in memory. A restart forgets them: a retried request that Muster sends after the restart then posts a
second message, and events that Muster has not collected are lost. Implement `bridge.Store` over your database and
set `Config.Store`. Long polls and pushers are woken in the process that queued an event, so with several processes
over one store, run each bot in one process only.

**8. Check it.** Run `muster bridge check` against your bridge (see [Test your bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#test-your-bridge)).

The library's repository has a complete bridge in one file, `examples/minimal`: its messenger lives in memory and
writes every message the bot posts to the log. From a clone of the repository, with Go 1.26 or newer, run it with a
token, the one a Bridge Connection in Muster would hold:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/muster-io/muster-bridge-go && cd muster-bridge-go
printf example-token > /tmp/bt
go run ./examples/minimal -token-file /tmp/bt
```

It listens on `127.0.0.1:18095`, knows the channels `alerts` and `ops` and the people `alice` and `bob`, and offers
every feature of the protocol. In another terminal:

```sh
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 127.0.0.1:18095/v1/info          # 401: no token
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer example-token' 127.0.0.1:18095/v1/info \
  | jq -c '{protocol_version, user_lookup}'                                 # {"protocol_version":"1","user_lookup":"login"}
```

Then run `muster bridge check` against it, here from Muster's development image, which reaches the host's loopback
with `--network host` on Linux only:

```sh
docker run --rm --network host -v /tmp/bt:/token:ro ghcr.io/muster-io/muster:edge bridge check \
  http://127.0.0.1:18095 --token-file /token --channel alerts --forbidden-channel nobot --handle alice \
  --no-interactive
```

```text
PASS info
PASS channel_check
PASS post
PASS replayed_key
PASS buttons
PASS edit
PASS thread_reply
PASS thread_ref
PASS forbidden_channel
PASS user_lookup
PASS direct_message
PASS delete
PASS poll
SKIP press: --no-interactive
SKIP push: --no-interactive
PASS answer
```

The package documentation on pkg.go.dev describes what the library does for every operation.

### The Python library

The Python library is `muster-bridge` on PyPI, and its import package is `muster_bridge`. It needs Python 3.11 or
newer and depends only on Starlette, httpx and pydantic 2. Like the Go library, it is released from its own repository,
`muster-bridge-python`, under the MIT licence and without a CLA.

```sh
pip install muster-bridge
```

The libraries are released when Muster's first release is. Until then the package is not on PyPI, so
`pip install muster-bridge` finds nothing: install it from a clone of its repository with `pip install .`. Its version
is `0.x` until Muster's first release; from then, `1.x` speaks protocol version 1.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/muster-io/muster-bridge-python && cd muster-bridge-python
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install .
```

The library serves the protocol as an ASGI application, `BridgeApp`, and calls your code with `async` methods on the
event loop that serves the bridge. Call your messenger with an asynchronous client, or move a blocking call off the
loop with `asyncio.to_thread`.

**1. Implement `Messenger`.** It is a protocol of five coroutines, each given the name of the bot whose token Muster
sent: `post_message`, `edit_message`, `reply_in_thread`, `check_channel` and `answer_event`. Define them with
`async def`. The sketch below is for Parley, the same fictional messenger; its asynchronous client `ParleyClient`
stands for whatever library your messenger has.

```python
from muster_bridge import (
    AnswerShownShownAs,
    Mention,
    MessageContent,
    MessageEdited,
    MessageInput,
    MessagePosted,
    ReportedEvent,
    ThreadReplyInput,
    ThreadReplyPosted,
    replace_mentions,
)


def mention(m: Mention) -> str:
    """Write a mention of a person as Parley does."""
    return f"<@{m.external_id}>"


class ParleyMessenger:
    """The bridge's calls to the fictional messenger Parley."""

    def __init__(self, api: ParleyClient) -> None:
        self.api = api

    async def post_message(self, bot: str, message: MessageInput) -> MessagePosted:
        body = replace_mentions(message.body, message.mentions, mention)
        try:
            message_id = await self.api.send(message.channel_id, render(message.title, body))
        except ParleyError as error:
            raise classify(error) from error
        return MessagePosted(message_id=message_id)

    async def edit_message(self, bot: str, message_id: str, content: MessageContent) -> MessageEdited:
        try:
            await self.api.edit(message_id, render(content.title, content.body))
        except ParleyError as error:
            raise classify(error) from error
        return MessageEdited()

    async def reply_in_thread(self, bot: str, message_id: str, reply: ThreadReplyInput) -> ThreadReplyPosted:
        body = replace_mentions(reply.body, reply.mentions, mention)
        try:
            reply_id, thread = await self.api.reply(message_id, reply.thread_ref, body)
        except ParleyError as error:
            raise classify(error) from error
        return ThreadReplyPosted(message_id=reply_id, thread_ref=thread)

    async def check_channel(self, bot: str, channel_id: str) -> str:
        try:
            return await self.api.channel_name(channel_id)
        except ParleyError as error:
            raise classify(error) from error

    async def answer_event(self, bot: str, event: ReportedEvent, text: str) -> AnswerShownShownAs:
        """Answer an Account link in its direct chat, a Thread message in its Thread, and a press privately."""
        try:
            if event.type == "account_link":
                await self.api.send_direct(event.chat, text)
                return AnswerShownShownAs.direct
            if event.type == "thread_message":
                await self.api.reply(event.message_id, event.thread_ref, text)
                return AnswerShownShownAs.thread
            await self.api.whisper(event.chat, text)
            return AnswerShownShownAs.ephemeral
        except ParleyError as error:
            raise classify(error) from error
```

For the features you declare, also implement `UserFinder` (`find_user`, when `user_lookup` is not `none`),
`DirectMessenger` (`send_direct_message`, when the bridge offers direct messages) and `Deleter` (`delete_message`, when
it offers deletion). `BridgeApp` raises `ConfigError` for a configuration whose features lack their methods, or whose
`info` would not match the protocol, and names every reason.

**2. Answer failures with error classes.** A method raises `Transient`, `RateLimited` (with the wait `retry_after` in
seconds, and `scope` `"channel"` or `"bot"`), `Gone` (with `edit_window_closed=True` for an edit that the messenger
refuses only for the message's age), `Forbidden` or `Invalid`. Each takes a `detail` that Muster shows the Admin, so
keep secrets out of it. Any other exception is answered as `transient`, with a generic detail that carries none of its
text.

```python
from muster_bridge import BridgeError, Forbidden, Gone, Invalid, RateLimited, Transient


def classify(error: ParleyError) -> BridgeError:
    """Tell Muster what a failure of Parley means. Only the bridge knows."""
    match error.code:
        case "slow_down":
            return RateLimited("Parley asks to slow down.", retry_after=error.retry_in, scope="channel")
        case "message_not_found" | "thread_removed":
            return Gone("The message no longer exists.")
        case "edit_too_old":
            return Gone("The message can no longer be edited.", edit_window_closed=True)
        case "channel_not_found" | "not_a_member" | "bot_banned" | "no_permission":
            return Forbidden("The bot is not a member of this channel.")
        case "user_blocked_bot":
            return Forbidden("This person cannot receive a message from the bot.")
        case "text_too_long" | "bad_request":
            return Invalid("Parley refused the request.")
        case _:
            return Transient("Parley is not available.")
```

**3. Create the bridge with `BridgeApp`.** Give its `Config` the bot's token in `bots`, the features in
`capabilities` and the limits in `limits`, and serve the `BridgeApp` with uvicorn or another ASGI server.

```python
from pathlib import Path

import uvicorn

from muster_bridge import (
    Bot,
    BridgeApp,
    ButtonStyle,
    Capabilities,
    CapabilitiesButtons,
    CapabilitiesPrivateAnswer,
    CapabilitiesThreadMessages,
    Config,
    Limits,
)

token = Path("/run/secrets/muster-token").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()

config = Config(
    name="parley-bridge",
    version="0.1.0",
    messenger_name="Parley",
    bots=[Bot(name="main", token=token)],
    limits=Limits(max_body_length=4000, edit_max_age_seconds=None),
    capabilities=Capabilities(
        buttons=CapabilitiesButtons(
            max_per_message=5,
            max_per_row=5,
            data_max_bytes=64,
            styles=[ButtonStyle.primary, ButtonStyle.success, ButtonStyle.neutral, ButtonStyle.danger],
        ),
        thread_messages=CapabilitiesThreadMessages.all,
        private_answers=[CapabilitiesPrivateAnswer.ephemeral],
    ),
    user_lookup="none",
)
bridge = BridgeApp(config, ParleyMessenger(ParleyClient()))

uvicorn.run(bridge, host="127.0.0.1", port=8095)
```

`max_body_length` is the longest `body` that your bridge always accepts, after its own rendering; the protocol's
smallest value is 500, and the library takes at most 100000. `Limits` also needs `edit_max_age_seconds`, how long the
bot can edit a message after posting it, or `None` when edits never expire. A member of `Capabilities` left `None` is
a feature the bridge does not offer, and Muster never calls an operation that the bridge did not declare.

To serve the bridge under a path of a Starlette or FastAPI application, mount it there and pass its `lifespan` to the
application. The base URL of the Bridge Connection then ends with that path.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI(lifespan=bridge.lifespan)
app.mount("/bridge", bridge)
```

Starlette runs the lifespan of the top-level application only, and the bridge's lifespan starts and stops its pushers.
An application with a lifespan of its own enters the bridge's in it, with `async with bridge.lifespan(app):`. A
`BridgeApp` has one lifespan, and its end stops the pushers for good: a program or a test that starts the application
again makes a new `BridgeApp`.

!!! warning "A read timeout above 75 seconds"
    `pollEvents` holds a request open for up to 60 seconds. uvicorn sets no timeout that cuts such a request short, but
    a proxy in front of the bridge needs a read timeout above 75 seconds. A shorter one cuts a poll off without an
    answer, and its events reach Muster late.

**4. Report what happens in the messenger.** When a person presses a button, writes in a Thread, deletes a message of
the bot or writes to the bot, await `bridge.press(...)`, `bridge.thread_message(...)`, `bridge.message_deleted(...)`
or `bridge.direct_message(...)`, all four coroutines, in the event loop that serves the bridge. Each queues
the event and returns at once, so confirm a press to your messenger within its deadline whatever Muster does. Give the
messenger's own id of the update as `update_id`: an update that the messenger delivers twice is then queued once.

```python
from muster_bridge import BridgeApp, Person


async def on_press(bridge: BridgeApp, update_id: str, message_id: str, data: str, chat: str, who: Person) -> None:
    """Report a press in Parley.

    chat is what answer_event needs to whisper to the person; the library keeps it with the event and never sends it
    to Muster.
    """
    # ... confirm the press to Parley first, then report it. press returns at once.
    await bridge.press("main", message_id=message_id, user=who, data=data, update_id=update_id, chat=chat)
```

`chat` comes back as `ReportedEvent.chat` when Muster answers the event; `thread_message` and `direct_message` take
one too. `Person` and the other models validate when they are built, so cut a display name to 200 characters before you
build the `Person` of a report. A report raises `UnknownBotError` for a bot that the `Config` lacks, `NotOfferedError`
for a feature that the bridge does not offer, and `InvalidEventError` for an event that would not match the protocol.
From another thread, hand the coroutine to the event loop with `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`.

A direct message whose whole text is an Account link token becomes an `account_link` event; any other direct message is
ignored.

**5. Turn Mention markers into mentions.** `replace_mentions(body, mentions, render)` replaces each marker
`[@Name](muster-mention:ref)` by what `render` returns for its entry in `mentions`, as the sketch above does. For a
bridge without `native_mentions`, pass `None` as `render` and the markers become plain names.

**6. Push, if you want it.** Give a bot a `PushTarget` with the callback address that its Bridge Connection shows and
the push secret you entered on it, in `Bot(push=...)` or later with `bridge.set_push(bot, target)`, from the thread of
the event loop that serves the bridge. The end of the bridge's lifespan, or `await bridge.aclose()`, stops the
pushers; the events stay queued for polling.

**7. Use a `Store` that survives restarts.** `MemoryStore`, the default, keeps the idempotency keys and the queued
events in memory. A restart forgets them: a retried request that Muster sends after the restart then posts a second
message, and events that Muster has not collected are lost. Implement the protocol `Store` over your database and pass
it as `Config(store=...)`. Long polls and pushes are woken in the process that queued an event, so with several
processes over one store, run each bot in one process only.

**8. Check it.** Run `muster bridge check` against your bridge (see [Test your bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#test-your-bridge)).

The library's repository has a complete bridge in one file, `examples/memory_bridge.py`: its messenger lives in memory
and writes every message the bot posts to the log. In the clone, with the library installed as above, install uvicorn
beside it and run the example with a token, the one a Bridge Connection in Muster would hold:

```sh
pip install uvicorn
printf example-token > /tmp/bt
python examples/memory_bridge.py --token-file /tmp/bt
```

Like the Go library's example, it listens on `127.0.0.1:18095`, knows the channels `alerts` and `ops` and the people
`alice` and `bob`, and offers every feature of the protocol, or only those that `BRIDGE_FEATURES` lists. The `curl`
calls and the `muster bridge check` command of [the Go library](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#the-go-library) give the same answers against it.
Outside the protocol, the example serves `POST /demo/press`, which presses the first button of a message as a person,
so that a script can play the person of an interactive check. It has no authentication of its own: keep it on
loopback.

The library's README and the docstrings of the package describe what the library does for every operation.

### The example bridge

The **example bridge** is built on the Go library and lives in its repository, in `examples/chat`. It is a small chat
that runs in memory, with a web page: channels, Threads, buttons, direct chats between a person and the bot, and users
found by login. It offers every feature of the protocol, one by one switchable, and both event delivery modes. Use it
to try Muster without a real messenger, and as a reference for your own bridge.

Its image is `ghcr.io/muster-io/muster-example-bridge`. Until the libraries' first release, use the tag `edge`, which
follows the `master` branch of the library's repository; releases will be tagged `vX.Y.Z`.

```sh
docker run --rm -p 8095:8095 -e BRIDGE_TOKEN=example-token ghcr.io/muster-io/muster-example-bridge:edge
```

The page is then at `http://127.0.0.1:8095/`, and the protocol under `/v1/` on the same port. `BRIDGE_FEATURES` limits
the features the example offers, comma-separated: with `BRIDGE_FEATURES=thread_messages`, for one, it shows no buttons,
and people answer with Text commands in Threads.

!!! warning "The page has no authentication"
    The protocol under `/v1/` needs the token, but the example's page and its JSON API under `/chat/api/` have no
    authentication of their own: whoever reaches them reads every message and acts as any person. Keep the example on
    your machine's loopback, or put it behind an authenticating proxy.

**Next to `muster dev`:**

1. Start `muster dev` from a Muster checkout (`make dev`) and sign in.
2. Start the example on the host's loopback at `127.0.0.1:18095`. From a checkout of the library, `go run
   ./examples/chat -token-file <file>` listens there by default. With the image on Linux, use `--network host`, mount
   the token file, and give `-listen 127.0.0.1:18095 -token-file /token`, because the image listens on `:8095`
   otherwise. The image runs as the user 65532, so the mounted file must be readable by that user, for example with
   mode 0644. `muster dev` lets Muster call loopback addresses; elsewhere the Organization's outbound address policy
   blocks them, and you allow the example's address there.
3. Create a Bridge Connection with the base URL `http://127.0.0.1:18095`, the token you gave the example and the
   event delivery **Polling**. **Check connection** shows "Messenger: Example chat" and the features the example
   offers.
4. Create a Destination on that Connection for the channel `alerts`. **Send test message** makes the message
   "🧪 Test message" appear in `#alerts` on the page.
5. Alert Groups that a Route sends to the Destination appear in `#alerts`, one Root message each. A press acts for the
   Muster User whose account is linked to the person who pressed, so link an account first: copy the token from your
   profile, pick the person under "You are", open their direct chat with the bot under "Direct", and send the token.

**Next to the Quick start:** run the example as one more service of the compose project, so that Muster reaches it by
name and nothing on the host's loopback is involved.

1. In the directory of the [Quick start](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/quick-start.md), where `docker-compose.yml` and `.env` are, add a token to
   `.env` and write a file `compose.override.yaml` next to them, which Docker Compose merges into the project by itself.
   `docker compose up -d --wait` then starts the example, and leaves Muster running if it already runs:

    ```sh
    echo "EXAMPLE_BRIDGE_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 16)" >> .env
    cat >compose.override.yaml <<'EOF'
    services:
      example-bridge:
        image: ghcr.io/muster-io/muster-example-bridge:edge
        environment:
          BRIDGE_TOKEN: ${EXAMPLE_BRIDGE_TOKEN}
        ports:
          - "127.0.0.1:8095:8095"
        restart: unless-stopped
    EOF
    docker compose up -d --wait
    ```

    The example's page is published on the loopback of the host only, at `http://127.0.0.1:8095/`, because it has no
    authentication (see the warning above). On a VM, reach it with an SSH tunnel, `ssh -L 8095:localhost:8095 <vm>`.
    The whole port is published, so `/v1/` is reachable on the host's loopback too, and it needs the token. Muster
    reaches
    the example inside the compose network.
2. Create a Bridge Connection with the base URL `http://example-bridge:8095`, the token from `.env`
   (`grep EXAMPLE_BRIDGE_TOKEN .env`) and the event delivery **Polling**. The Organization's outbound address policy
   is **Standard**, which allows the private address that the name resolves to; only loopback is blocked.
3. Then do the check of step 3 above, which shows "Messenger: Example chat", and steps 4 and 5: a Destination for the
   channel `alerts`, and an account link to press buttons. Do not create the loopback Connection of step 3.

To remove the example and keep Muster and its data, run `docker compose rm -sf example-bridge` and delete
`compose.override.yaml`. Do not run `docker compose down -v` for this: it deletes Muster's database too.

For **Push**, choose a push secret (see [Push](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#push)), enter it in the Connection, and restart the example with
`BRIDGE_PUSH_URL` set to the callback address that the Connection shows, and the secret in `BRIDGE_PUSH_SECRET` or in
the file of `-push-secret-file`. With the compose service, set `BRIDGE_PUSH_URL` in the override's `environment` to the
callback address with the service name of Muster, `http://muster:8080/api/v1/callbacks/bridge/<id>`, not `localhost`:
the example reaches Muster inside the compose network.

## The protocol without a library

This part describes the protocol in the order a bridge author implements it. The full definition is the
[Bridge protocol reference](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/bridge/spec/index.html), rendered from `api/bridge.yaml`; the page
[Bridge protocol](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/bridge-protocol.md) in the Reference gives its version and the specification itself.
Every request and answer below follows that specification. The values in the examples are examples only.

**Conventions.**

- Every path is under `/v1/`. `GET /v1/info` returns `protocol_version` `"1"`. A bridge ignores request fields it does
  not know, and Muster ignores fields of `info` it does not know. A change that breaks existing bridges gets a new major
  path.
- Muster sends the Connection's token on every request as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The bridge answers `401` to
  a missing or wrong token. Muster sends the token only to the base URL saved on the Connection, and follows no
  redirects.
- The Bridge Connection's base URL may have a path prefix. Muster sends every request to `<base URL>/v1/…`.
- `message_id` and `channel_id` are opaque strings of up to 512 characters. Muster percent-encodes each as one path
  segment, and the bridge decodes it.
- Request bodies are JSON, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Errors are `application/problem+json`.
- One token is one bot. A bridge that serves several Connections tells them apart by the token.

**What every bridge implements:** `getInfo`, `postMessage`, `editMessage`, `replyInThread`, `checkChannel`,
`answerEvent`, and events by `pollEvents`, by the `bridgeEvent` push, or by both. A bridge sends at least
`account_link` events, because every bridge takes Account link tokens. Everything else is optional and declared in the
`capabilities` of `info`.

### `getInfo`

Muster calls it on every Connection check, and again before a call that depends on it when its copy is older than 10
minutes. A bridge whose features change is therefore picked up without a restart of Muster.

```http
GET /v1/info HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

```json
{
  "protocol_version": "1",
  "bridge": { "name": "parley-bridge", "version": "0.1.0" },
  "messenger": { "name": "Parley" },
  "capabilities": {
    "buttons": { "max_per_message": 5, "max_per_row": 5, "data_max_bytes": 64,
                 "styles": ["primary", "success", "neutral", "danger"] },
    "thread_messages": "all",
    "direct_messages": { "bot_can_start": true },
    "private_answers": ["ephemeral"],
    "native_mentions": true,
    "quiet_messages": true,
    "status_color": true
  },
  "limits": { "max_body_length": 4000, "edit_max_age_seconds": null },
  "user_lookup": "login",
  "event_delivery": ["poll", "push"],
  "link_url_template": "https://chat.example.org/bots/muster?start={token}"
}
```

- `messenger.name` is shown on the Connection and the Destinations.
- `limits.max_body_length` is the longest `body` you always accept, in code points, at least 500.
  `limits.edit_max_age_seconds` is how long after posting the bot can still edit a message, at least 300, or `null`
  when edits never expire.
- `user_lookup` is what a person enters to be found for an Account link by code: `email`, `login`, `username`,
  `user_id` or `none`.
- `event_delivery` lists the modes you offer, `poll`, `push` or both. Each Connection chooses one.
- `link_url_template` is an `http` or `https` link that opens a chat with the bot and hands it the Account link token,
  with `{token}` where the token goes. Use `null` or leave it out when your messenger has no such link.

The answer must match the protocol and be smaller than 64 KiB, or the Connection check fails.

### `checkChannel`

The Destination check. It must **not** post anything. Answer `200` only when the bot can post, edit its own messages and
reply in Threads in the channel. Muster runs it when a Destination is saved, when a person presses **Check**, and every
few minutes while the Destination is Broken.

```http
POST /v1/channels/ch-alerts/check HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

```json
{ "channel_id": "ch-alerts", "name": "alerts" }
```

`name` is the channel's name as people see it. When the channel does not exist, or the bot cannot use it, answer
`forbidden` with a `detail` that a person can act on:

```json
{
  "title": "Forbidden",
  "status": 403,
  "detail": "The bot is not a member of this channel.",
  "class": "forbidden"
}
```

### `postMessage`

Posts a Root message, a Storm summary or a test message. The request carries an `Idempotency-Key`, and the answer
names the message for later edits and Thread replies.

```http
POST /v1/messages HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: <key>
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "channel_id": "ch-alerts",
  "kind": "root",
  "status": "firing",
  "color": "#d32f2f",
  "emoji": "🔴",
  "title": "#42 HighErrorRate",
  "link": {
    "url": "https://muster.example.org/alert-groups/AGK7M3QX9P2RTA",
    "label": "Open in Muster"
  },
  "body": "[@Alice Smith](muster-mention:m1)\n\nprod · started 14:03\n\n> **namespace** payments\n\n- `api-7f9c` error rate 12 %\n- `api-5d2a` error rate 9 %\n\n[Runbook](https://wiki.example.org/runbooks/high-error-rate)",
  "buttons": [
    { "label": "Ack", "style": "primary", "data": "a1.k2.QmFzZTY0U2lnbmF0dXJlRXhhbXBsZQ" },
    { "label": "Resolve", "style": "success", "data": "a2.k2.U2Vjb25kU2lnbmF0dXJlRXhhbXBsZQ" }
  ],
  "mentions": [
    { "ref": "m1", "external_id": "u-alice", "display_name": "Alice Smith" }
  ],
  "notify": true
}
```

```json
{
  "message_id": "m-77",
  "thread_ref": null,
  "url": "https://chat.example.org/c/alerts/m-77",
  "truncated": false,
  "replayed": false
}
```

- `kind` is `root`, `storm_summary` or `test`. `status` is `firing`, `acknowledged`, `snoozed`, `resolved` or `storm`.
- `message_id` is opaque to Muster: encode in it whatever you need to edit the message and reply under it.
- `thread_ref` may be returned when the messenger's Thread id is known at once; otherwise the first `replyInThread`
  returns it (see [`thread_ref`](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#thread_ref)).
- `url` is a link that opens the message in your messenger, if it has one. Muster shows it on the Alert Group page and
  links to it from the Thread of an older Root message.
- `truncated` is `true` when you shortened the body to fit your messenger (see
  [Rendering the envelope](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#rendering-the-envelope)).

### `editMessage`

Replaces the whole message with the envelope of its new state. An edit is always Quiet and never carries Mentions, so
its body has no `channel_id`, `kind`, `mentions` or `notify`. An empty `buttons` removes the buttons. Editing to the
state that the message already shows is a success.

```http
PATCH /v1/messages/m-77 HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "status": "acknowledged",
  "color": "#f57c00",
  "emoji": "🟠",
  "title": "#42 HighErrorRate",
  "link": {
    "url": "https://muster.example.org/alert-groups/AGK7M3QX9P2RTA",
    "label": "Open in Muster"
  },
  "body": "prod · started 14:03\n\n> **namespace** payments\n\n- `api-7f9c` error rate 12 %\n- `api-5d2a` error rate 9 %",
  "buttons": [
    { "label": "Unack", "style": "neutral", "data": "a3.k2.VGhpcmRTaWduYXR1cmVFeGFtcGxl" },
    { "label": "Resolve", "style": "success", "data": "a2.k2.U2Vjb25kU2lnbmF0dXJlRXhhbXBsZQ" }
  ]
}
```

```json
{ "truncated": false }
```

A message that no longer exists is `gone`. An edit that the messenger refuses because the message is older than it
allows is `gone` with the `reason` `edit_window_closed` (see [Edit windows](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#edit-windows)).

### `replyInThread`

Posts a reply in the Thread of a message, usually a Root message. Muster sends the last `thread_ref` it received for
that message, or `null` when it has none, and the bridge creates the Thread if its messenger needs that.

```http
POST /v1/messages/m-77/thread-replies HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: <key>
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "thread_ref": null,
  "body": "New alert: `api-1c3e` error rate 14 %",
  "buttons": [],
  "mentions": [],
  "notify": false
}
```

```json
{
  "message_id": "m-78",
  "thread_ref": "t-77",
  "truncated": false,
  "replayed": false
}
```

`message_id` of the answer is the reply; a press on its buttons names it. A Thread that no longer exists, or a message
that was deleted, is `gone`. A reply may carry buttons, such as "Still on it" on a Reminder, when the bridge declares
`buttons`.

### Events and `answerEvent`

The rest of the required protocol is the way a person's actions reach Muster, and the way Muster answers them:

- `pollEvents`, `GET /v1/events`, returns the events after a cursor, and the `bridgeEvent` push posts each event,
  signed, to Muster's callback address. A bridge offers either or both; the Admin chooses one per Connection. See
  [Events](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#events).
- `answerEvent`, `POST /v1/answers`, shows Muster's answer to the person behind an event. See
  [Presses within 3 seconds, and answers later](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#presses-within-3-seconds-and-answers-later).

### Optional: `deleteMessage`, `findUsers` and `sendDirectMessage`

- `DELETE /v1/messages/{message_id}` is offered when `capabilities.delete` is declared. Muster L1 never deletes
  messages; the operation is reserved so that a later version of Muster can remove its test messages without a new
  protocol version. A message that no longer exists is a success, `204`.
- `GET /v1/users?handle=alice` is offered when `user_lookup` is not `none`. Muster calls it when a person asks to link
  an account by a code. The answer lists the one account with that handle, or none; a handle you cannot search for is
  `invalid`.
- `POST /v1/direct-messages` is offered when `capabilities.direct_messages` is declared with `bot_can_start`. Muster
