  uses it to send the code of an Account link. An account that cannot receive a message from the bot is `forbidden`.

```http
GET /v1/users?handle=alice HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

```json
{ "items": [ { "external_id": "u-alice", "display_name": "Alice Smith", "handle": "alice" } ] }
```

```http
POST /v1/direct-messages HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: <key>
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "user_external_id": "u-alice",
  "body": "You requested a link to Muster. Do not share this code.\n\n**K7M3Q9XT**"
}
```

```json
{ "message_id": "dm-12", "replayed": false }
```

## Required and optional features

The `capabilities` of `info` declare the optional features. A missing member means the feature is not offered, and
Muster adapts:

`buttons`
:   Without it: Muster sends no buttons. When the bridge has `thread_messages`, a Root message that is not resolved ends
    with the commands line, such as "Reply in the Thread: ack · resolve · snooze 1h", and people write **Text
    commands** in the Thread. Without either, the link to Muster is the only way to act.

`thread_messages`
:   Without it: Muster receives no Text commands. `all` reports every message of a person in a Thread of a message of
    the bot, `mentions_only` only those that mention the bot (the commands line then says "mentioning the bot").

`direct_messages` with `bot_can_start`, and a `user_lookup` other than `none`
:   Without it: Account links work by token only: the person sends the token to the bot. With both, a person can also
    link by a code that the bot sends.

`private_answers`
:   Without it: Muster's answer to a press appears in the Thread of the message instead of privately. `ephemeral` is a
    message only the person sees, `popup` a short plain-text pop-up.

`native_mentions`
:   Without it: a Mention marker is rendered as the person's name in plain text, which notifies nobody.

`quiet_messages`
:   Without it: a Quiet message (`notify: false`) is posted as an ordinary message, without Mentions.

`status_color`
:   Without it: the bridge shows the `emoji` of the status instead of the `color`.

`deletion_events`
:   Without it: Muster learns that a Root message was deleted from `gone` on its next edit or Thread reply, instead of
    at once.

`delete`
:   Without it: Muster L1 never deletes messages, so nothing changes.

`link_url_template`
:   Without it: the profile shows the Account link token without a link that opens the bot.

`edit_max_age_seconds`
:   Without it: a value of `null` means Muster edits a Root message for as long as its Alert Group changes.

A bridge sends `press` events only with `buttons`, `thread_message` events only with `thread_messages`, and
`message_deleted` events only with `deletion_events`. Muster handles every event type whatever its copy of `info`
says, so an event sent just after a feature was switched on is not lost.

## Rendering the envelope

Muster sends a JSON envelope: the `status`, `color` and `emoji`, the `title`, the `link`, the `body` and the `buttons`.
**The bridge renders it in its messenger's markup.** Muster never writes a messenger's markup for a bridge.

**The body is CommonMark 0.31 with one extension, strikethrough** (`~~text~~`) as GitHub Flavored Markdown writes it.

- Muster uses paragraphs, hard line breaks, emphasis, strong emphasis, strikethrough, code spans, links, bullet lists
  and block quotes.
- Muster never uses headings, tables, images or raw HTML.

Use a CommonMark parser rather than patterns, and map each construct to the closest thing your messenger has. The
`title` is plain text. Show it as the heading of the message, linked to `link`. Alert data in the body is already
escaped for CommonMark, and it cannot mention anyone or form a link.

**Links** are `http` and `https` links, plus Mention markers.

**Mention markers** are links of the form `[@Display Name](muster-mention:<ref>)`, where `ref` names an entry of
`mentions`. A bridge with `native_mentions` renders the marker as its messenger's mention of the entry's `external_id`,
which notifies that person. Any other bridge renders the link text alone, as plain text. The Mentions of a Loud message
form the first line of its body. The `external_id` is the account's id in the messenger as the bridge reported it when
the account was linked.

**Colours and emoji.** `color` is `#rrggbb` in lower case, for messengers that colour messages. `emoji` is the status
as an emoji, for messengers that do not: 🔴 firing, 🟠 acknowledged, ⚪ snoozed, 🟢 resolved, ⛈ storm.

**Loud and Quiet.** `notify: true` is a **Loud** message: it should notify people as the messenger's new messages do,
and it carries the `mentions` of the envelope. `notify: false` is **Quiet**: with `quiet_messages` declared, send it
without a notification. Edits are always Quiet. Do not make an edit ring anyone.

**Buttons.** Each button has a `label` (up to 64 characters), a `style` hint (`primary`, `danger`, `neutral` or
`success`), and `data`. The data is opaque and signed by Muster; return it unchanged with the press. Map a style that
your messenger lacks to the closest one, or show a plain button. Muster sends at most `max_per_message` buttons, and
drops Snooze buttons first: the preset of the first day of the week ("Until Monday 09:00"), then the preset of the next
morning ("Until tomorrow 09:00"), then the durations from the longest. A firing Root message on an On-call Route has
seven buttons, Ack, Resolve, three durations and the two presets, so a bridge that declares `max_per_message: 5` gets
Ack, Resolve and the three durations.

**Length and safe truncation.** Muster keeps the `body` within `limits.max_body_length` code points of the CommonMark it
sends. Choose that limit so that a body of that length fits your messenger after your rendering. When the rendered
message is still too long, you make the final cut where your markup needs it, and answer `truncated: true`. Cut by
whole code points, never inside an entity, a tag or a surrogate pair, and close any markup you opened. A request whose
body exceeds `max_body_length` is `invalid`.

## `Idempotency-Key`

Every request that creates something carries an `Idempotency-Key` header: `postMessage`, `replyInThread`,
`sendDirectMessage` and `answerEvent`. The key is one to 255 printable ASCII characters without spaces. Muster reuses a
key when it retries a request, also after a crash or a timeout.

The bridge must:

- store each key **per token**: the same key sent with another Connection's token is another request;
- keep each key with its **successful** (`2xx`) result for **at least 24 hours**, because Muster may retry long after
  the first attempt, and a bridge that forgot the key would post a second message;
- answer a repeated key with that first result and `replayed: true`, whatever the body of the repeated request, without
  creating anything again;
- store nothing for a failed request, so that its retry is a new attempt;
- answer a repeated key whose first request is still running with `transient`;
- pass the key on to the messenger when the messenger has an idempotency mechanism of its own.

Muster treats a `postMessage` whose answer says `replayed` as the same message, and follows it with an `editMessage` of
its current state, because the retry may carry a newer state than the request whose answer was lost. If the bridge did
not know the key, the retry posts a second message, and Muster records a **possible duplicate** in the Alert Group's
Timeline.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant M as Muster
  participant B as Bridge
  participant X as Messenger

  M->>B: POST /v1/messages with Idempotency-Key K1
  B->>X: post the message
  X-->>B: posted
  Note over B: stores K1 with its result for 24 hours, per token
  B--xM: the answer is lost, Muster times out
  M->>B: POST /v1/messages with the same Idempotency-Key K1
  B-->>M: 201 with message_id and replayed true, nothing is posted again
  M->>B: PATCH /v1/messages/message_id with the current state
  B->>X: edit the message
  B-->>M: 200 truncated false
  M->>B: POST /v1/messages/message_id/thread-replies with Idempotency-Key K2 and thread_ref null
  B->>X: reply in the Thread
  B-->>M: 201 with thread_ref
  M->>B: POST the next reply with Idempotency-Key K3 and that thread_ref
  B-->>M: 201 with the same thread_ref
```

## `thread_ref`

The messenger decides how a Thread is named, and some messengers need a Thread to be created before the first reply.
The `thread_ref` carries that between calls, so that the bridge needs no store of its own that maps messages to Threads:

- `postMessage` may return a `thread_ref` when the Thread's id is known at once, and may leave it out or return
  `null`.
- `replyInThread` carries the last `thread_ref` Muster received for that message, from `postMessage` or from an earlier
  reply, or `null` when it has none. When it is `null`, create the Thread if your messenger needs that.
- `replyInThread` always returns a `thread_ref`. Muster stores it and sends it with the next reply of the same Thread.

A `thread_ref` is opaque to Muster, up to 512 characters, and it may equal the message id. In a `thread_message` event,
the `thread_ref` is the same value, or `null`.

## Presses within 3 seconds, and answers later

The bridge confirms a press to its messenger itself, within the messenger's deadline and **at most 3 seconds after the
press**, before Muster has seen it. Messengers expect that quick answer; Muster would be too late. Only then does the
bridge report the press to Muster as an event.

When Muster has something to say to the person, it answers with a separate `answerEvent` call, made before it
acknowledges the event: before it answers a push with `204`, or polls with the next cursor. Muster makes the call within
a few seconds of receiving the event, or not at all. A press that works is not answered; the edited Root message shows
its result. A refusal, a failure, a press from an account without an Account link and a press on a test message are
answered.

```http
POST /v1/answers HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: <key>
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{ "event_id": "ev-1001", "text": "Done: Acknowledged #42" }
```

```json
{ "shown_as": "ephemeral", "replayed": false }
```

The bridge shows `text` to the person who caused the event `event_id`, as plain text of at most 500 characters, and
answers where:

A `press`
:   Privately (`ephemeral` or `popup`) when the messenger allows it, with `private_answers`, and the press is recent
    enough; otherwise in the Thread of the message (`thread`).

A `thread_message`
:   In that Thread (`thread`), never as a pop-up.

An `account_link`
:   In the direct chat it came from (`direct`).

An event that the bridge no longer knows, or can no longer answer anywhere, is `gone`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor P as Person
  participant X as Messenger
  participant B as Bridge
  participant M as Muster

  P->>X: presses a button
  X->>B: callback with the button's data
  B->>X: confirms the press at once, within 3 seconds
  B->>B: queues a press event
  alt Poll mode
    M->>B: GET /v1/events with the cursor
    B-->>M: the events and next_cursor
  else Push mode
    B->>M: POST the signed event to the callback address
  end
  M->>M: verifies the button's data and runs the Command
  opt Muster has something to say
    M->>B: POST /v1/answers with event_id and text
    B->>X: shows the text to the person
    X-->>P: privately (ephemeral or pop-up), or in the Thread
    B-->>M: 200 with shown_as
  end
  alt Poll mode
    M->>B: the next GET /v1/events with next_cursor
  else Push mode
    M-->>B: 204
  end
  Note over M: A press that works is not answered, the edited Root message shows the result
```

Muster ignores, without answering, a press or a Thread message about a message that it did not post through that
Connection. It drops a press or a Text command whose `occurred_at` is more than an hour old.

## Error classes

Errors are RFC 9457 problems (`application/problem+json`) with a `class` member that **the bridge chooses**, because
only the bridge knows what its messenger's codes mean. Muster acts on the class:

`transient`
:   A temporary failure: the messenger is down, a timeout.

    Muster retries with exponential backoff; repeated failures make the Destination Broken.

`rate_limited`
:   The messenger or the bridge throttles; send `Retry-After` in seconds.

    Muster waits exactly that long, for the channel, or for every channel of the bot when `scope` is `bot`; not counted
    as a failure; a wait longer than 15 minutes (`bridge.retry_after_max`), or none given, is treated as `transient`.

`gone`
:   The message no longer exists: deleted, or its Thread is gone.

    Muster publishes the Alert Group again once; with `reason` `edit_window_closed`, treats the message as past its edit
    window.

`forbidden`
:   The channel is missing, the bot was removed from it or lacks a right, the bot was blocked.

    Muster marks the Destination Broken until a check succeeds.

`invalid`
:   The request cannot succeed as sent: too long, malformed, an unknown id.

    Muster ends that delivery as Not delivered, without retrying.

The problem members are `title`, `status`, an optional `detail`, the `class`, and for `rate_limited` a `scope` of
`channel` (the default) or `bot`. The `detail` is shown to the Admin as the reason, as untrusted text, so write it for a
person and never put a secret in it.

```json
{ "title": "The messenger is not available.", "status": 503, "class": "transient" }
```

```json
{ "title": "Too many requests", "status": 429, "class": "rate_limited", "scope": "channel" }
```

The `429` carries `Retry-After: 7`, for example.

```json
{ "title": "The message no longer exists.", "status": 404, "class": "gone" }
```

```json
{ "title": "The message is too long for this messenger.", "status": 400, "class": "invalid" }
```

**Who decides `gone`.** Only the bridge. Muster never treats a message as gone because of a status code, and a `404`
without the class `gone` is `invalid`. A bridge that means `gone` says so in `class`. Use it for a message, a Thread or
an event that no longer exists. Muster reacts by publishing the Alert Group again, once, so do not use it for anything
else.

**Why a missing channel is `forbidden`.** A channel that does not exist, or that the bot cannot see, is
**`forbidden`, never `gone`**. `gone` makes Muster post the message again, and that would fail again at once.
`forbidden` marks the Destination Broken with your `detail`, which the Admin reads ("The bot is not a member of this
channel."), and Muster probes it with `checkChannel` until the channel works again.

**An answer without a `class`.** Muster still classifies a problem without a `class`, or an answer that is not a
problem, by its status, so a plain framework error does no harm:

`401`, `403`
:   class: `forbidden`

`408`
:   class: `transient`

`429`, and `503` with `Retry-After`
:   class: `rate_limited`

Other `5xx`, timeouts and network errors
:   class: `transient`

`404`, `410`, a redirect and everything else
:   class: `invalid`

No status is ever read as `gone`. Muster also follows no redirects, and treats one as a configuration error.

**An example mapping.** Parley, a fictional messenger, answers its own error codes. The bridge for Parley maps them
like this, as the `classify` function above does:

`502`, a timeout, `unavailable`
:   class: `transient` · why: the messenger is down

`slow_down`, with `retry_in` seconds
:   class: `rate_limited` · why: send `Retry-After`; use `scope` `bot` if the limit holds for the whole account

`message_not_found`, `thread_removed`
:   class: `gone` · why: the message or its Thread is deleted

`edit_too_old`
:   class: `gone` with `reason` `edit_window_closed` · why: the message exists, but cannot be edited any more

`channel_not_found`, `not_a_member`, `bot_banned`, `no_permission`
:   class: `forbidden` · why: the channel is unusable until somebody fixes it

`text_too_long`, `bad_request`
:   class: `invalid` · why: this request cannot succeed

`user_blocked_bot` on a direct message
:   class: `forbidden` · why: the account cannot receive a message from the bot

### Edit windows

Some messengers let a bot edit a message only for a while. Declare how long in `limits.edit_max_age_seconds`. Muster
then stops editing a Root message once it is as old as that, less 60 seconds, measured from its publication on Muster's
clock, without sending a failing request. If the messenger refuses an edit earlier than declared, answer `gone` with
`reason` `edit_window_closed`:

```json
{
  "title": "The message can no longer be edited.",
  "status": 404,
  "class": "gone",
  "reason": "edit_window_closed"
}
```

This is not a deletion. Muster marks the Root message as past its window. When the status of the Alert Group changes
after that, Muster posts a new Root message, Quietly, to the same channel, and replies under the old Thread: "This
message is no longer updated. The current one: {link}", where the link is the new message's `url` when you returned one,
and the Alert Group page otherwise. Later Thread replies go under the new Root message. Any other change leaves the old
Root message as it is. The old message keeps working: a press on its buttons, and a Text command in its Thread, act on
the Alert Group as on the current one, so the bridge must keep reporting them.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor P as Person
  participant M as Muster
  participant B as Bridge
  participant X as Messenger

  M->>B: PATCH /v1/messages/old_id after a change of status
  B->>X: edit the message
  X-->>B: refused, the message is too old
  B-->>M: 404 with class gone and reason edit_window_closed
  Note over M: marks the Root message as past its edit window
  M->>B: POST /v1/messages with the new state, Quiet, new Idempotency-Key
  B->>X: post the new Root message
  B-->>M: 201 with the new message_id and url
  M->>B: POST /v1/messages/old_id/thread-replies, a pointer to the new message
  B->>X: reply in the old Thread
  B-->>M: 201
  Note over M: later Thread replies go under the new Root message
  P->>X: presses a button of the old message
  X->>B: callback
  B->>M: press event with the old message_id
  M->>M: runs the Command on the Alert Group as for the current message
```

## Events

The bridge reports what people do in the messenger as events. Every event has a stable `id`, a `type` and
`occurred_at`; Muster handles each `id` of a Connection once. An `id` is up to 200 printable ASCII characters without
spaces, because it travels as the `webhook-id` header of a push. A bridge delivers every event at least once, so
Muster deduplicates.

`press`
:   needs: `buttons`

    A person pressed a button of a message of the bot, already confirmed to the messenger.

`thread_message`
:   needs: `thread_messages`

    A person, never the bot itself, wrote in the Thread of a message of the bot.

`account_link`
:   needs: always

    A person sent the bot an Account link token, or opened the `link_url_template` link.

`message_deleted`
:   needs: `deletion_events`

    A message of the bot was deleted in the messenger.

```json
{
  "id": "ev-1001",
  "type": "press",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-18T14:05:12Z",
  "message_id": "m-77",
  "user": { "external_id": "u-alice", "display_name": "Alice Smith", "handle": "alice" },
  "data": "a1.k2.QmFzZTY0U2lnbmF0dXJlRXhhbXBsZQ"
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "ev-1002",
  "type": "thread_message",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-18T14:07:40Z",
  "message_id": "m-77",
  "thread_ref": "t-77",
  "user": { "external_id": "u-alice", "display_name": "Alice Smith", "handle": "alice" },
  "text": "ack"
}
```

`message_id` of a `thread_message` is the message whose Thread it is in, as in the path of `replyInThread`, usually the
Root message, never the id of a reply. `text` is plain text of at most 4000 characters, with mentions of the bot
removed.

```json
{
  "id": "ev-1003",
  "type": "account_link",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-18T14:09:03Z",
  "token": "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFG",
  "user": { "external_id": "u-alice", "display_name": "Alice Smith", "handle": "alice" }
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "ev-1004",
  "type": "message_deleted",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-18T14:11:30Z",
  "message_id": "m-77"
}
```

### Polling

Offer `poll` in `event_delivery` and implement `pollEvents`. Muster, on the Leader, calls it in a loop:

```http
GET /v1/events?cursor=<next_cursor>&wait=25 HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

```json
{
  "events": [
    {
      "id": "ev-1001",
      "type": "press",
      "occurred_at": "2026-10-18T14:05:12Z",
      "message_id": "m-77",
      "user": { "external_id": "u-alice", "display_name": "Alice Smith", "handle": "alice" },
      "data": "a1.k2.QmFzZTY0U2lnbmF0dXJlRXhhbXBsZQ"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "c-5"
}
```

- Return the events after `cursor`, oldest first, at once when there are any. Without `cursor`, return all of them.
  When there are none, hold the request open until one arrives or until `wait` seconds have passed, and then return an
  empty list. `wait` is 0 to 60, 25 by default (`bridge.poll_wait` is the 25 that Muster sends). Muster waits for your answer up to `wait` plus 15 seconds.
- `next_cursor` is opaque to Muster. Muster handles the batch and sends the `next_cursor` with its next call; only
  then may you forget the events before that cursor. Keep events that Muster has not passed for at least 24 hours.
- A cursor that you do not know is `invalid`; Muster then polls again without one. Return only the events of the
  token's bot.
- Only one Muster replica polls a Connection at a time, but after a handover two calls may overlap. That is why events
  are deduplicated by `id`.

### Push

Offer `push` in `event_delivery`. The Admin chooses it on the Connection and enters a **push secret**. The bridge posts
each event, one per request, to the callback address that the Connection shows:

```text
<MUSTER_INGEST_URL>/api/v1/callbacks/bridge/<connection id>
```

The request is signed as [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) specifies:

`webhook-id`
:   The event's `id`, kept across retries.

`webhook-timestamp`
:   The Unix time of this attempt, in seconds.

`webhook-signature`
:   `v1,` followed by the base64 of HMAC-SHA256 over `<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<body>`.

The push secret is `whsec_` followed by the base64 of at least 24 random bytes. The HMAC key is **the decoded bytes**:
strip the prefix `whsec_` and base64-decode the rest. The signed content is the three values joined with full stops,
followed by the exact body that you send. `webhook-signature` may hold several signatures separated by spaces, which is
how a secret is rotated. Muster refuses a `webhook-timestamp` more than 5 minutes away from its own clock, so keep your
clock right, and sign each attempt with the time of that attempt.

Generate a secret and enter it on both sides:

```sh
printf 'whsec_%s\n' "$(head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64)"
```

Muster answers:

| Answer | Means | The bridge |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Muster handled the event, now or before | forgets the event |
| `400` | the event can never be handled | drops it |
| `401` | the signature, the Connection or its mode is wrong | keeps the event, retries after fixing its configuration |
| anything else, a timeout | a temporary failure | retries with backoff for at least an hour, same `webhook-id` |

Muster answers `401` for a bad signature, an unknown Connection and a Connection in poll mode alike, so the endpoint
reveals nothing about which Connections exist.

**In the protocol the bridge signs and Muster verifies.** The snippets below show both sides: the signer is what your
bridge needs, and the verifier is what Muster checks, which is useful in your tests. Both were run against Muster's own
code.

```go
package pushsig

import (
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/base64"
	"errors"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// timestampPattern is what Muster accepts as webhook-timestamp: Unix seconds, digits only.
var timestampPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9]{1,12}$`)

// key decodes a push secret: whsec_ and the standard base64 of the key.
func key(secret string) ([]byte, error) {
	encoded, ok := strings.CutPrefix(secret, "whsec_")
	if !ok {
		return nil, errors.New("the push secret does not start with whsec_")
	}
	k, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(encoded)
	if err != nil || len(k) == 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("the push secret is not whsec_ and base64")
	}
	return k, nil
}

// signature is v1, a comma and the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of "<id>.<timestamp>.<body>".
func signature(k []byte, id, timestamp string, body []byte) string {
	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, k)
	mac.Write([]byte(id + "." + timestamp + "."))
	mac.Write(body)
	return "v1," + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
}

// Sign returns the value of webhook-timestamp and of webhook-signature for the event with this id, sent now.
// The bridge sets webhook-id to the id of the event, and retries the event with the same webhook-id, with a new
// timestamp and signature.
func Sign(secret, id string, now time.Time, body []byte) (timestamp, sig string, err error) {
	k, err := key(secret)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	timestamp = strconv.FormatInt(now.Unix(), 10)
	return timestamp, signature(k, id, timestamp, body), nil
}

// Verify checks the three headers of a pushed event the way Muster does. The header may hold several
// signatures separated by spaces; one that matches is enough.
func Verify(secret, id, timestamp string, body []byte, header string, now time.Time) error {
	k, err := key(secret)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	want := []byte(signature(k, id, timestamp, body))
	matched := false
	for _, part := range strings.Fields(header) {
		if hmac.Equal([]byte(part), want) {
			matched = true
		}
	}
	if !matched {
		return errors.New("no signature matches")
	}
	if !timestampPattern.MatchString(timestamp) {
		return errors.New("the timestamp is not Unix seconds")
	}
	sent, err := strconv.ParseInt(timestamp, 10, 64)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if d := now.Sub(time.Unix(sent, 0)); d > 5*time.Minute || d < -5*time.Minute {
		return errors.New("the timestamp is more than 5 minutes from the clock")
	}
	return nil
}
```

For a bridge in Python:

```python
import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import re
import time


def _key(secret: str) -> bytes:
    """Decode a push secret: whsec_ and the standard base64 of the key."""
    if not secret.startswith("whsec_"):
        raise ValueError("the push secret does not start with whsec_")
    key = base64.b64decode(secret.removeprefix("whsec_"), validate=True)
    if not key:
        raise ValueError("the push secret is not whsec_ and base64")
    return key


def _signature(secret: str, msg_id: str, timestamp: str, body: bytes) -> str:
    mac = hmac.new(_key(secret), f"{msg_id}.{timestamp}.".encode() + body, hashlib.sha256)
    return "v1," + base64.b64encode(mac.digest()).decode()


def sign(secret: str, msg_id: str, body: bytes, now: float | None = None) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return the values of webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature."""
    timestamp = str(int(now if now is not None else time.time()))
    return timestamp, _signature(secret, msg_id, timestamp, body)


def verify(secret: str, msg_id: str, timestamp: str, body: bytes, header: str,
           now: float | None = None) -> bool:
    """Check the three headers of a pushed event the way Muster does."""
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]{1,12}", timestamp):
        return False
    want = _signature(secret, msg_id, timestamp, body).encode()
    matched = False
    for part in header.split():
        if hmac.compare_digest(part.encode(), want):
            matched = True
    drift = (now if now is not None else time.time()) - int(timestamp)
    return matched and abs(drift) <= 300
```

Verification compares in constant time, so that the time it takes tells nothing about the signature. It accepts a
header with several signatures when one of them matches, and refuses a timestamp more than 5 minutes from the clock.
Sign and send the exact bytes of the body: a re-serialized body has another signature.

### Account links

An **Account link** ties a Muster User to their account in the messenger. A press, a Text command or a Mention names a
person only through it, and it is started in the person's Muster profile, never from the messenger. Every bridge takes
a **token**; a bridge that can look people up and write to them also offers a **code**. See
[Link your messenger accounts](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/account-links.md) for what the person sees.

- **By token.** The profile shows a token of 43 characters of base64url, valid for 10 minutes and for one use. The
  person sends it to the bot in a direct message, or opens your `link_url_template` link, which hands it to the bot. The
  bridge sends an `account_link` event. The token is the whole text of the direct message, trimmed and after an
  optional `/start `. Muster links the sender's account and answers with `answerEvent`, which you show in the direct
  chat the event came from: "Linked to Muster user …".
- **By code.** It is offered only with `direct_messages` and `bot_can_start`, and a `user_lookup` other than `none`. The
  person enters their handle, of the kind `user_lookup` declares, in their Muster profile. Muster calls `findUsers`,
  then `sendDirectMessage` with the code and a warning, and the person types the code into the profile. The bot sends
  no confirmation.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor P as Person
  participant W as Muster profile
  participant M as Muster
  participant B as Bridge
  participant X as Messenger

  alt By token
    P->>W: selects Link and chooses the Connection
    W-->>P: a token of 43 characters, and the link from link_url_template
    P->>X: sends the token to the bot in a direct message
    X->>B: the direct message
    B->>B: the text is a token, so it queues an account_link event
    B-->>M: the event, by poll or push
    M->>M: links the sender's account to the User
    M->>B: POST /v1/answers with event_id, Linked to Muster user
    B->>X: shows the answer in the direct chat
  else By code
    P->>W: enters the handle, such as a login
    W->>M: asks for a code
    M->>B: GET /v1/users with handle
    B-->>M: items with the account
    M->>B: POST /v1/direct-messages with the code and a warning
    B->>X: sends the direct message
    X-->>P: the code
    P->>W: types the code
    W->>M: confirms, and the link is made
  end
```

## Test your bridge

### `muster bridge check`

`muster bridge check <url>` runs the protocol against a bridge, without a Muster database, master key or configuration.
It writes no file and stores nothing, and never changes the bridge's configuration. It does post, edit and reply in the
channel of `--channel`, delete its own message there when the bridge offers deletion, and write to the person of
`--handle`.

```sh
muster bridge check http://127.0.0.1:18095 --token-file ./token --channel alerts \
  --forbidden-channel nobot --handle alice --no-interactive
```

`--token-file <file>`
:   The bridge's token, alone in the file (required).

`--channel <id>`
:   A channel the bot can post to (required).

`--forbidden-channel <id>`
:   A channel the bot cannot use, which must answer `forbidden`; without it the step `forbidden_channel` is skipped.

`--handle <handle>`
:   A person to look up and write to; without it `user_lookup` and `direct_message` are skipped.

`--push-listen <addr>`
:   Where the push listener listens, `127.0.0.1:0` by default.

`--push-url <url>`
:   Where the bridge reaches the push listener, the listener's own address by default.

`--push-secret-file <file>`
:   The push secret, `whsec_` and base64, instead of a generated one.

`--no-interactive`
:   Skip `press` and `push`, which need a person.

Flags may come before or after the URL. The check prints one line per step as it ends: `PASS <step>`,
`FAIL <step>: <reason>` or `SKIP <step>: <why>`. The steps run in this order: `info`, `channel_check`, `post`,
`replayed_key`, `buttons`, `edit`, `thread_reply`, `thread_ref`, `forbidden_channel`, `user_lookup`, `direct_message`,
`delete`, `poll`, `press`, `push` and `answer`. A failed `info` ends the run. `replayed_key` posts the same request
again with its `Idempotency-Key`, which must return the same `message_id` with `replayed`.

```text
PASS info
PASS channel_check
PASS post
PASS replayed_key
PASS buttons
PASS edit
PASS thread_reply
PASS thread_ref
PASS forbidden_channel
PASS user_lookup
PASS direct_message
PASS delete
PASS poll
SKIP press: --no-interactive
SKIP push: --no-interactive
PASS answer
```

It exits `0` when no step failed, `1` when one did, and `2` on a usage error. A step for an optional feature that the
bridge does not declare is skipped.

Without `--no-interactive`, the check also needs a person. For a bridge that offers push, it opens a push listener and
prints `PUSH <url> <secret>` (or `PUSH <url>` with `--push-secret-file`): point your bridge's push target there with
that secret. Before it waits, up to five minutes, for a press, it prints `WAIT press: …, message_id <id>`; press a
button of that message in your messenger, or play the person in a script.

The check runs from the `muster` binary, or from the development image:

```sh
docker run --rm --network host -v "$PWD/token:/token:ro" ghcr.io/muster-io/muster:edge bridge check \
  http://127.0.0.1:18095 --token-file /token --channel alerts --forbidden-channel nobot --handle alice \
  --no-interactive
```

(`--network host` gives the container your loopback on Linux only.)

### The fake bridge of `muster dev`

`muster dev` starts a fake bridge on `127.0.0.1:18094` that offers every feature and both event delivery modes, and
creates a Bridge Connection "Dev Bridge" to it in poll mode, with the token `muster-dev-bridge-token`. The fake serves
a second bot with the token `muster-dev-bridge-token-b`, which `muster dev` creates no Connection for, so you can run
the check against it without touching the demo. Its channels are `ch-alerts` and `ch-alerts-prod`, and `ch-nobot` is one
it refuses with `forbidden`. It records every request at `/_fake/requests` and takes scripted faults at
`/_fake/faults`. It is for Muster's own tests and for trying Muster; it is not a messenger.

### The example bridge

The [example bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/write-a-bridge.md#the-example-bridge) passes every step of the check, and skips the optional ones when
`BRIDGE_FEATURES` switches them off. Use it as a second opinion when your own bridge fails a step.

### Check a bridge before saving it

The Admin can check a bridge before saving the Connection. **Check connection** in the form of a Bridge Connection runs
the steps `info` and `event_delivery` against the base URL and token typed in the form, and stores nothing; see
[Check before saving](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/bridge.md#check-before-saving).

### See what Muster sent

The **Request log** tab of the Bridge Connection (**Connections → a Connection → Request log**) shows the recent
requests that Muster sent to your bridge and the answers it got, and the events that reached Muster's callback address,
with secrets masked. Open a record for the request with its headers and body, and the problem your bridge answered. See
[Request log](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/request-log.md).

## Run your bridge

- **The token and the push secret.** One token is one bot. Keep both in a secret store or a file with restricted
  access, not in the image or on a command line. To change the push secret without a refused push, sign with both the
  old and the new secret while it changes in Muster: `webhook-signature` may hold both signatures, separated by a
  space, and Muster accepts the header when one of them matches. The Go library's `PushTarget` holds one secret, so it
  signs with one: between the change in Muster and `b.SetPush` with the new secret, Muster answers its pushes `401`.
  The library keeps those events and retries them, for at least an hour and at once after `b.SetPush`, so none is lost
  when the bridge gets the new secret within that hour.
- **Logs.** Never log a token, a push secret, an Account link token, or an `Authorization` header. The Account link
  token is a credential until it is used. A `detail` that you answer is shown to the Admin, so keep secrets out of it
  too.
- **Who calls you.** Muster sends `User-Agent: Muster/<version>` on every request, only to the base URL saved on the
  Connection, and follows no redirects. Serve the bridge over HTTPS when it is reachable from beyond a trusted
  network. A bridge that cannot reach Muster should use polling.
- **Timeouts.** Answer quickly, and return an error class rather than hang: Muster waits only so long for an answer, and
  treats a timeout as `transient`. A `pollEvents` call may be held for up to 60 seconds, so do not put a shorter
  timeout in front of it.
- **Monitoring.** Muster monitors your bridge through the health of its Destinations. A Destination that the bridge
  refuses with `forbidden`, or that keeps failing for the whole Transient budget (10 attempts within 30 minutes),
  becomes **Broken**, with your `detail` as the reason. A bridge that asks Muster to wait does not make a Destination
  Broken unless it asks for more than 15 minutes. While a Destination is Broken, Muster probes it every 5 minutes, with
  `checkChannel` when nothing waits, and the first success ends the state. The Internal alert `MusterDestinationBroken`
  tells the operators; its runbook is [MusterDestinationBroken](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDestinationBroken.md). A
  Bridge Connection whose bridge cannot be reached does not become Broken itself: its Destinations do.

## Licence

- **The protocol**, `api/bridge.yaml`, is MIT licensed. A bridge may stay closed: nothing in the protocol obliges you to
  publish your bridge, or to license it under Muster's licence.
- **The bridge libraries** and the **example bridge** are MIT licensed. They are developed in their own repositories,
  which take contributions under the MIT licence and without a CLA.
- **Muster** itself is AGPL-3.0-only. A contribution to `api/bridge.yaml` in Muster's repository is a contribution to
  Muster and falls under the CLA that Muster's repository asks for.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/account-links.md -->
# Link your messenger accounts

An **Account link** ties your Telegram account, your account on a Mattermost server, your account in a Slack workspace,
or your account on a messenger that Muster reaches through a [Bridge](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/bridge.md), to your Muster User. With it, a button
you press under an Alert Group in a messenger runs as you — the Timeline names you and shows the messenger you pressed
in — and Mentions and footers in the messenger name you.

A Telegram account belongs to one User across every Telegram Connection. A Mattermost account belongs to one User per
Mattermost Connection, since each Connection is its own server, and so does a Slack account, per Slack Connection,
and an account reached through a Bridge, per Bridge Connection. You have at
most one Telegram account and one account per Mattermost, Slack or Bridge Connection; linking another one replaces the
earlier link, and linking the same account again keeps its link and updates its username and name.

## Why links start in your profile

Every link starts in your signed-in Muster session, and the secret travels from there to your messenger account —
never the other way. Nobody can link your account by typing your name into a chat, and nobody can link their account
to your User: only the account that receives the secret Muster gave you in your own session gets linked. That is why
linking needs no extra password or TOTP code, and why an API token, an Admin's included, cannot start, confirm or
remove a link of its own User.

## Link Telegram

1. In your profile, open **Messenger accounts**, choose the Telegram Connection and select **Link Telegram** — or
   **Relink Telegram** once you have a Telegram link, which the new link replaces.
2. Muster shows a link `https://t.me/<bot>?start=<token>`. Open it on the device where you use Telegram, within 10
   minutes (`account_link.telegram_token_ttl`); the link works once.
3. Telegram opens a chat with the bot. Press **Start**.
4. The bot answers "Linked to Muster user {your name} ({your login})", and your profile shows the link at once.

If the bot answers "This link is invalid or expired. Start again from your Muster profile.", the link was used
already, expired, belongs to another Telegram bot of Muster, or was never issued: start again from your profile. If it
answers "This account is linked to another user. Its owner or an admin can unlink it.", that Telegram account is
linked to someone else; nothing changed.

## Link Mattermost

1. In your profile, open **Messenger accounts**, choose the Mattermost Connection, enter your Mattermost username —
   with or without the `@` — and select **Send code**.
2. The Connection's bot sends you a direct message: "You requested a link to Muster. Do not share this code." with an
   8-character code. If you did not ask for it, ignore it.
3. Type the code into your profile within 10 minutes (`account_link.mattermost_code`); capital and small letters are the same. The bot confirms
   "Linked to Muster user {your name}".

A code allows 5 attempts; after five wrong codes it stops working, even with the right code, and you request a new one.
A new request replaces your earlier one. You can request 5 codes an hour, and one Mattermost account gets at most 3
codes an hour, whoever asks (`account_link.mattermost_code_requests`); beyond that, wait until the oldest request is an hour old. A username the server does not
know, a bot account and a deactivated account cannot be linked. An account that is linked to another User is refused.

The bot must be allowed to open direct messages with you; see [Direct messages](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/mattermost.md#direct-messages).

## Link Slack

1. In your profile, open **Messenger accounts**, choose the Slack Connection, enter your Slack email or name and select
   **Send code**. An email finds your account for sure; a name is compared with the name and the display name of each
   account, regardless of case.
2. The Connection's bot sends you a direct message: "You requested a link to Muster. Do not share this code." with an
   8-character code. It shows in the **Messages** tab of the bot's app, which is read-only, so you can read the code and
   cannot write to the bot. If you did not ask for it, ignore it.
3. Type the code into your profile within 10 minutes (`account_link.slack_code`); capital and small letters are the
   same. The bot confirms "Linked to Muster user {your name}".

If Muster answers "No Slack account with this email or name was found.", check what you typed. If it answers "Several
Slack accounts have this name. Enter the email instead.", do. A bot, a deleted account and Slackbot cannot be linked,
and an account that is linked to another User is refused.

A code allows 5 attempts; after five wrong codes it stops working, even with the right code, and you request a new one.
A new request replaces your earlier one. You can request 5 codes an hour, and one Slack account gets at most 3 codes an
hour, whoever asks (`account_link.slack_code_requests`); beyond that, wait until the oldest request is an hour old.

The bot can send the code only while the Messages tab of its app is on. Slack documents that with it off it refuses the
direct message, and then Muster answers that the Messages tab of the Slack app is turned off; the problem is
`messages_tab_disabled`. Ask the admin of the Slack app to turn the tab on under **App Home**, then request a new code.
The refused request still counts toward the limits above, so if you tried several times before the tab was on, you may
have to wait up to an hour. See [Connect Slack](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/slack.md#what-the-manifest-sets).

## Link through a Bridge

A Bridge Connection reaches a messenger through a bridge, which tells Muster in its info what it can do for Account
links. Every bridge takes a **token** that you send to its bot. A bridge that can look people up and start a direct
chat with them also offers a **code** that its bot sends you, as Mattermost does. Your profile offers what the
Connection's bridge declares.

Once linked, a Mention of you in a message of that Connection names you by the name the bridge reported for your
account, which a bridge with native mentions turns into its messenger's mention, and the footer of a message you
acknowledged, snoozed or resolved names you by that name. Without a link, a Mention is your Muster name as plain text,
which notifies nobody.

### By a token sent to the bot

1. In your profile, open **Messenger accounts**, choose the Bridge Connection and select **Link**.
2. Muster shows a token of 43 characters and, when the bridge declares a link that opens a chat with its bot, that link
   as well. Within 10 minutes (`account_link.bridge_token_ttl`), send the token to the bot of that Connection in a direct message, or open the link,
   which hands the token to the bot. The token works once, and only with the bot of the Connection you chose.
3. The bot answers "Linked to Muster user {your name} ({your login})", and your profile shows the link with the name
   and the handle the bridge reported for your account.

If the bot answers "This link is invalid or expired. Start again from your Muster profile.", the token was used
already, expired, was started for another Connection — another bridge, or another bot of the same bridge — or was
never issued: start again from your profile. If it answers "This account is linked to another user. Its owner or an
admin can unlink it.", that account is linked to someone else; nothing changed.

### By a code by direct message

The code is offered only when the bridge declares how it finds people — its **lookup kind**, one of email address,
login, username or user id — and that its bot can start a direct chat. Your profile names the field after that kind:
**Email**, **Login**, **Username** or **User id**.

1. In your profile, choose the Bridge Connection, enter your email address, login, username or user id in the
   messenger, as the field asks, and select **Send code**.
2. The bot sends you a direct message: "You requested a link to Muster. Do not share this code." with an 8-character
   code. If you did not ask for it, ignore it.
3. Type the code into your profile within 10 minutes (`account_link.bridge_code`); capital and small letters are the same. The link is made at
   once, and the bot sends no confirmation.

If the bridge finds no one, Muster answers "No account with this email was found." — or login, username or user id. If
the bot may not write to you, Muster answers "The bot cannot send you a direct message. Send it the token instead."
The limits are those of Mattermost: 5 attempts per code, a new request replaces your earlier one, 5 code requests an
hour for you and at most 3 codes an hour for one account, whoever asks (`account_link.bridge_code_requests`). An account
that is linked to another User is refused.

## Several Connections of one messenger

An Organization may have several Connections of one messenger, such as two Mattermost bots on one server, two Slack apps
or a second Telegram bot. What a link covers differs by messenger:

- **Mattermost links are per Connection.** Each Mattermost Connection is its own Identity space, even when two
  Connections use bots on the same server: two bots on one server need two links, made one after the other from
  **Link Mattermost** with each Connection. Your profile lists one row per Connection.
- **Slack links are per Connection.** Each Slack Connection is its own Identity space, even when two Connections serve
  the same workspace with two apps: two Connections need two links, made one after the other from **Link Slack** with
  each Connection. Your profile lists one row per Connection.
- **Bridge links are per Connection.** Each Bridge Connection is its own Identity space, also when two Connections reach
  the same bridge with two bots: two Connections need two links, made one after the other, and a token started for one
  of them links nothing when you send it to the other's bot. Your profile lists one row per Connection.
- **A Telegram link is valid for all Telegram bots.** Telegram has one Identity space, so the link you make through any
  Telegram Connection lets you press buttons sent by every Telegram bot of Muster. Your profile shows it as "Telegram ·
  @<username> · for all Telegram bots", with "linked via <Connection>" below.

One chat reached through two Connections is two Destinations, and each posts its own message for every Alert Group. This
is allowed, but the Route editor warns when two or more of a Route's Destinations deliver to the same chat — one
Telegram chat, or one Mattermost server and channel — since their messages appear twice. The Destinations list, the
Route editor and the Alert Group page name each Destination's Connection and channel, so you can tell them apart.

## Unlink

In your profile, under **Messenger accounts**, remove the link. Nothing can be unlinked from a chat. Removing a link,
like making one, is recorded in the Audit log with who did it and from where.

## What Admins can do

Admins see the links of every User on the user page, under **Account links**, and can remove any of them — their own
from the web session only, as above. They cannot create a link for someone else. Deleting a User removes their links and voids the links they had started.

## What a press answers

| Who pressed | What happens | The private answer |
|---|---|---|
| An account without a link | Nothing changes | "Your Telegram account is not linked to Muster. Link it in your profile: {link}" — or the same for Mattermost or Slack, and "Your account is not linked to Muster. Link it in your profile: {link}" through a Bridge; the link goes to your profile and carries no secret |
| A linked Viewer | Nothing changes | "You are not permitted to do this" |
| A linked User who is disabled | Nothing changes | "Your Muster account is disabled" |
| A linked Responder or Admin | The Command runs as that User | "Done: {command}", or why it was refused |

The Audit log records `account_link.link`, `account_link.unlink` and `account_link.link_rejected` with the User, the
messenger, the account's id and username, and the Connection; a rejection says why: `token_unknown`, `token_used`,
`token_expired`, `wrong_connection`, `wrong_code` or `conflict`.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/events.md -->
# Outgoing webhook: events mode

An outgoing webhook Destination in the **events mode** sends one HTTP `POST` for every lifecycle event of every Alert
Group on its Routes: an ordered, signed stream of versioned JSON events that an automation can record, react to or
forward. Muster renders nothing for a chat here; for a chat with a REST API, use the template mode instead.

In the examples, `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL` is `https://muster.example.org` and the receiving endpoint is
`https://automation.example.org/muster`.

## Create the Destination

Create a Destination of type `webhook` with the mode `events`:

```json
{
  "type": "webhook",
  "name": "automation",
  "mode": "events",
  "events": {
    "url": "https://automation.example.org/muster",
    "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }]
  },
  "proxy": { "enabled": false },
  "mentions": { "...": "Mention settings, as for any Destination" },
  "limiter": { "limit": 5, "per_seconds": 1 }
}
```

- The **URL** and the **header values** are Go templates. They can read the Destination's Secrets as
  `{{ .Secrets.<name> }}` (or `{{ $.Secrets.<name> }}`, or `{{ index .Secrets "<name>" }}`) and nothing else; any
  other use of `.Secrets`, such as `{{ with .Secrets }}` or `{{ $s := .Secrets }}`, is refused, because Muster could
  not check that the Secret exists. They are parsed and run on a dry run when you save; an error names the field, its
  line and its column.
- Muster sets `Content-Type`, `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` itself; a header template may
  not name them. Every request also carries `User-Agent: Muster/<version>` unless a header template sets its own.
- The **proxy** is the Destination's own; the requests never read `HTTP_PROXY` or `HTTPS_PROXY`.
- The **limiter** defaults to 5 requests per second in the form (`destination.webhook.limiter`).
- An outgoing webhook has no Connection and no Destination check: checking it answers `422 check_not_supported`.

The answer to the creation carries the **Signing secret** once, in `signing_secret`. Store it where the endpoint verifies the signatures; Muster
never shows it again.

## Secrets

Credentials the endpoint needs go into the Destination's **Secrets**, never into the URL or a header as text:

```sh
curl -X PUT https://muster.example.org/api/v1/destinations/DSK7M3QX9P2RTA/secrets/token \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MUSTER_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"value":"the-token-of-the-endpoint"}'
```

- A Secret name is a letter or an underscore followed by letters, digits and underscores.
- Values are write-only: `GET …/secrets` lists names, whether they are set and when they last changed, with an `ETag`
  that `If-Match` on `PUT` and `DELETE` compares with.
- Everyone who can read Destinations sees the URL and header templates as written, with the references only.
- Secret values and the Signing secrets are masked as `[redacted]` in delivery errors, the Timeline and the logs.
- A template that reads a Secret the Destination does not have fails: that event is not sent and ends as Not
  delivered.

A header named `Authorization`, or a URL whose user information or query holds a literal value instead of a
`{{ .Secrets.<name> }}` reference, gives the Destination the warning `literal_credential` with the JSON Pointer of the
field, for example `/events/headers/0/value`: the value is shown to everyone who can read Destinations.

## What is sent

One `POST` per lifecycle event, with the version 1 body as `application/json`:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "event": "created",
  "notify": true,
  "mentions": [{ "type": "user", "id": "SR2K9D1VW3MPTE", "name": "Alice Smith", "login": "alice" }],
  "sequence": 1,
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-03T09:41:07Z",
  "actor": { "kind": "system", "transport": "system" },
  "alert_group": {
    "number": 412,
    "id": "AGK7M3QX9P2RTA",
    "title": "HighErrorRate payments-api",
    "summary": "Error rate above 5% for 10 minutes",
    "status": "firing",
    "route": { "id": "RT8Q2M4X7K1P3B", "name": "payments" },
    "urgent": false,
    "severity_level": "critical",
    "started_at": "2026-10-03T09:41:07Z",
    "resolved_at": null,
    "snooze_until": null,
    "reopen_count": 0,
    "url": "https://muster.example.org/alert-groups/AGK7M3QX9P2RTA"
  },
  "alerts": [
    {
      "fingerprint": "6f1c2b0e9d4a7c31",
      "status": "firing",
      "labels": { "alertname": "HighErrorRate", "service": "payments-api" },
      "annotations": { "summary": "Error rate above 5%" },
      "starts_at": "2026-10-03T09:31:07Z",
      "resolved_at": null,
      "resolve_reason": null,
      "generator_url": "https://prometheus.example.org/graph?g0.expr=…"
    }
  ]
}
```

`version`
:   `1`.

`event`
:   The lifecycle event, one of the names below.

`notify`
:   `true` exactly when the event is Loud.

`mentions`
:   Who the event mentions under the Destination's Mention settings, as data: `{"type": "everyone"}`,
    `{"type": "group", "name": …}` or `{"type": "user", "id": …, "name": …, "login": …}`. Always `[]` for a Quiet
    event.

`sequence`
:   The Alert Group's lifecycle event number. It grows with every lifecycle event of the Alert Group, may have gaps,
    and does not start at 1 for a Destination added to the Route later: rely only on "greater means newer".

`occurred_at`
:   When the event was recorded.

`actor`
:   Who made the change: a `user` or `service_account` with `id`, `name` (and the user's `login`, or the `token_name`
    used) and the `transport` (`ui`, `api`, `mattermost`, `telegram`, `bridge`, `slack`, `cli`), or `system` with the
    `reason`, for example `timer`.

`alert_group`
:   The Alert Group as it was when the event was recorded: number, `id`, title, `summary`, status, the `owner` (`id`,
    `name`, `login`) while acknowledged, Route, Urgent, Severity level, times, Reopen count and its page in Muster.

`alerts`
:   One element per Alert, by fingerprint, with its status, labels, annotations, times and the resolve reason.

The body is rendered when the event is recorded, so a retry hours later still carries the state the event described.

### Event names

Every row of the lifecycle event tables is one event, Quiet ones and those with nothing to show in a messenger
included. What delivery itself does — a Publication, a Storm summary, a final edit — is not a lifecycle event and is
never sent.

`created`
:   `notify`: true

`alerts_added`
:   `notify`: true while firing; false while acknowledged or snoozed

`alert_replaced`, `alert_resolved`, `alert_continued`, `annotations_changed`, `severity_raised`
:   `notify`: false

`urgency_raised`
:   `notify`: true when the rise ends a Snooze or removes the acknowledgement; false otherwise

`reopened`
:   `notify`: true while firing or acknowledged; false while snoozed

`snooze_ended`
:   `notify`: true

`resolved`
:   `notify`: false

`moved_to_default_route`
:   `notify`: false

`acknowledged`
:   `notify`: false

`takeover`
:   `notify`: true

`unacknowledged`
:   `notify`: true when disabling or deleting the Owner released it; false for the Command

`unresolved`, `snoozed`, `unsnoozed`, `note_added`
:   `notify`: false

`ack_timeout`
:   `notify`: true

`unclaimed`
:   `notify`: false

`reminder`
:   `notify`: true

`reminder_answered`
:   `notify`: false

`auto_unacknowledged`
:   `notify`: true

`notices_missed`
:   `notify`: true

The event `test` is sent only by a Destination test: it carries `test: true` and `sequence` 0 and belongs to no Alert
Group's order.

### Versioning

New event names and new fields are added within `version` 1. Removing a field or changing its meaning needs a new
`version`. Ignore event names and fields you do not know.

## Order and duplicates

- The events of one Alert Group are sent **in order**: the next one waits until the previous one is delivered or ends
  as Not delivered. Events of different Alert Groups do not wait for each other.
- Delivery is **at least once** and never collapsed: a retry sends the same event again with the same `webhook-id`
  and the same body. **Drop duplicates by `webhook-id`.**
- Events are never subject to Storms: during a Storm every event is sent, `created` of every Alert Group included.
- While the Destination is Broken its events wait; after it recovers, every event that came due meanwhile is sent in
  order per Alert Group, none dropped and with no age limit.

## How the answer counts

`2xx`
:   Delivered.

`429` or `503` with `Retry-After`
:   The same event is sent again exactly when asked.

`408`, any other `5xx`, a timeout or a network error
:   Retried with backoff; after `delivery.transient_budget` the Destination becomes Broken.

`401`, `403`, `404`, `410`
:   The Destination becomes Broken; the event waits and is the probe.

`400`, `413`, `422`, a redirect, any other answer
:   That event ends as Not delivered and the next one follows; the Destination stays healthy. A redirect is never
    followed; the error names its target.

Requests go through the outbound address policy: a URL that resolves to a link-local, cloud metadata, multicast or
unspecified address is refused under every policy, and loopback and private addresses need an allowed network. A
refused request makes the Destination Broken with the rule as the reason, because every later request would be
refused too. A Broken outgoing webhook is probed with its oldest waiting event; with none waiting, the next event is
attempted as soon as it comes due.

## Verify the signature

Every request carries three headers, in the style of the
[Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) specification:

- `webhook-id` — the id of the event, kept across retries;
- `webhook-timestamp` — Unix seconds when the request was signed;
- `webhook-signature` — one or more signatures `v1,<base64>`, separated by a space.

Each signature is the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}` — the raw body, byte for
byte — with the key that is the base64 after `whsec_` in the Signing secret. Accept a request when one of its
signatures matches, compare in constant time, and refuse a timestamp more than five minutes from your clock.

Go:

```go
func verify(secret, id, timestamp string, body []byte, header string) bool {
	key, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(strings.TrimPrefix(secret, "whsec_"))
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	ts, err := strconv.ParseInt(timestamp, 10, 64)
	if err != nil || math.Abs(time.Since(time.Unix(ts, 0)).Seconds()) > 300 {
		return false
	}
	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
	mac.Write([]byte(id + "." + timestamp + "."))
	mac.Write(body)
	want := []byte(base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil)))
	for _, sig := range strings.Fields(header) {
		if v, s, ok := strings.Cut(sig, ","); ok && v == "v1" && hmac.Equal([]byte(s), want) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
```

Python:

```python
import base64, hashlib, hmac, time

def verify(secret: str, msg_id: str, timestamp: str, body: bytes, header: str) -> bool:
    key = base64.b64decode(secret.removeprefix("whsec_"))
    try:
        if abs(time.time() - int(timestamp)) > 300:
            return False
    except ValueError:
        return False
    mac = hmac.new(key, f"{msg_id}.{timestamp}.".encode() + body, hashlib.sha256)
    want = base64.b64encode(mac.digest()).decode()
    for sig in header.split():
        version, _, value = sig.partition(",")
        if version == "v1" and hmac.compare_digest(value, want):
            return True
    return False
```

A shell, with `openssl`, to check a recorded request by hand — it compares neither in constant time nor the
timestamp, so do not use it in a receiver — for a body saved in `body.json`:

```sh
KEY=$(printf '%s' "${SECRET#whsec_}" | base64 -d | od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
EXPECTED="v1,$( { printf '%s.%s.' "$WEBHOOK_ID" "$WEBHOOK_TIMESTAMP"; cat body.json; } |
  openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt "hexkey:$KEY" -binary | base64)"
case " $WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE " in *" $EXPECTED "*) echo valid ;; *) echo invalid ;; esac
```

## Regenerate and retire the Signing secret

`POST /api/v1/destinations/{id}/signing-secret` makes a new Signing secret and shows it once. Until you retire the
previous one, requests carry two signatures — with the new and with the previous secret — and the Destination shows the
warning `previous_signing_secret_active` with the date since when: deploy the new secret to the receiving endpoint, then retire
the previous one with `DELETE /api/v1/destinations/{id}/signing-secret/previous`. Requests then carry one signature.
Both changes are recorded in the Audit log, never with the secret. Rotating the master keys re-encrypts the Signing
secrets but never changes them.

## Delete the Destination

Deleting an events-mode Destination sends nothing more: its waiting events end as Not delivered with "the Destination
was deleted", no final event is sent, and its secrets — the Signing secrets, the Secrets and the proxy password — are
wiped at once, or as soon as a request that was already being sent ends.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/templates.md -->
# Outgoing webhook: template mode

An outgoing webhook Destination in the **template mode** keeps one message per Alert Group in any chat that has a REST
API, the way Muster keeps a message in Mattermost or Telegram: a **create** request posts it, an **update** request
edits it to the current state, and optional **open thread** and **reply in thread** requests carry the follow-ups.
You write each request as Go templates; Muster sends them, signed, and reads the values it needs from the answers.

The messages that Muster keeps in a messenger are customised with templates written the same way: see
[Messages and templates](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/configure/messages-and-templates.md).

For an ordered stream of every lifecycle event instead, use the [events mode](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/events.md); the mode `both` sends both.

In the examples, `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL` is `https://muster.example.org` and the chat's API is
`https://chat.example.org/api`.

## Create the Destination

Create a Destination of type `webhook` with the mode `template` (or `both`, with the `events` request too):

```json
{
  "type": "webhook",
  "name": "team chat",
  "mode": "template",
  "template": {
    "create": {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "https://chat.example.org/api/channels/ops/messages",
      "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }],
      "body": "{\"text\":{{ printf \"#%d %s (%s)\" .AlertGroup.Number .AlertGroup.Title .AlertGroup.Status | toJson }}}",
      "extract": [{ "name": "id", "path": "$.data.id" }]
    },
    "update": {
      "method": "PUT",
      "url": "https://chat.example.org/api/channels/ops/messages/{{ .Response.id }}",
      "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }],
      "body": "{\"text\":{{ printf \"#%d %s (%s)\" .AlertGroup.Number .AlertGroup.Title .AlertGroup.Status | toJson }}}"
    }
  },
  "proxy": { "enabled": false },
  "mentions": { "...": "Mention settings, as for any Destination" },
  "limiter": { "limit": 5, "per_seconds": 1 }
}
```

Each request has:

- a **method**: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`;
- a **URL**, **headers** and an optional **body**, each a Go template in the same sandbox as message templates;
- for `create` and `open_thread` only, **extraction rules**: a name and a JSONPath (RFC 9535) into the JSON answer.

`create` and `update` are required; `open_thread` and `reply_in_thread` are optional. When you save, every template
is parsed and run on a dry run with a built-in example Alert Group, its Secrets and the values it may read filled with
`example-<name>`; an error answers `422` at `/template/<request>/<field>` with its line and column. The URL must then be
an absolute `http` or `https` URL.

Muster sets `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` on every request, signed with the Destination's
Signing secret as in the events mode, `Content-Type: application/json` when a request has a body and no
`Content-Type` header of its own, and `User-Agent: Muster/<version>` when it has no `User-Agent` of its own. The
requests go through Muster's outbound address policy and the Destination's proxy; redirects are never followed. The answers map to outcomes as in the [events mode](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/events.md#how-the-answer-counts).

## What the templates read

`.AlertGroup`
:   `Number`, `Title`, `Summary`, `Status`, `Route`, `SeverityLevel`, `Urgent`, `StartedAt`, `URL`, `ReopenCount`,
    `Owner`; absent (nil) for a Storm summary.

`.Alerts`
:   The Alerts, as in Alertmanager: `Status`, `Labels`, `Annotations`, `StartsAt`, `EndsAt`, `GeneratorURL`,
    `Fingerprint`; with `.Alerts.Firing` and `.Alerts.Resolved`.

`.Status`, `.GroupLabels`, `.CommonLabels`, `.CommonAnnotations`, `.ExternalURL`
:   As in Alertmanager templates.

`.Storm`
:   For a Storm summary only: `Route`, `AlertGroupCount`, `UrgentCount`, `Final` (the Storm ended) and `URL` (the
    Route's Alert Groups in Muster).

`.Response`
:   The values the extraction rules found, by name.

`.Event`
:   The lifecycle event a Thread reply carries, such as `alerts_added`; empty otherwise.

`.Notify`
:   `true` when the message is Loud.

`.Mentions`
:   The Mention targets of a Loud message (see below).

`.Secrets`
:   The Destination's Secrets, by name.

`.Final`
:   In the final edit only: "No longer updated here; current state in Muster: {link}".

Alert data reach the templates **as received**, not escaped for any markup, because Muster does not know the chat's
format. Write JSON bodies with `toJson` (or `js` inside a string), so that a label with a quote or a line break cannot
break the body.

Read a Secret as `{{ .Secrets.<name> }}` and an extracted value as `{{ .Response.<name> }}` — or with `$.` in front, or
as `{{ index .Secrets "<name>" }}` with a quoted name. Any other use, such as `{{ with .Secrets }}`, `{{ $s := .Secrets }}`
or `{{ toJson .Response }}`, is refused when you save: Muster checks before each request that every Secret and value a
template reads exists, which it can only do for names written out. Printed or encoded whole, as `{{ toJson . }}` would,
the Secrets show as `[redacted]`.

## Extraction rules and `.Response`

A rule picks the first node its JSONPath selects in the JSON answer of `create` or `open_thread` — a string, a number
as written, or a boolean — and stores it as a string under its name, per Alert Group and Destination. The first rule
of `create` is also the message id Muster shows. `create` reads no values (it runs first), `open_thread` and `update`
read those of `create` (an `update` can come before any thread exists), and `reply_in_thread` reads those of both.

When a rule finds nothing — the answer is not JSON, the path selects nothing, `null`, an object or an array, or a value
longer than 1024 bytes — the `create` still counts as delivered, the Alert Group's Timeline records
`template_value_missing` with the rule's name, and every later request that reads the value fails as a template error.

## Reconciliation

The template mode follows the Desired state like a messenger. The Desired state is the rendered `update` request
(with Secrets and extracted values left out): when a change leaves it as it was, no request is made, and changes made
while a request is pending collapse into the next `update`. Lifecycle events whose form is a Thread reply in the
lifecycle event tables — new Alerts, a Takeover, a Reopen, an ack timeout notice, a Reminder… — go through
`reply_in_thread`, batched like Thread replies in a messenger; without `reply_in_thread` they are not sent.

After the Destination was Broken, the template mode sends only the current state: one `update` per published Alert
Group, no reply for the events of the period, and no `create` for an Alert Group that started and resolved meanwhile.

Deleting the Destination sends the final edit through `update`, with `.Final` set, and wipes its secrets once the
final edits are done; in the mode `both`, the queued events end as Not delivered at once.

## Recipe: a chat with one-step threads

A reply is posted under the message:

```json
"reply_in_thread": {
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "https://chat.example.org/api/channels/ops/messages/{{ .Response.id }}/replies",
  "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }],
  "body": "{\"text\":{{ printf \"%s on #%d\" .Event .AlertGroup.Number | toJson }},\"notify\":{{ .Notify }}}"
}
```

## Recipe: a chat with two-step threads

The chat needs a thread created first; `open_thread` runs once, before the first reply of each message, and adds its
values:

```json
"open_thread": {
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "https://chat.example.org/api/threads",
  "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }],
  "body": "{\"root\":\"{{ .Response.id }}\"}",
  "extract": [{ "name": "thread", "path": "$.thread.id" }]
},
"reply_in_thread": {
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "https://chat.example.org/api/threads/{{ .Response.thread }}/messages",
  "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }],
  "body": "{\"text\":{{ printf \"%s on #%d\" .Event .AlertGroup.Number | toJson }}}"
}
```

If `open_thread` fails, no reply is sent and the reply is retried by the usual rules; once it succeeded it does not
run again for that message, whatever the reply after it came to.

## Recipe: Storm summaries

During a Storm, the Destination gets one Storm summary through `create` — Loud, first — and its later counts and final
state through `update`, instead of the Alert Groups the Storm holds. Their templates see `.Storm` and no Alert Group, so
templates that should handle both branch on it:

```json
"body": "{\"text\":{{ if .Storm }}{{ printf \"Storm on %s: %d new Alert Groups, %d Urgent — %s\" .Storm.Route .Storm.AlertGroupCount .Storm.UrgentCount .Storm.URL | toJson }}{{ else }}{{ printf \"#%d %s (%s)\" .AlertGroup.Number .AlertGroup.Title .AlertGroup.Status | toJson }}{{ end }},\"over\":{{ if .Storm }}{{ .Storm.Final }}{{ else }}false{{ end }}}"
```

A template that reads `.AlertGroup` without the branch fails for a summary as a template error.

## Mentions

Muster does not know the chat's syntax for a Mention, so a Loud message carries its targets as data in `.Mentions`:
each has `Type` (`everyone`, `group` or `user`) and, by type, `Everyone` (`all`, `channel` or `here`), `Name`, `ID` and
`Login`. The trusted function `mention` renders a target as plain text — `@all` (or `@channel`, `@here` as the Mention
settings chose), the group's name, or `@` and the login — for the template to wrap in the chat's syntax:

```
{{ range .Mentions }}<{{ mention . }}> {{ end }}
```

## Template errors

A request whose template fails is not sent: that delivery or Thread reply ends as Not delivered with no fallback body,
since the chat expects its own format. The Destination shows `template_error` with `fallback` `not_sent`,
`muster_template_errors_total{template="webhook_request"}` grows, the log line `webhook_template_failed` names the
request, and the Internal alert `MusterTemplateError` fires with the labels `destination`, `destination_name` and
`template`. The next request of the Destination that renders clears the error and resolves the alert.

Preview a request template before you save it with `POST /api/v1/template-previews` and the kind `webhook_request`: it
renders against a sample, with Secrets shown as `[redacted]` and extracted values as `example-<name>`.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/recipes.md -->
# Recipes

Four ways to use an outgoing webhook, built only from what it has: the [events mode](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/events.md) sends one signed event per
lifecycle event; the [template mode](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/templates.md) sends the requests you write and keeps their answers. Each recipe says
which mode it uses and why.

!!! note "These are sketches"
    The recipes show the shape of a setup, not a tested integration. The endpoints, fields and header names of the other
    system are examples, taken from the public documentation of an open tool. They change between versions and settings,
    so check them against the documentation of the version you run, and use **Preview** and **Send test message** on
    the Destination before you rely on it. In template mode, **Send test message** makes a real `create` request: on a
    status page or in an issue tracker it opens a real incident or issue, so send the first ones to a status page nobody
    reads or to a test repository. Everything about Muster in them is real: the modes, the fields the templates read,
    the extraction rules, the Secrets and the signature.

Common to all four:

- **Use a Route of its own.** Create a Route whose Matchers pick only the Alerts you want to reach this system, for
  example `severity="critical"`, and give it the webhook as its Destination. The other Routes are unaffected. See [Routes
  and Group keys](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/routes-and-group-keys.md).
- **Keep credentials in Secrets**, never in the URL or in a header as text. See [Secrets](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/events.md#secrets).
- **Template mode follows Storms.** While a Storm lasts, a template-mode Destination gets one Storm summary through its
  `create` request, and templates that read `.AlertGroup` fail for it. On a dedicated, narrow Route this rarely matters;
  otherwise branch on `.Storm` as [Recipe: Storm summaries](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/templates.md#recipe-storm-summaries) shows.
- **Look at the Request log** when something does not work: it shows the requests Muster sent and the answers, with
  secrets masked. See [Request log](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/request-log.md).

In the examples, `MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL` is `https://muster.example.org`.

## A phone call or an SMS

**Mode: events.** A provider with an HTTP API starts a call or sends a text when you post a small request to it. You want
that only for the changes that need a human, and you want to send it once. The events mode fits, because every event
carries `notify`, which is true exactly when the change is [Loud](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/concepts/loud-and-quiet.md), and a `webhook-id` that
stays the same across retries.

Template mode does not fit here. It always has an `update` request, which sends again whenever its rendered `update`
changes, and a call provider has nothing to update. It cannot decide to skip an event either.

Muster cannot know your provider's request, so put a small **relay** between them. The relay checks the signature, drops
duplicates, picks the events worth a call, and calls the provider.

1. Create a Destination of type `webhook`, mode `events`, with the relay's URL, as in
   [Create the Destination](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/events.md#create-the-destination). The relay below checks only the signature, so it needs
   the Secret `token` and its header from that example only when something in front of it asks for a credential. Keep
   the Signing secret that the answer shows once, and give it to the relay.
2. Create a Route that matches what should ring a phone, with the Destination, and an On-call profile.
3. Run the relay. This sketch is Python; the `verify` function is the one on [Verify the
   signature](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/events.md#verify-the-signature):

   ```python
   import json, os, urllib.request
   from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

   CALL_ON = {"created", "ack_timeout", "reopened"}   # the events worth a call
   seen = set()                                        # webhook-ids; use a store with an expiry in real life

   class Relay(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
       def do_POST(self):
           body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
           if not verify(os.environ["SIGNING_SECRET"], self.headers["webhook-id"],
                         self.headers["webhook-timestamp"], body, self.headers["webhook-signature"]):
   ```
