- for a request of a check or a test, its kind — **Connection check**, **Check before saving**, **Destination check**,
  **Test message** or **Broken probe** — and its check run, which the requests of one check or test share;
- the Connection or the outgoing webhook Destination it belongs to, and the Destination and the Alert Group it
  concerns, when it concerns one.

## What is not recorded

- A long poll that ended without events: an empty `getUpdates` of Telegram or `pollEvents` of a bridge.
- A request to a callback address whose path names no Connection, or a deleted one.
- The requests of OIDC sign-in and of the outgoing heartbeat.
- The requests of `muster doctor` and `muster bridge check`, which run outside the server.

## Bounds

The bounds are built in; nothing configures them.

`request_log.max_records`
:   The newest 500 records of each Connection, of each outgoing webhook Destination, and of the checks before saving of
    new Connections in an Organization.

`request_log.max_age`
:   7 days on the business clock.

`request_log.body_max`
:   16 KB (16,384 bytes) of each request or answer body.

- A record past either bound is neither listed nor shown, even before it is deleted. The Leader deletes such records
  every minute (the task `request_log_pruning`).
- A longer body is cut at a character boundary and marked with its full size: the record shows "Cut at 16 KB of
  {size} KB". Bodies are stored as text; bytes that are not UTF-8 are replaced.
- A URL is kept up to 16 KB and the names and values of a request's or an answer's headers up to 64 KB in all; what is
  cut ends with "…".
- The body of a request that reached Muster, or of Muster's answer, that is larger than 256 KB, or that was not read to
  the end, is kept as its size only: the record shows "Not kept: {size} KB, too large or not read to the end".
- Writing a record never fails or delays the request it records beyond the write itself, which may take at most 2
  seconds. A record that cannot be written is dropped, logged as `request_log_write_failed` and counted in
  `muster_request_log_write_failures_total`; see [Log events](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/log-events.md) and
  [Metrics](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/metrics.md).

## Masking

Nothing secret is stored. Muster masks a record before it writes it: the requests it sends where they are made, which
knows each request's secrets, and the requests that reach it in one place shared by the three callback addresses.
Every masked value reads `[redacted]`.

- **Secrets a request carries**, wherever they appear — the URL, the headers and both bodies: a bot token, also inside
  a Telegram URL, the proxy password, an outgoing webhook's Secrets and Signing secret, a bridge's push secret, a
  secret in a query.
- **Headers whose values are always masked**, whatever they hold: `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`,
  `Set-Cookie`, `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`, `X-Slack-Signature` and `webhook-signature`, the signature header of
  outgoing webhooks and of pushed Bridge events.
- **The URL** keeps no user information, and the path of a Connection's base URL, which may be a secret — such as the
  path of a bridge behind a reverse proxy — is shown as `[redacted]`, as in errors.
- **Values that authenticate a person**: the signed action ids of buttons, which authenticate a Mattermost or a Slack
  press, and the tokens and codes of Account links — `/start <token>` in a Telegram update, the `token` of an
  `account_link` event, the code in a direct message.
- **What Slack sends and answers with**: the bot token and the app-level token, the Slack signing secret, the address
  that `apps.connections.open` answers with, whose single-use `ticket` opens a socket, the `response_url` of a press,
  and the legacy verification `token` that every Slack payload still carries.

Headers and bodies are untrusted text. The record view shows them as plain text and never renders HTML or Markdown.

## Who may read it

To list the records of a Connection, or of a check run
:   needs: `connections:read`

To list the records of a Destination
:   needs: `destinations:read`

To open a record of a Connection, or of a check before saving
:   needs: `connections:read`

To open a record of an outgoing webhook Destination
:   needs: `destinations:read`

A messenger Destination's requests are its Connection's: its list shows the records of its Connection that concern
it, and opening one of them needs `connections:read`. The built-in Roles — Admin, Responder and Viewer — hold both
Permissions; a Personal access token may hold fewer.

## Where to find it

- **Connections → a Connection → Request log**, for every type, and **Destinations → an outgoing webhook → Request
  log**. A messenger Destination's page has no tab of its own. The list shows, newest first, the time in your time
  zone, the direction arrow, the operation with the kind of check below it, the status — or, without an answer, what
  failed — and the latency; **Load more** shows older records. Filters by direction, status class (`2xx`, `3xx`,
  `4xx`, `5xx` or **No answer**) and operation are kept in the address, such as
  `?tab=request-log&direction=inbound&status_class=4xx`, so a link to a filtered list can be shared.
- **The Alert Group page → Delivery → Requests** on each Destination's row: what was sent to that Destination for this
  Alert Group and what came back.
- **Requests of this check** under the result of the Connection check, of the check before saving and of the
  Destination's check and test: the requests that check or test made.
- **A record** opens with the request — method, URL, headers, body — and the answer — status, headers, body — side by
  side on a wide screen and one under the other on a narrow one; a JSON body is indented. **Copy URL**, **Copy
  headers** and **Copy body** copy each, the body as it is stored rather than indented. A record links to its
  Destination, its Alert Group and the other requests of its check.

The API reads the same records: `listRequestLog` and `getRequestRecord` in the [API reference](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/api.md),
with the check run in the results of the Connection check, the check before saving, the Destination check and the
Destination test.

## Examples

- **Button presses in Mattermost do nothing.** Filter the Connection's Request log by **Received**. No `press` at all
  means that the Mattermost server does not reach Muster: see
  [Let button presses reach Muster](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/mattermost.md#let-button-presses-reach-muster). A `press` that Muster
  answered shows the answer the person got, such as the text that their account is not linked.
- **Button presses in Slack do nothing.** In the HTTP event mode, filter the Connection's Request log by **Received**.
  No `interactive` at all means that Slack does not reach Muster: see [Socket Mode or
  HTTP](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/slack.md#socket-mode-or-http). An `interactive` answered `401` means a wrong Slack signing secret,
  a clock further than `slack.request_tolerance` from Slack's, or a Connection in Socket Mode. In Socket Mode, an
  `interactive` is recorded for each press, and the Connection page says whether another program shares the app.
- **A Root message looks wrong.** On the Alert Group page, open **Requests** of that Destination: the `createPost`,
  `sendMessage` or `postMessage` shows the body Muster sent and what the messenger answered.
- **A bridge refuses a message.** The Connection's Request log shows the `postMessage`, the problem the bridge answered
  with its detail, and the latency.
- **A check before saving fails.** **Requests of this check** shows what the address answered, such as an HTML page
  of a reverse proxy instead of the bridge's info.
- **Pushed events are refused.** A bridge that signs its pushes with an old secret shows each `push` answered `401`.
- **An outgoing webhook fails.** The Destination's Request log, filtered by `5xx`, shows each attempt with the
  endpoint's status and body.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/index.md -->
# Runbooks

One page for every alert Muster can raise: the rules of the Helm chart, evaluated by Prometheus or VictoriaMetrics
from Muster's metrics, and the Internal alerts that Muster raises itself. Each page says what the alert means, its
impact, how to diagnose it and how to fix it.

| Alert | Severity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| [MusterDown](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDown.md) | critical | chart rule |
| [MusterNoLeader](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterNoLeader.md) | critical | chart rule |
| [MusterDeliveryFailing](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDeliveryFailing.md) | critical | chart rule |
| [MusterDestinationBroken](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDestinationBroken.md) | critical | both |
| [MusterHeartbeatLost](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterHeartbeatLost.md) | critical | both |
| [MusterDeliverySlow](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDeliverySlow.md) | warning | chart rule |
| [MusterDeliveryQueueGrowing](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDeliveryQueueGrowing.md) | warning | chart rule |
| [MusterIngestBacklog](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterIngestBacklog.md) | warning | chart rule |
| [MusterIngestRejected](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterIngestRejected.md) | warning | chart rule |
| [MusterTemplateError](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterTemplateError.md) | warning | both |
| [MusterClockSkew](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterClockSkew.md) | warning | chart rule |
| [MusterLoginFailures](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterLoginFailures.md) | warning | chart rule |
| [MusterSnapshotTruncated](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterSnapshotTruncated.md) | warning | Internal alert |
| [MusterOIDCSecretExpiring](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterOIDCSecretExpiring.md) | warning | Internal alert |

## Two sources

- **Chart rules** are evaluated by your monitoring from the metrics Muster serves at `/metrics`, and reach people
  through your Alertmanager like any other rule. Their thresholds, windows and job selector are values of the chart;
  the expressions on these pages are the defaults.
- **Internal alerts** are raised by Muster itself, as Alerts of the built-in Integration "Muster" that every
  Organization has. Ordinary Routes pick them by their labels and deliver them like any other Alert Group; see
  [Internal alerts](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/reference/internal-alerts.md).
- An alert listed as **both** is an Internal alert with a chart rule of the same name for the same condition. The
  chart rule is the backup for when Muster cannot deliver the Internal alert itself.

Send the critical chart rules through an Alertmanager route that bypasses Muster, to a pager or a chat that Muster
does not manage: when Muster is down or cannot deliver, it cannot deliver an alert about that either.

## Runbook links

Every Internal alert carries a `runbook_url` annotation that opens its page here, for the version of Muster that
raised it, and the chart rules link to the same pages:

```text
<MUSTER_RUNBOOK_BASE_URL>/<version>/operations/runbooks/<alertname>/
```

`MUSTER_RUNBOOK_BASE_URL` is `https://muster-io.github.io/muster` by default, the published site; point it at your own
copy of the site where people cannot reach the public one. `<version>` is the `major.minor` of the binary, such as
`1.2`, or `latest` for a development build. For example, `MusterOIDCSecretExpiring` of a development build links to
`https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterOIDCSecretExpiring/`.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDown.md -->
# MusterDown

## Meaning

Prometheus cannot scrape a Muster replica: the target of the job `muster` is down. The chart rule is:

```promql
up{job="muster"} == 0
```

It fires after 2 minutes, with severity `critical` and one alert per scrape target (`instance`). It is a chart rule
only; Muster cannot raise it about itself.

!!! warning "Route it around Muster"
    Send this alert through an Alertmanager route that bypasses Muster, for example straight to a pager or a chat
    that Muster does not manage. While Muster is down it cannot deliver anything, this alert included.

## Impact

- With every replica down, nothing is ingested, no message is sent or edited, and the UI, the API and the buttons in
  the messengers do not answer. Alertmanager retries its failed notifications, and each later notification carries the
  whole Alertmanager group again, so Muster catches up once it is back.
- With one replica of several down, the others keep working: ingestion, delivery and timers run on every replica, and
  another replica takes over the Leader tasks if the stopped one was the Leader.
- After the downtime, the new Leader records it (`downtime_recorded`) and Muster recovers: see
  **Recovery after downtime** on the System status page.

## Diagnosis

1. Find out whether the process runs at all: the pod or the container, its restarts and its exit code.
2. Ask the internal listener (`MUSTER_LISTEN_INTERNAL`, `:8082` by default) directly. `GET /health/live` answers
   `200` while the process serves; `GET /health/ready` answers `503` while the database does not answer or the
   shutdown has begun.
3. Read the last log lines of the replica:
    - `startup_failed`: start-up stopped; its `error` says what to fix — the database cannot be reached, a migration
      failed or a listener cannot listen.
    - `listener_failed`: a listener stopped with an error and the process exits so that it is restarted.
    - `shutdown_requested`: the replica received SIGTERM, for example during a rollout.
4. When the process runs but the scrape fails, check the scrape configuration against `MUSTER_LISTEN_INTERNAL`: the
   port, the path `/metrics` and the network policy between Prometheus and the replica.
5. Run `muster doctor` with the replica's settings. The lines `database`, `session_connection` and `key_canary` name
   a database that cannot be reached, a session connection whose advisory locks or `LISTEN` do not work, and master
   keys that do not decrypt the stored data.

## Fix

- Fix what `startup_failed` or `muster doctor` names: the database URL or its credentials, the master keys, a port
  that another process holds.
- When the database is down, bring it back first; Muster becomes ready as soon as it answers.
- When only the scrape fails, correct the scrape target or the network policy.
- Once Muster is back, open **Recovery after downtime** on the System status page (`/admin/system-status`) and the
  Alert Group list: Alertmanager's next notifications bring the state up to date.
- Set up an outgoing heartbeat (Organization → **Outgoing heartbeat**, `/admin/organization/outgoing-heartbeat`) to an
  external dead man's switch, so that a stopped Muster is noticed even when Prometheus cannot report it.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterNoLeader.md -->
# MusterNoLeader

## Meaning

Every replica of Muster reports that it is not the Leader. The chart rule is:

```promql
max(muster_leader{job="muster"}) == 0
```

It fires after 2 minutes, with severity `critical`. It is a chart rule only. One replica, the **Leader**, holds a lock
in the database and runs the Leader tasks; when it cannot confirm its lock within `leader.fencing_timeout` (15 s) it
stops them, and any replica may take the lock. This alert means that none has for 2 minutes.

!!! warning "Route it around Muster"
    Send this alert through an Alertmanager route that bypasses Muster. Muster still delivers without a Leader, but
    the problem behind the missing Leader — usually the database — may stop delivery next.

## Impact

What stops while no replica leads:

- **Telegram polling**: Connections in the long polling update mode receive no button presses and no messages from
  the discussion group.
- **Bridge polling**: Bridge Connections in the `poll` event delivery mode receive no events — no button presses, Text
  commands, Account link requests or reports of deleted messages — until a replica leads again. A press or a Text
  command that is older than `bridge.event_max_age` (1 hour) by then is dropped unanswered.
- **Slack's Socket Mode**: Slack Connections in the `socket` event mode hold no Socket Mode connection, so a button
  press made meanwhile is lost — the person sees Slack's error — until a replica leads again and connects. Muster does
  not count on Slack to send such presses again.
- The **Heartbeat** check and the **Stale** check: no Integration becomes Heartbeat lost, and no alert is resolved as
  Stale.
- Partition maintenance, retention and the pruning of short-lived state, the outgoing heartbeat, the expiry check of
  the OIDC client secret and the Leader-only metrics (`muster_alert_groups`, `muster_delivery_queue`, `muster_destination_broken`,
  `muster_heartbeat_lost`, `muster_ingest_backlog`, `muster_storm_active`), which go stale or disappear.

What keeps working: ingestion, delivery to every Destination, timers (the end of a Snooze, Ack timeouts and Reminders),
the UI, the API, the webhook update mode of Telegram, the `push` event delivery mode of Bridge Connections and the
`http` event mode of Slack Connections, whose presses any replica receives. After `leader.absence_notice` (2 minutes)
without a Leader, the UI shows the banner "No replica is leading: Telegram and Bridge polling, Slack's Socket Mode,
Heartbeat and Stale checks are paused."

## Diagnosis

1. Open **System status** (`/admin/system-status`). **Replicas** lists every replica that refreshed its record, when
   it last did ("Refreshed …"), and which one is the **Leader**; with no Leader, no replica carries the flag.
2. Check `muster_leader` per replica: `max by (instance) (muster_leader{job="muster"})`. A replica that does not
   appear at all is not scraped; see [MusterDown](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDown.md).
3. Read the logs of the replicas:
    - `leadership_lost` (`replica`, `error`): the Leader could not confirm its lock within `leader.fencing_timeout`,
      or its lock session failed.
    - `leadership_acquired` (`replica`): a replica took the lock. Alternating lost and acquired lines mean that the
      lock keeps breaking.
    - `leader_task_failed` (`task`, `error`): a Leader task failed, usually because the database was unavailable.
4. Run `muster doctor` with the replicas' settings. `session_connection` must say "advisory locks and LISTEN work":
   the Leader lock is an advisory lock on the session connection. Behind a pooler in transaction mode, such as
   PgBouncer, advisory locks do not hold, and `MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_URL` must point at the database directly or
   at a pool in session mode.
5. Check the database itself: its availability, failovers, connection limits and the latency between the replicas
   and the database.

## Fix

- Restore the database or the network path to it. Once the session connection works again, a replica takes the lock
  within seconds and the banner disappears.
- Set `MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_URL` when the main connection goes through a pooler in transaction mode, and restart
  the replicas.
- Raise the database's connection limit if the session connections are refused: each replica holds about three of
  them besides its main pool.
- Once a Leader returns, the paused tasks run again at their next interval: the new Leader polls Telegram and the
  bridges and connects Slack's Socket Mode, and the Heartbeat and Stale checks resume from the signals and Snapshots
  that ingestion recorded meanwhile.
- A Slack Connection that must not lose a press while no replica leads uses the `http` event mode, which every replica
  serves.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDeliveryFailing.md -->
# MusterDeliveryFailing

## Meaning

A Destination has deliveries waiting and has not had a successful delivery for 10 minutes. The chart rule is:

```promql
max by (destination) (muster_delivery_queue{job="muster"}) > 0 unless on (destination) sum by (destination) (increase(muster_delivery_attempts_total{job="muster",outcome="delivered"}[10m])) > 0
```

It fires after 5 minutes, with severity `critical` and the label `destination`, the Destination's id;
`muster_destination_info{destination="…"}` gives its name. It is a chart rule only. It fires before the Destination
becomes Broken as well as after: Muster retries a Transient error with a growing pause (`delivery.transient_backoff`,
from 2 s up to 5 min) and marks the Destination Broken only when the Transient budget runs out
(`delivery.transient_budget`, 10 attempts within 30 minutes) or after a Fatal error.

!!! warning "Route it around Muster"
    Send this alert through an Alertmanager route that bypasses Muster: the Destination it is about may be the one
    that would carry it.

## Impact

- The Root messages of the Destination are not created or edited: people in that chat do not see new Alert Groups,
  and the messages they see may show an old status. Thread replies wait too.
- Other Destinations, ingestion, Commands from the UI and the API, and timers keep working. The Alert Group pages show
  the current state, and the Alert Group list filter **Delivery problem** finds the affected Alert Groups.
- Nothing is lost while deliveries wait: once the Destination answers again, Muster delivers the current state of
  each Root message, not every change it missed.

## Diagnosis

1. Open **System status** (`/admin/system-status`): **Delivery queues** shows how many deliveries wait per
   Destination, and **Broken Destinations** whether the Destination is already Broken.
2. Open the Destination page (`/destinations/<id>`). **Health** says Healthy or Broken; a Broken Destination shows
   "Broken since HH:MM: {reason}. Muster tries again every {interval}."
3. Look at the outcomes of its attempts:
   `sum by (outcome) (increase(muster_delivery_attempts_total{job="muster",destination="<id>"}[15m]))`. `transient`
   and `unknown` point at the network or the messenger; `retry_after` at rate limits; `fatal` and `markup_rejected` at
   the configuration or the message; `template_error` at a template, see [MusterTemplateError](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterTemplateError.md).
4. Read the log lines `delivery_attempt` for the Destination (`destination` is its id): `outcome`, `code` (the HTTP
   status of the answer or the `error_code` of a Telegram answer, 0 when the outcome carries no status), `reason` (the
   masked error the messenger answered or the call failed with), `attempt`, `duration_ms` and `retry_after_ms`.
   `outbound_blocked` means that the outbound address policy refused the address or the proxy (`rule` names why);
   `delivery_work_failed` that the worker itself could not attempt, for example because the database connection was
   lost.
5. Compare with all outbound calls of the delivery client class:
   `sum by (outcome) (rate(muster_client_requests_total{job="muster",client="delivery"}[5m]))`. Failures across
   every Destination point at the network, a proxy or DNS rather than one messenger.
6. Press **Check** on the Destination page, or run `muster doctor`, which prints one line per Mattermost, Slack,
   Telegram and Bridge Destination (`destination <name>`) with the result of its check.

## Fix

- Network, DNS or proxy: fix the path from the replicas to the messenger, the proxy of the Connection, or the
  Organization's **Outbound addresses** (`/admin/organization/outbound`) when `outbound_blocked` names the address.
- Credentials or permissions: replace the bot token on the Connection, or give the bot back the rights the
  Destination check asks for, then press **Check**.
- Telegram is blocked in your network: see
  [Telegram in restricted networks](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/telegram-restricted-networks.md).
- When the Destination has become Broken, follow [MusterDestinationBroken](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDestinationBroken.md).
- The alert resolves once a delivery to the Destination succeeds, or its queue is empty.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDestinationBroken.md -->
# MusterDestinationBroken

## Meaning

A Destination is **Broken**: Muster stopped sending to it after a Fatal error — the messenger refused the bot or the
request for good — or after its Transient budget ran out (`delivery.transient_budget`, 10 attempts within 30
minutes). Muster then probes it every `delivery.broken_probe_interval` (5 minutes) with the oldest waiting delivery,
or with the Destination check when nothing waits, and ends the Broken state on the first success.

This alert has two sources with the same name, severity `critical` and this page:

- The **Internal alert**, raised by Muster itself as an Alert of the built-in "Muster" Integration when the
  Destination becomes Broken, with the labels `destination` (the Destination's id) and `destination_name`. It is
  resolved when a probe, the Destination check or a test message succeeds, and when the Destination is deleted.
- The **chart rule**, the backup for when Muster cannot deliver the Internal alert:

    ```promql
    max by (destination) (muster_destination_broken{job="muster"}) == 1
    ```

    It fires after 5 minutes with the label `destination`. `muster_destination_broken` is set by the Leader.

!!! warning "Route it around Muster"
    Send the chart rule through an Alertmanager route that bypasses Muster. Route the Internal alert to a Destination
    of another kind than the Broken one — a Broken Telegram Destination usually means that Telegram is unreachable
    for every Telegram Destination, so send `MusterDestinationBroken` of Telegram Destinations to Mattermost or an
    outgoing webhook.

## Impact

- Nothing is sent to the Destination: no new Root messages, no edits, no Thread replies. Its deliveries wait, and the
  Alert Groups that wait for it show a delivery problem; the Alert Group list filter **Delivery problem** finds them.
- Other Destinations, ingestion, Commands and timers keep working.
- When the Broken state ends, Muster brings every waiting Root message to its current state; it does not replay the
  changes it missed one by one.

## Diagnosis

1. Open **System status** (`/admin/system-status`): **Broken Destinations** lists every Broken Destination and
   since when. The Destination list (`/destinations`) has the filter **Broken Destinations** too.
2. Open the Destination page (`/destinations/<id>`). The banner says "Broken since HH:MM: {reason}. Muster tries
   again every {interval}." The reason is the error the messenger answered, with secrets masked.
3. Find the log line `destination_broken` (`destination`, `cause`, `reason`): `cause` is `fatal` after a Fatal error
   and `unavailable` after the Transient budget ran out. `outbound_blocked` lines for the same address mean that the
   outbound address policy refused it.
4. Press **Check** on the Destination page to run the Destination check now, or run `muster doctor`, which prints a
   line `destination <name>` with the failing step. For a Connection problem, press **Check connection** on the
   Connection page (`/connections/<id>`).

## Fix

- `cause` `fatal`: fix what the reason names. Typical cases are a revoked bot token (replace it on the Connection),
  a bot that lost its admin rights in a Telegram channel or its discussion group, a bot removed from a Slack channel
  (invite it again with `/invite`) or a Slack channel that was archived, a deleted channel or chat, or an outgoing
  webhook that answers with a permanent error. Then press **Check**: a check that passes ends the Broken
  state at once.
- `cause` `unavailable`: the messenger or the path to it was down long enough to use up the Transient budget. Fix the
  network, the proxy of the Connection or the **Outbound addresses** (`/admin/organization/outbound`); the next probe
  ends the Broken state by itself, or press **Check** to end it now.
- Slack answers `429`: it limits each method per app and workspace. Muster holds the whole Connection for the seconds
  of `Retry-After` and does not count that as a failed attempt, so a `429` with `Retry-After` does not make a
  Destination Broken. A `429` without it counts as a transient failure, and enough of them use up the Transient budget
  (`cause` `unavailable`): lower the limiters or spread the load. See [Rate
  limits](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/slack.md#rate-limits).
- Telegram is unreachable from your network: see
  [Telegram in restricted networks](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/telegram-restricted-networks.md).
- **Send test message** on the Destination page also ends the Broken state when every step succeeds.
- The Internal alert resolves and `destination_recovered` (`destination`, `broken_for_s`) is logged when the Broken
  state ends; the chart rule resolves at the Leader's next update of `muster_destination_broken`.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterHeartbeatLost.md -->
# MusterHeartbeatLost

## Meaning

An Integration is **Heartbeat lost**: its Heartbeat is on, and no signal arrived within its Heartbeat timeout
(`integration.heartbeat_timeout`, 5 minutes by default). Something on the path from Prometheus through Alertmanager
and the network to Muster has stopped; see [Heartbeat](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/heartbeat.md).

This alert has two sources with the same name, severity `critical` and this page:

- The **Internal alert**, raised by the Leader's Heartbeat check, which runs every 10 seconds, as an Alert of the
  built-in "Muster" Integration. Its labels are `integration` (the Integration's id), `integration_name` and the
  Integration's Static labels, so a Route can send it to the team of that cluster. It is resolved by the next signal,
  by turning the Heartbeat off, and by deleting the Integration.
- The **chart rule**, the backup for when Muster itself cannot deliver the Internal alert:

    ```promql
    max by (integration) (muster_heartbeat_lost{job="muster"}) == 1
    ```

    It fires after 1 minute with the label `integration`. `muster_heartbeat_lost` is set by the Leader's Heartbeat
    check.

!!! warning "Route it around Muster"
    Send the chart rule through an Alertmanager route that bypasses Muster, so that it reaches people even when the
    path through Muster is the one that broke.

## Impact

- Alerts from that Alertmanager may not reach Muster: new problems in that cluster may go unnoticed.
- **Stale resolution pauses** for the Integration: the time without a live Heartbeat does not count towards an
  alert's time to go Stale, so nothing is resolved as Stale until the signal returns.
- Other Integrations, delivery and Commands keep working.

## Diagnosis

1. Open the Integration page (`/integrations/<id>`): the banner says "No contact with Alertmanager since HH:MM…",
   the time of the last signal. **System status** (`/admin/system-status`) lists the Integration under
   **Integrations needing attention** as "Heartbeat lost since …".
2. Find the log line `heartbeat_lost` (`integration`, `last_signal_at`). The signal returning logs `heartbeat_live`
   with `first` false.
3. Check Alertmanager: is it running, and does it still have the Heartbeat route and receiver? Its own metrics show
   failed notifications to the Heartbeat receiver.
4. Check Prometheus: the always-firing alert (`MusterHeartbeat`, or `Watchdog` in kube-prometheus-stack) must be
   firing, so the rule evaluation and the connection from Prometheus to Alertmanager work.
5. Check the path to Muster's ingest listener (`MUSTER_INGEST_URL`): DNS, ingress, certificates and network
   policies. Requests that arrive with a wrong or revoked token are refused with `401` and logged as
   `ingest_rejected`; see [MusterIngestRejected](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterIngestRejected.md).
6. When many Integrations are Heartbeat lost at once, the problem is likely on Muster's side: its ingest listener or
   the network in front of it.

## Fix

- Restart or repair Alertmanager or Prometheus, or restore the Heartbeat route and receiver from the snippet
  ([The snippet](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/heartbeat.md#the-snippet)).
- Fix the network path or the ingress to `MUSTER_INGEST_URL`.
- Replace a revoked token in the Heartbeat receiver with a token of the Integration.
- When the cluster was retired on purpose, turn the Heartbeat off or delete the Integration; both resolve the alert.
- The next signal makes the Heartbeat live again and resolves the Internal alert; see
  [When the Heartbeat is lost](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/heartbeat.md#when-the-heartbeat-is-lost).

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDeliverySlow.md -->
# MusterDeliverySlow

## Meaning

Deliveries are slow: the 95th percentile of the time from receiving a Snapshot to the API call that delivers the
resulting change is above 5 seconds, the objective Muster keeps while its rate limiters have room. The chart rule is:

```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(muster_delivery_latency_seconds_bucket{job="muster"}[15m]))) > 5
```

It fires after 15 minutes, with severity `warning`. It is a chart rule only and has no labels of its own: it covers
every Destination together. Changes made by Commands or timers are not measured, only those caused by Snapshots.

## Impact

- New Alert Groups and their changes appear in the messengers later than usual. Nothing is lost.
- The UI and the API show the current state without delay; Commands keep working.

## Diagnosis

1. Find the slow Destinations:
   `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, destination) (rate(muster_delivery_latency_seconds_bucket{job="muster"}[15m])))`.
   `muster_destination_info` gives their names.
2. Look for rate limits: `increase(muster_delivery_attempts_total{job="muster",outcome="retry_after"}[15m])` by
   `destination`. A messenger that answers "retry after" makes Muster wait as long as it asks.
3. Look for a Storm: `muster_storm_active` by `route`, the log line `storm_started` and **Storms** on the System
   status page (`/admin/system-status`). More than `route.storm_threshold` (20) new Alert Groups per minute on a
   Route fill the limiters.
4. Check Muster's own limiters. Telegram: `destination.telegram.limiter` (10 requests per minute per Destination, sends
   and edits together, in the channel and its discussion group) and `connection.telegram.limiter` (15 messages per
   second per Connection). Slack: `destination.slack.limiter` (30 requests per minute per Destination, sends and edits
   together) and `connection.slack.limiter` (50 requests per minute per Connection). A busy Destination waits for its
   limiter, which is expected and not a fault.
5. Check the latency of the calls themselves:
   `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, outcome) (rate(muster_client_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="muster",client="delivery"}[15m])))`.
   Slow calls point at the network, a proxy or the messenger.
6. Check **Delivery queues** on the System status page; when a queue keeps growing, see
   [MusterDeliveryQueueGrowing](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDeliveryQueueGrowing.md).

## Fix

- A Storm or a noisy Route: tune the Route's grouping so that one problem makes one Alert Group, or create an
  Alertmanager silence for the source. The Storm summary already replaces separate messages while the Storm lasts.
- Rate limits of one chat: spread the Routes of that Destination over more Destinations (chats or channels).
- Slow calls: fix the network path or the proxy of the Connection; for Telegram in a restricted network, see
  [Telegram in restricted networks](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/messengers/telegram-restricted-networks.md).
- The alert clears once the 95th percentile over 15 minutes is back under 5 seconds.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDeliveryQueueGrowing.md -->
# MusterDeliveryQueueGrowing

## Meaning

A Destination has more than 100 deliveries waiting, and the number keeps growing. The chart rule is:

```promql
max by (destination) (muster_delivery_queue{job="muster"}) > 100 and max by (destination) (deriv(muster_delivery_queue{job="muster"}[15m])) > 0
```

It fires after 15 minutes, with severity `warning` and the label `destination`, the Destination's id;
`muster_destination_info` gives its name. It is a chart rule only. `muster_delivery_queue` is counted by the Leader
every 15 seconds: the pending deliveries and Thread replies that are due.

## Impact

- The messages of that Destination fall further and further behind: new Alert Groups and their changes appear late.
  Deliveries are still made; nothing is lost.
- Other Destinations, the UI and the API keep working.

## Diagnosis

1. Open **System status** (`/admin/system-status`): **Delivery queues** shows the waiting deliveries per Destination,
   **Storms** the Routes in a Storm and **Broken Destinations** whether the Destination stopped.
2. Look at the outcomes of its attempts:
   `sum by (outcome) (increase(muster_delivery_attempts_total{job="muster",destination="<id>"}[15m]))`. Many
   `retry_after` mean that the messenger limits the rate; `transient` or `unknown` that calls fail; few attempts of any
   kind that Muster's own limiter holds them back.
3. Check whether a Storm feeds the queue: `muster_storm_active` by `route` and the log line `storm_started`.
   `route.storm_threshold` is 20 new Alert Groups per minute.
4. For Telegram, compare the load with the limiters: `destination.telegram.limiter` allows 10 requests per minute per
   Destination, sends and edits together, in the channel and its discussion group. For Slack,
   `destination.slack.limiter` allows 30 requests per minute per Destination, sends and edits together, and
   `connection.slack.limiter` 50 requests per minute per Connection.
5. When no delivery succeeds at all, follow [MusterDeliveryFailing](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDeliveryFailing.md) instead.

## Fix

- Reduce what feeds the Destination: tune the grouping of its Routes, create an Alertmanager silence for a noisy source,
  or move some Routes to another Destination.
- When calls fail, fix the cause as in [MusterDeliveryFailing](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterDeliveryFailing.md).
- A queue that only grows during a Storm shrinks after it: Muster coalesces the changes of a Root message, so it
  delivers the current state rather than every change.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterIngestBacklog.md -->
# MusterIngestBacklog

## Meaning

Processing falls behind ingestion: more than 1,000 Stored Snapshots wait to be processed, or the 95th percentile of
the time from receiving a Snapshot to the end of its processing is above 60 seconds. The chart rule is:

```promql
max(muster_ingest_backlog{job="muster"}) > 1000 or histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(muster_ingest_processing_delay_seconds_bucket{job="muster"}[5m]))) > 60
```

It fires after 5 minutes, with severity `warning`. It is a chart rule only. `muster_ingest_backlog` is counted by the
Leader over every Organization. Ingestion itself keeps answering Alertmanager: Muster stores each Snapshot first and
processes it afterwards, in arrival order per Alertmanager group.

## Impact

- New Alerts reach their Alert Groups late, and so do resolves: Alert Groups appear, change and resolve in the UI and
  in the messengers later than Alertmanager sent them.
- Nothing is lost: the Stored Snapshots wait and are processed in order.

## Diagnosis

1. Find the slow Integrations:
   `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, integration) (rate(muster_ingest_processing_delay_seconds_bucket{job="muster"}[5m])))`.
2. List what waits for one Integration: `GET /api/v1/stored-snapshots?integration=<id>&state=pending`, or the
   Stored Snapshots of the Integration page (`/integrations/<id>`).
3. Read the log lines `snapshot_processing_interrupted` (`integration`, `error`): the processing worker stopped
   because the database failed or the connection was lost, and tries again after a growing pause.
4. Check the database pool of each replica: `muster_db_pool_connections` by `state` against
   `muster_db_pool_max_connections`, and the rate of `muster_db_pool_acquire_wait_seconds_total`. A pool that is always
   fully acquired, with the wait time growing, means that the replicas need more connections.
5. Check whether failures add to the load: `muster_ingest_failed_snapshots_total` by `integration` and the log line
   `snapshot_failed` (`integration`, `stored_snapshot`, `error`). A failed Snapshot is not retried by itself; the
   Snapshots behind it are processed.
6. Check the database itself: CPU, I/O, locks and slow queries.

## Fix

- Restore the database or the connection to it; the worker resumes on its own.
- Give the replicas more connections (`pool_max_conns` of `MUSTER_DATABASE_URL`, by default the larger of 10 and the
  number of CPUs), or run more replicas. Each Integration processes `processing.parallel_groups` (2) Alertmanager
  groups at the same time.
- Reduce the input: an Alertmanager that sends very often or very large groups makes more work. Check its
  `group_interval` and `repeat_interval`.
- After fixing the cause of `snapshot_failed`, process the failed Snapshots again with
  `muster ingest replay --since <duration> [--integration <name>] --actor <name>`, for example
  `muster ingest replay --since 2h --integration prod-eu --actor "Jane Doe"`. Processing is idempotent, so Snapshots
  that were processed change nothing.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterIngestRejected.md -->
# MusterIngestRejected

## Meaning

Muster refused ingestion requests within 15 minutes: an oversized one, or more than 10 without a valid Integration
token, counted per value of the label `integration`. The chart rule is:

```promql
sum by (integration, outcome) (increase(muster_ingest_requests_total{job="muster",outcome="too_large"}[15m])) > 0 or sum by (integration, outcome) (increase(muster_ingest_requests_total{job="muster",outcome="unauthorized"}[15m])) > 10
```

It fires at once (`for: 0m`), with severity `warning` and the labels `integration` — the id of the token's
Integration, or `unknown` when the token matched none — and `outcome`. It is a chart rule only.

- `too_large`: the body was larger than `ingest.body_limit` (16 MB) and was refused with `413`.
- `unauthorized`: the token was missing, wrong or revoked, belonged to a deleted Integration, or was an API token
  instead of an Integration token; refused with `401`.

## Impact

- The refused requests are not stored or processed. When they come from an Alertmanager, its Alerts do not reach
  Muster, and with a Heartbeat on, the Integration soon becomes Heartbeat lost.
- Requests with a valid Integration token and a body within `ingest.body_limit` keep working.

## Diagnosis

1. See which Integration and outcome:
   `sum by (integration, outcome) (increase(muster_ingest_requests_total{job="muster"}[15m]))`.
2. Read the log lines `ingest_rejected` (`integration`, `outcome`, `route_pattern`, `client_address`): the route
   pattern tells ingestion from the Heartbeat, and the client address which host sent it. Muster never logs a token.
3. For `unauthorized`, open the Integration page (`/integrations/<id>`) and compare its tokens and their last use with
   the Alertmanager receivers that send to it. `integration="unknown"` means the token matched no Integration at all:
   a mistyped token, one of a deleted Integration, an API token, or a scanner probing the ingest listener.
4. For `too_large`, find the Alertmanager group that produces such a Snapshot: a group with very many Alerts or very
   long annotations.

## Fix

- A revoked or old token still in use: put a current token into the Alertmanager receiver and reload Alertmanager;
  see [Token rotation](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/alertmanager.md#token-rotation).
- An API token in a receiver: replace it with a token of the Integration; ingestion accepts only Integration tokens.
- Traffic from unknown addresses: restrict who may reach the ingest listener (`MUSTER_INGEST_URL`) with a network
  policy or the ingress.
- `too_large`: split the Alertmanager group with a finer `group_by`, or shorten the annotations that make it large.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterTemplateError.md -->
# MusterTemplateError

## Meaning

A template failed to render. This alert has two sources with the same name, severity `warning` and this page:

- The **Internal alert**, raised by Muster as an Alert of the built-in "Muster" Integration when a template of a Route
  or of a Destination starts failing, and resolved when that template renders again or, for a Route, when a new
  template of that kind is saved; for a Destination, also when the Destination is deleted. Its labels are `route`
  and `route_name` for a template of a Route — the Root message, the Alert line or the Ack timeout notice (`template`
  is `root_message`, `line` or `ack_timeout_notice`) — or `destination` and `destination_name` for a request template
  of an outgoing webhook (`template` is `webhook_request`).
- The **chart rule**, on every failure counted in the last 15 minutes:

    ```promql
    sum by (route, destination, template) (increase(muster_template_errors_total{job="muster"}[15m])) > 0
    ```

    It fires at once (`for: 0m`) with the labels `route`, `destination` (one of them empty) and `template`. The
    counter also counts the URL templates of Link rules (`template="link_rule"`), which raise no Internal alert, so
    the chart rule can fire where the Internal alert does not.

## Impact

- A Route template that fails: the message is rendered with the **Fallback template** instead — every label under
  Muster's heading, with the footer and the buttons. People still see and act on the Alert Group, in a plainer
  format.
- A request template of an outgoing webhook that fails: that request is not sent; the delivery or the Thread reply
  ends as Not delivered, with no fallback body.
- A Link rule that fails: its link is left out of the Alert Group's links.
- Everything else keeps working.

## Diagnosis

1. Open **System status** (`/admin/system-status`): **Template errors** lists every Route and Destination whose
   template fails, with the kind — Root message, Alert line, Ack timeout notice, Link rule or Request template.
2. Open the Route page (`/routes/<id>`): the banner says "Template error since HH:MM: {error}." with the line and
   column that failed. The Route list marks the Route with "Template error".
3. Read the log lines:
    - `fallback_template_used` (`route`, `group`, `template`, `error`): a Route template failed and the message used
      the Fallback template.
    - `webhook_template_failed` (`destination`, `group`, `request`, `error`): a request template of an outgoing
      webhook failed.
    - `link_rule_failed` (`link_rule`, `route`, `group`, `error`): the URL template of a Link rule failed.
4. Check which labels the template reads: a template that works for most Alert Groups often fails on one whose
   Alerts lack a label or carry an unexpected value.

## Fix

- Correct the template so that it handles the missing or unexpected value, and check it with the preview before you
  save it. For outgoing webhooks, see [Template errors](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/outgoing-webhooks/templates.md#template-errors).
- For a Link rule, correct its URL template under Organization → **Link rules** (`/admin/organization/link-rules`).
- The Internal alert resolves when the next message of the Route renders with the template (logged as
  `template_recovered`) or when a new template of that kind is saved on the Route, and when the next request of the
  Destination renders or the Destination is deleted. Deleting a Route does not resolve it. The chart rule resolves
  15 minutes after the last failure.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterClockSkew.md -->
# MusterClockSkew

## Meaning

A replica's clock differs from the database clock by more than 2 seconds. The chart rule is:

```promql
max by (instance) (abs(muster_clock_skew_seconds{job="muster"})) > 2
```

It fires after 5 minutes, with severity `warning` and the label `instance`. It is a chart rule only. Each replica
measures its clock against the database every minute and exports the difference as `muster_clock_skew_seconds`,
positive when the replica is ahead.

## Impact

Every replica takes the time from its own system clock, and the replicas share one database, so a replica that is off
disagrees with the others:

- Timestamps it writes — of Alerts, Alert Groups and Timeline entries — are off by the skew, and the timers and
  windows it evaluates, such as Snooze ends, Ack timeouts and the Reopen window, run early or late.
- TOTP codes may be refused at sign-in.
- ID tokens of the identity provider may be refused as not yet valid or expired, so OIDC sign-in fails.
- Signatures of outgoing webhooks carry a timestamp that receivers may reject.
- Leases of claimed rows and of the Leader lock expire too early or too late, which can make work run twice or wait.

## Diagnosis

1. Find the replica: `muster_clock_skew_seconds` by `instance`.
2. Read its log lines `clock_skew` (`skew_seconds`, `warning_seconds`): logged on every measurement above
   `process.clock_skew_warning` (2 s).
3. Run `muster doctor` on the same host or node. The line `clock_skew` prints the measured skew, and warns with
   "… against the database clock, more than 2s" above the limit.
4. Check time synchronisation on the node of the replica and on the database server: whether NTP (chrony,
   systemd-timesyncd or the cloud provider's time service) runs and is in sync.

## Fix

- Synchronise the clocks of the nodes and of the database server with NTP. The skew is measured again every minute,
  and the alert resolves 5 minutes after it falls under 2 seconds.
- When only one node is off, move the replica to another node until its clock is fixed.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterLoginFailures.md -->
# MusterLoginFailures

## Meaning

A burst of failed sign-ins: more than 20 for one method within 10 minutes. The chart rule is:

```promql
sum by (method) (increase(muster_login_failures_total{job="muster"}[10m])) > 20
```

It fires at once (`for: 0m`), with severity `warning` and the label `method`: `local` for a wrong login or password,
`totp` for a wrong TOTP or recovery code, `oidc` for a refused OIDC sign-in. It is a chart rule only. Attempts that
the sign-in throttle refuses before evaluating them are not counted.

## Impact

- Someone may be guessing passwords or codes. The sign-in throttle (`auth.signin_throttle`) slows them down: after 3
  consecutive failures per account or source address, each attempt waits twice as long as the previous one, up to 60
  seconds.
- Legitimate users of the same account or address wait longer between attempts.
- With `oidc`, people may be unable to sign in at all because the identity provider or its settings fail.

## Diagnosis

1. See the method: `sum by (method) (increase(muster_login_failures_total{job="muster"}[10m]))`.
2. For `local` and `totp`, open the **Audit log** (Organization → **Audit log**, `/admin/audit-log`) and look for the
   actions `session.sign_in_failed` and `session.second_factor_failed`: each names the account, when it is known, and
   the source address.
3. For `oidc`, read the log lines `oidc_sign_in_failed` (`reason`, `error`): the identity provider reported an error,
   could not be reached, or answered with an ID token that did not verify. A clock that is off also makes ID tokens
   fail; see [MusterClockSkew](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterClockSkew.md).
4. Tell an attack from a mistake: many accounts from few addresses look like guessing; one account from its usual
   address looks like a forgotten password or a script with an old one.

## Fix

- Guessing from outside: block the source addresses at the ingress or the firewall, and restrict who may reach the
  UI.
- A forgotten password or a lost authenticator: on the user's page (`/admin/users/<id>`), create a **New password
  setup link** or **Reset TOTP**. Without an Admin who can sign in, use the emergency commands
  `muster admin reset-password --actor <name> <login>` and `muster admin reset-totp --actor <name> <login>`.
- A script or a tool with old credentials: give it a Personal access token or an API token of a Service account
  instead of a password.
- `oidc` failures: fix the identity provider, or the **OIDC settings** (`/admin/oidc`) and their **Check
  connection**; see [Sign-in with Keycloak](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/oidc-keycloak.md). Local sign-in stays available meanwhile.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterSnapshotTruncated.md -->
# MusterSnapshotTruncated

## Meaning

Alertmanager truncates the Snapshots of an Integration: it left Alerts out of a Snapshot because of the `max_alerts`
limit of its webhook receiver, or, for Grafana, the Max alerts limit of its webhook contact point. Muster treats each
Snapshot as the whole Alertmanager group, so a Truncated Snapshot hides Alerts from it.

It is an **Internal alert** only, severity `warning`, raised by Muster as an Alert of the built-in "Muster"
Integration when the first Alertmanager group (`groupKey`) of the Integration arrives truncated. Its labels are
`integration` (the Integration's id) and `integration_name`. It is resolved when no group of the Integration is
truncated any more: each group's next untruncated Snapshot ends its truncation, and so does a group that has sent
nothing for as long as it takes an Alert to go Stale.

## Impact

- The Alerts that Alertmanager left out do not reach their Alert Groups: Muster may show fewer Alerts than fire, miss
  an Alert Group entirely, or keep an Alert open that Alertmanager no longer lists.
- For Grafana, when a whole group resolves, its last Snapshot lists only the first alerts, up to Max alerts, and
  Grafana sends nothing more for the group until one of its alerts fires again. The Alerts it left out stay firing in
  Muster until they go Stale, which needs a live Heartbeat; the Heartbeat through Grafana has not been verified (see
  [Connect Grafana](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/grafana.md#heartbeat)).
- Everything else of the Integration keeps working.

## Diagnosis

1. Open the Integration page (`/integrations/<id>`): the banner says "Alertmanager truncates Snapshots for N groups.
   Set `max_alerts: 0` on the Alertmanager receiver." Its **Alertmanager routes** list shows the **Truncated groups**.
2. **System status** (`/admin/system-status`) lists the Integration under **Integrations needing attention** with
   "Snapshots truncated".
3. `muster_ingest_truncated_snapshots_total` by `integration` counts the truncated Snapshots; the log line
   `internal_alert_raised` (`alertname`, `fingerprint`, `entity`) marks when the alert was raised.
4. Open a recent Stored Snapshot of the Integration (`/integrations/<id>/snapshots/<id>`): a Truncated Snapshot has
   `truncatedAlerts` above 0.
5. In the Alertmanager configuration, find the `webhook_configs` entry of the receiver that sends to Muster and its
   `max_alerts`. For Grafana, open the webhook contact point that sends to Muster and check its Max alerts (`maxAlerts`
   in a provisioning file).

## Fix

- Set `max_alerts: 0` on the Alertmanager receiver that sends to Muster, so that every Alert of the group is sent,
  and reload Alertmanager; see [Connect Alertmanager](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/alertmanager.md).
- For Grafana, set Max alerts to 0, the default, on the webhook contact point that sends to Muster; see
  [Connect Grafana](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/integrations/grafana.md#create-a-webhook-contact-point). Max alerts 0 does not end the Alerts
  that a wholly resolved group of Grafana's left firing: they go Stale while the Heartbeat is live, or end once the
  group fires again and sends untruncated Snapshots. Resolving their Alert Group by hand does not end them either:
  Alerts still firing when its Grace period ends start a new Alert Group.
- The alert resolves once each truncated group has sent an untruncated Snapshot, at its next notification. A group of
  Grafana's that resolved wholly sends none until one of its alerts fires again, so its truncation ends as
  [Meaning](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterSnapshotTruncated.md#meaning) says.

<!-- Source: https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/operations/runbooks/MusterOIDCSecretExpiring.md -->
# MusterOIDCSecretExpiring

## Meaning

The OIDC client secret expires soon: the date entered as **Client secret expires on** in the OIDC settings is within
`oidc.secret_expiry_lead` (14 days).

It is an **Internal alert** only, severity `warning`, with no labels besides `alertname` and `severity`. The Leader
checks the date every 5 minutes and raises it as an Alert of the built-in "Muster" Integration; it is resolved when
the date is changed to a later one or cleared.

## Impact

- Nothing yet. Once the secret expires, the identity provider refuses Muster's back-channel requests, and OIDC
  sign-in fails for everyone.
- Local sign-in keeps working, so an Admin with a local password can still fix the settings.

## Diagnosis

1. Open the **OIDC settings** (`/admin/oidc`): the banner says "The client secret expires on {date}. Issue a new one in
   the identity provider and enter it here."
2. The log line `oidc_secret_expiring` (`expires_on`) is written once per raise.
3. In the identity provider, look up the client's secret and its real expiry date; the date in Muster is only what
   someone entered.

## Fix

1. Issue a new client secret in the identity provider, for Keycloak under the client's **Credentials**; see
   [Sign-in with Keycloak](https://muster-io.github.io/muster/latest/sign-in/oidc-keycloak.md).
2. Enter the new secret in the OIDC settings, set **Client secret expires on** to its new expiry date, or clear it if
   the new secret does not expire, and save. With the API, `PUT /api/v1/oidc-settings` takes the fields
   `client_secret` and `client_secret_expires_on`.
3. Press **Check connection**, then sign in once through OIDC to confirm.

The alert resolves within 5 minutes, at the Leader's next check.

The pages of this section are generated from the code and the specification of this version of Muster.

# Metrics

Muster serves these metrics in the Prometheus text format at `/metrics` on the internal listener and never pushes
them; the endpoint also serves the process (`process_*`) and Go runtime (`go_*`) metrics. Configuration entities
appear only by their `public_id` (`integration`, `route`, `destination`); the labels of an `*_info` metric carry
what it describes, such as a name or the version; every other label takes its values from the closed set listed
below. Histograms are Prometheus histograms with `le` buckets. A Leader-only metric is exported only by the
replica that is the Leader. The capability is the one that exports the metric.

### `muster_alert_group_time_to_ack_seconds`

histogram · labels: `route` · C-10 · exported by every replica

Time from the start of an Alert Group to its first acknowledgement, observed once per Alert Group, by Route.

Buckets (`le`): 60, 300, 600, 1800, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 43200, 86400.

- `route` (entity): the public_id of the route

### `muster_alert_group_time_to_resolve_seconds`

histogram · labels: `route` · C-09 · exported by every replica

Time from the start of an Alert Group to its resolution, observed at each resolution, by Route.

Buckets (`le`): 60, 300, 600, 1800, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 43200, 86400.

- `route` (entity): the public_id of the route

### `muster_alert_groups`

gauge · labels: `route`, `status` · C-09 · exported by the Leader only

Open Alert Groups by Route and status, counted by the Leader; an Alert Group moved to the Default route counts there.

- `route` (entity): the public_id of the route
- `status`: `firing`, `acknowledged`, `snoozed` — the status of the open Alert Groups

### `muster_alert_groups_created_total`

counter · labels: `route` · C-09 · exported by every replica

Alert Groups that started, by Route.

- `route` (entity): the public_id of the route

### `muster_alert_groups_reopened_total`

counter · labels: `route` · C-09 · exported by every replica

Alert Groups that reopened within their Route's Reopen window, by Route.

- `route` (entity): the public_id of the route

### `muster_alert_groups_resolved_total`

counter · labels: `route`, `by` · C-09 · exported by every replica

Alert Groups that were resolved, by Route and by who resolved them.

- `route` (entity): the public_id of the route
- `by`: `user`, `system` — user is a person's resolve, system the resolve when the last Alert resolved

### `muster_alerts_resolved_total`

counter · labels: `integration`, `reason` · C-06 · exported by every replica

Alerts that resolved, by Integration and reason.

- `integration` (entity): the public_id of the integration
- `reason`: `resolved`, `gone`, `stale`, `integration_deleted` — resolved is a resolve from Alertmanager, for the Alert or its whole Alertmanager group; gone an Alert Alertmanager no longer lists; stale one not seen for stale_after with a live Heartbeat; integration_deleted one of a deleted Integration

### `muster_client_request_duration_seconds`

histogram · labels: `client`, `outcome` · C-02 · exported by every replica

Duration of outbound HTTP requests, one per attempt, from the dial to the end of the body, by client class and outcome.

Buckets (`le`): 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 30, 60.

- `client`: `delivery`, `interactive`, `background`, `heartbeat` — the client class of ADR-0015
- `outcome`: `ok`, `retry_after`, `transient`, `fatal`, `unknown`, `blocked`, `redirect` — the classified outcome of the request

### `muster_client_requests_total`

counter · labels: `client`, `outcome` · C-02 · exported by every replica

Outbound HTTP requests, one per attempt, by client class and classified outcome.

- `client`: `delivery`, `interactive`, `background`, `heartbeat` — the client class of ADR-0015
- `outcome`: `ok`, `retry_after`, `transient`, `fatal`, `unknown`, `blocked`, `redirect` — the classified outcome of the request

### `muster_clock_skew_seconds`

gauge · no labels · C-02 · exported by every replica

This replica's clock minus the database clock, corrected by half the round trip; positive when the replica is ahead.

### `muster_commands_total`

counter · labels: `command`, `transport`, `outcome` · C-10 · exported by every replica

Commands run on Alert Groups, one per Alert Group, by command, Transport and outcome.

- `command`: `acknowledge`, `unacknowledge`, `resolve`, `unresolve`, `snooze`, `unsnooze`, `add_note`, `still_on_it` — the Command
- `transport`: `ui`, `api`, `mattermost`, `telegram`, `bridge`, `slack`, `system` — how the Command reached Muster
- `outcome`: `done`, `unchanged`, `refused`, `skipped`, `failed` — done changed the Alert Group, unchanged was an idempotent repeat, refused a refusal or a missing Permission, skipped an Alert Group a bulk Acknowledge left to its Owner, failed an Alert Group that was not found

- `template`: `root_message`, `line`, `ack_timeout_notice`, `link_rule`, `webhook_request` — the kind of template
